title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
我
國家以經學造士論其秀者而
顯庸之學古入官誦詩達政
其法蓋古也故奇傑豪儁鴻
博忠鯁清彊之士繇是以出
而元臣碩輔倚毗康濟彬彬
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

我國家以經學造士，論其秀者而顯庸之。學古入官，誦詩達政，其法蓋古也。故奇傑豪儁、鴻博忠鯁、清彊之士繇是以出，而元臣碩輔倚毗康濟，彬彬
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

Our dynasty cultivates scholars through the study of the Classics, assesses the outstanding among them, and raises them to prominent office. They study antiquity to enter official service and recite the Odes to attain an understanding of government: these methods indeed derive from antiquity. Thus emerge men of extraordinary talent and heroic gifts, vast learning and outspoken loyalty, integrity and strength. Great ministers and eminent counsellors, relied upon to bring peace and order, flourish in cultivated distinction…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皇上履乾體正仁涵義洽道乆而
化成之靡不丕孚况三楚皆
在翼軫之分野
虹流
龍飛休祥濬發謀詒翼燕比之豐
芑起籲帝之思建共臣之業
罔不烝烝然思效其休譽寧
===
能從兩畿後邪乃今歲嘉靖
丙午四月監察御史高節奉
命來玆土按圖攷法去太去甚風
紀肅然無不改嚮諸司以秋
試期告乃聚謀曰是役也節
實監臨之其敢不慎於是稽
典肅幣官預其程守疆除館
punctuated:
皇上履乾體正，仁涵義洽，道乆而化成之，靡不丕孚。况三楚皆在翼軫之分野，虹流龍飛，休祥濬發，謀詒翼燕，比之豐芑。起籲帝之思，建共臣之業，罔不烝烝然思效其休譽，寧能從兩畿後邪？
乃今歲嘉靖丙午四月，監察御史高節奉命來玆土，按圖攷法，去太去甚，風紀肅然，無不改嚮。諸司以秋試期告，乃聚謀曰：「是役也，節實監臨之，其敢不慎？」於是稽典肅幣，官預其程；守疆除館，
translation_en:
His Majesty follows Heaven’s course and embodies rectitude. His benevolence embraces all, and his righteousness permeates everywhere; with the enduring practice of the Way, transformation is accomplished, and none fails profoundly to trust him. Moreover, the whole region of the Three Chu lies within the terrestrial divisions corresponding to the celestial lodges Yi and Zhen. The rainbow flowed and the dragon took flight; auspicious signs issued forth abundantly. Plans bequeathed to posterity bring assistance and repose, comparable to the luxuriant millet of the ode Feng Qi [?]. All are inspired to address the sovereign and establish the achievements of reverent ministers, striving earnestly to live up to this splendid reputation. How could they lag behind the two metropolitan regions?
In the fourth month of this year, the bingwu year of the Jiajing reign [1546], Investigating Censor Gao Jie came to this territory under imperial command. Consulting maps and examining the laws, he eliminated excesses and abuses. Discipline became strict, and everyone changed his conduct. The various offices reported the approaching date of the autumn examination. Those concerned then assembled to deliberate, and Gao said: “For this undertaking, I, Jie, am indeed the Supervising Official. How could I dare to be anything but careful?” Accordingly, precedents were examined and ceremonial gifts duly prepared, while officials took part in arranging the procedures; the precincts were secured and the examination quarters cleared and prepared …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
工綜其役陳軌詰姦吏防其
怠崇雅黜浮士濯其志品式
物采錯綜咸戒而州等胥以
聘至乃以學正何梁教諭楊
成周鼎劉三正林一清阮琳
包澤宋時分試之而屬州與
教諭姜周使總其事曰學也
===
者以徵才也文也者以徵用
也匪是則否巳於事而竣其
百執事自知府以下皆遴選
以充而以提調屬左布政使
菅懷理右參政鄒守愚監試
屬按察使孫應奎僉事卜大
同曰內其毋出乎精白一心
punctuated: 工綜其役，陳軌詰姦，吏防其怠；崇雅黜浮，士濯其志。品式物采，錯綜咸戒。而州等胥以聘至，乃以學正何梁、教諭楊成、周鼎、劉三正、林一清、阮琳、包澤、宋時分試之，而屬州與教諭姜周使總其事，曰：「學也者，以徵才也；文也者，以徵用也。匪是則否巳。」於事而竣，其百執事自知府以下，皆遴選以充，而以提調屬左布政使菅懷理、右參政鄒守愚，監試屬按察使孫應奎、僉事卜大同，曰：「內其毋出乎，精白一心
translation_en:
…the workmen coordinated their tasks. Regulations were set out and wrongdoing investigated, so that the clerks guarded against negligence; refinement was promoted and superficiality rejected, so that the candidates purified their intentions. The prescribed arrangements and material appointments were coordinated, and all were admonished to be vigilant [?]. Zhou and the others all arrived in response to invitations. He Liang, an Instructor, and Yang Cheng, Zhou Ding, Liu Sanzheng, Lin Yiqing, Ruan Lin, Bao Ze, and Song Shi, all Directors of Studies, were assigned to examine the candidates in separate groups. Zhou and the Director of Studies Jiang Zhou were entrusted with overall responsibility. They were told: “Learning is the means of discerning talent; writing is the means of discerning fitness for service. Those who do not meet these criteria are to be rejected.”
To carry the undertaking through [?], all the functionaries, from prefects downward, were carefully selected for their assignments. Responsibility as Proctors was entrusted to the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, Jian Huaili, and the Right Administration Vice Commissioner, Zou Shouyu; supervision of the examination was entrusted to the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, Sun Yingkui, and the Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, Bu Datong. They were told: “Those within must not go out [?]; with purity and singleness of heart…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以稱
德意已於事而竣稽其均守辨其
旗物罔不祗愼而相與防範
之以屬右布政使劉寅左叅
政丁汝夔右叅政許琯右叅
議戴邦正張緒鄭有周張拱
文副使楊應奇陳仕賢潘九
===
齡公躋奎僉事米榮侯寧王
喬齡鄭汝舟都指揮劉遠鐵
冠李杲曰外其毋入乎堊厥
蠹萌明神其森已於事而竣
是時都御史巡撫姜儀振文
耀威邇遠服懷士志大興以
彌力於學撫治鄖陽先任維
punctuated:
以稱德意，已於事而竣。稽其均守，辨其旗物，罔不祗愼，而相與防範之，以屬右布政使劉寅、左叅政丁汝夔、右叅政許琯、右叅議戴邦正、張緒、鄭有周、張拱文，副使楊應奇、陳仕賢、潘九齡、公躋奎，僉事米榮、侯寧、王喬齡、鄭汝舟，都指揮劉遠、鐵冠、李杲。曰：「外其毋入乎！堊厥蠹萌，明神其森！」已於事而竣。
是時，都御史巡撫姜儀振文耀威，邇遠服懷，士志大興，以彌力於學。撫治鄖陽，先任維
translation_en:
…so as to accord with the emperor’s gracious intentions, and thus bring the work to completion [?]. Their respective guard duties were checked and their flags and insignia distinguished; all exercised reverent care and cooperated in maintaining safeguards. These responsibilities were entrusted to Liu Yin, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Ding Rukui, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Xu Guan, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Dai Bangzheng, Zhang Xu, Zheng Youzhou, and Zhang Gongwen, Right Administration Assistant Commissioners; Yang Yingqi, Chen Shixian, Pan Jiuling, and Gong Jikui, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Mi Rong, Hou Ning, Wang Qiaoling, and Zheng Ruzhou, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Liu Yuan, Tie Guan, and Li Gao, Regional Military Commissioners. They were instructed: “Let nothing from outside enter! Suppress the beginnings of corruption [?]; the watchful spirits stand solemnly arrayed!” Thus the work was brought to completion [?].
At this time, Jiang Yi, Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator, promoted literary learning and displayed his authority. Those near and far submitted and were won over; the scholars’ aspirations rose greatly, and they devoted still greater effort to their studies. The governor of Yunyang was formerly Ren Wei…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賢今葉照提督南贛先虞守
愚今顧遂寧宇不聳樹聲克
崇總兵豐城侯李熈爼豆臨
戎室家無恐故視昔加隆焉
比鎖院合提學副使今陞右
參政王嘉賓及副使楊勉學
所校士二千六百有奇三試
===
之御史節猶慮其不瀝衷殫
力也乃又合而誓之曰所不
與祓除其心以報
國者有如此哉於是諸執事大
用竦惕不懈彌虔拔其尤異
者九十人拜錄其文以
獻
punctuated: 賢，今葉照；提督南贛，先虞守愚，今顧遂，寧宇不聳，樹聲克崇。總兵豐城侯李熈，爼豆臨戎，室家無恐，故視昔加隆焉。比鎖院，合提學副使今陞右參政王嘉賓及副使楊勉學所校士二千六百有奇，三試之。御史節猶慮其不瀝衷殫力也，乃又合而誓之曰：「所不與祓除其心以報國者，有如此哉！」於是諸執事大用竦惕，不懈彌虔，拔其尤異者九十人，拜錄其文以獻。
translation_en:
…xian, formerly, and now Ye Zhao; and, as supreme commander of Nan-Gan, formerly Yu Shouyu and now Gu Sui: they kept the region peaceful and undisturbed and established a lofty reputation. The regional commander Li Xi, Marquis of Fengcheng, brought ritual cultivation to military command, so that households had nothing to fear. Thus conditions flourished even more than in the past.

When the examination compound was sealed, the candidates assessed by Wang Jiabin, vice commissioner for education, now promoted to administration vice commissioner of the Right, and Vice Commissioner Yang Mianxue were assembled. They numbered more than 2,600 and were examined in three sessions. Censor Jie [?] still feared that those conducting the examination might not devote their whole hearts and utmost efforts to it. He therefore assembled them again and bound them with an oath, saying: “Should anyone fail to join us in purifying his heart to repay the state, let this be his fate!” Thereupon all the functionaries became deeply apprehensive and vigilant, increasingly earnest and unremitting. They selected ninety exceptionally outstanding candidates and respectfully transcribed their essays for presentation to the throne…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
制也御史乃言曰於乎慎爾多士
夫篤培者天靈傑者地化成
者人夫明明赫赫厥類惟彰
自烈山氏之興也遐乎邈矣
天生
聖人起於南離我
皇上受圖錫紀遠邁前古而士類
===
之興雲蒸風從蓋其氣然也
詩曰天監有周昭假于下保
玆天子生仲山甫言乎天也
夫高而衡嶽環列者以萬數
淵而江漢迴繞者以千數洩
令德之珍鳩靈貢祉以效於
上猶恐其後也士望國紀厥惟在
punctuated:
制也。御史乃言曰：「於乎！慎爾多士！夫篤培者天，靈傑者地，化成者人。夫明明赫赫，厥類惟彰。自烈山氏之興也，遐乎邈矣！天生聖人，起於南離。我皇上受圖錫紀，遠邁前古，而士類之興，雲蒸風從，蓋其氣然也。
詩曰：『天監有周，昭假于下，保玆天子，生仲山甫。』言乎天也。夫高而衡嶽環列者以萬數，淵而江漢迴繞者以千數，洩令德之珍，鳩靈貢祉，以效於上，猶恐其後也。士望國紀，厥惟在
translation_en:
…as prescribed. The Censor then declared: “Ah! Be vigilant, you many scholars! Heaven provides abundant nurture; earth supplies spiritual potency and outstanding talent; human effort transforms and brings to completion. Bright and resplendent, those of this kind become manifest. How distant is the time when Lieshan Shi arose! Heaven brought forth a sage, who rose in the south, the direction of the trigram Li. Our Emperor received the chart of sovereignty and was granted the succession of ages, far surpassing antiquity. Scholars have risen like gathering clouds and followed like the wind: surely this is the working of that vital force.
The Book of Odes says: ‘Heaven looked upon Zhou; its light reached down below. To protect this Son of Heaven, it brought forth Zhongshan Fu.’ This speaks of Heaven. The heights arrayed around Mount Heng number in the tens of thousands; the deep waters encircled by the Yangzi and Han rivers number in the thousands. They release their treasures of excellent virtue, gather spiritual potency, and offer blessings in service to the sovereign, fearing only to fall behind. The eminent scholars and the mainstays of the state are to be found in…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
茲詩曰思皇多士生此王國
王國克生維周之楨言乎地
也夫士以明義所以思奮庸
而熙帝載乃今爾多士濟濟
蹌蹌炳蔚相章抒經藝之指
而敷宏博之詞蓋將賛慮於
智廣業於仁要其卓卓可効
===
用者何以加焉可謂吉士也
已詩曰藹藹王多吉士維天
子使媚于天子又曰藹藹王
多吉人維天子命媚于庶人
言乎人也於乎慎爾多士州
不佞從而申言曰州聞之古
者以榮為懼也是故能以懼
punctuated:
茲。《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。」言乎地也。夫士以明義，所以思奮庸而熙帝載。乃今爾多士，濟濟蹌蹌，炳蔚相章，抒經藝之指，而敷宏博之詞，蓋將賛慮於智，廣業於仁。要其卓卓可効用者，何以加焉？可謂吉士也已。《詩》曰：「藹藹王多吉士，維天子使，媚于天子。」又曰：「藹藹王多吉人，維天子命，媚于庶人。」言乎人也。
於乎！慎爾多士！州不佞，從而申言曰：「州聞之，古者以榮為懼也，是故能以懼
translation_en:
…here. The Book of Odes says: “How splendid the many scholars, born in this royal kingdom! The royal kingdom indeed brings them forth, the pillars of Zhou.” This speaks of the earth. Scholars clarify righteousness so that they may aspire to exert themselves in service and bring lustre to the emperor’s undertakings. Now you many scholars, dignified and stately, display your brilliance, each enhancing the others; you express the purport of the classics and unfold words of breadth and learning. Surely you will assist deliberations through wisdom and enlarge accomplishments through benevolence. Considering your outstanding capacity for useful service, what could surpass it? You may indeed be called worthy scholars. The Book of Odes says: “In flourishing abundance, the king has many worthy scholars; the Son of Heaven employs them, and they are pleasing to the Son of Heaven.” It also says: “In flourishing abundance, the king has many worthy men; the Son of Heaven commissions them, and they are pleasing to the common people.” This speaks of humanity.
Ah! Be vigilant, you many scholars! I, Zhou, unworthy though I am, would further declare: “I have heard that the ancients regarded honour with apprehension. Thus they were able, through apprehension, to…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
為榮爾多士敬哉無忘爾御
史之言州寔與有光耀也矧
曰其爾多士言以徵志文以
足言州睹其志矣如其貳焉
非州之所願於多士者也詩
曰庶幾夙夜以永終譽爾多
士愼諸是役也左參議戴嘉
===
猷副使魏尚純以入賀
萬壽行守備太監廖□員外郎孫
續主事王景象劉慤行人姚
一元賀承光以有事茲土至
右參政楊本仁按察使林雲
同副使孫世祐以遷代去皆
嘗與於先事而樂觀其成者
punctuated:
為榮。爾多士敬哉！無忘爾御史之言，州寔與有光耀也，矧曰其爾多士！言以徵志，文以足言。州睹其志矣，如其貳焉，非州之所願於多士者也。《詩》曰：「庶幾夙夜，以永終譽。」爾多士愼諸！
是役也，左參議戴嘉猷、副使魏尚純以入賀萬壽行；守備太監廖□、員外郎孫續、主事王景象、劉慤、行人姚一元、賀承光以有事茲土至；右參政楊本仁、按察使林雲同、副使孫世祐以遷代去，皆嘗與於先事而樂觀其成者
translation_en:
…turn apprehension into honor. You, gentlemen, must be reverent! Do not forget the words of your Censor. I, Zhou, truly share in this glory; how much more do you, gentlemen! [?] Words attest one's intentions, and writing gives full expression to words. I, Zhou, have seen your intentions. Should you depart from them, that would not be what I wish for you, gentlemen. The Book of Odes says: “May you strive morning and night, to preserve your good name to the end.” You, gentlemen, must take heed!
During this undertaking, Dai Jiayou, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, and Wei Shangchun, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, departed to attend court and offer congratulations on the imperial birthday. Liao □, the eunuch serving as Garrison Commander; Sun Xu, Vice Director; Wang Jingxiang and Liu Que, Secretaries; and Yao Yiyuan and He Chengguang, Messengers, arrived on official business in this region. Yang Benren, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Lin Yuntong, Surveillance Commissioner; and Sun Shiyou, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, departed upon transfer or replacement. All had taken part in the preliminary arrangements and were pleased to see the undertaking brought to completion…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
法得書
江西南昌府儒學教授陸州
謹序
punctuated:
法得書。

江西南昌府儒學教授陸州謹序。
translation_en:
…may, according to established convention, be recorded.

Preface respectfully composed by Lu Zhou, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史高節〔文豐順天府永清縣籍太興左衛人戊戌進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使管懷理〔一初山東臨邑縣人己丑進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右參政鄒守愚〔君哲福建莆田縣人丙戌進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使孫應奎〔文宿河南河南衛籍直隸長洲縣人辛巳進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事卜大同〔吉夫浙江秀水縣人戊戌進士〕
===
考試官
江西南昌府儒學教授陸州〔汝行浙江海寧縣人甲辰進士〕
浙江處州府麗水縣儒學教諭婁周〔廷佐直隸太倉州人丁酉貢士〕
同考試官
河南汝州儒學學正何梁〔少奕廣東香山縣人甲午貢士〕
山東兖州府寧陽縣儒學教諭楊成〔位中福建閩縣人丁酉貢士〕
河南河南府嵩縣儒學教諭周鼎〔鳴功四川內江縣人丁酉貢士〕
直隸常州府武進縣儒學教諭劉三正〔世準四川內江縣人庚子貢士〕
直隸徽州府績溪縣儒學教諭林一清〔子時福建福清縣人辛卯貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按湖廣監察御史高節〔文豐，順天府永清縣籍，太興左衛人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官：
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使管懷理〔一初，山東臨邑縣人，己丑進士〕。
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右參政鄒守愚〔君哲，福建莆田縣人，丙戌進士〕。

監試官：
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使孫應奎〔文宿，河南河南衛籍，直隸長洲縣人，辛巳進士〕。
湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事卜大同〔吉夫，浙江秀水縣人，戊戌進士〕。

考試官：

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
立則見其參於前也在輿則見其倚於衡
也夫然後行
唯天下至誠為能盡其性能盡其性則能
盡人之性能盡人之性則能盡物之性
能盡物之性則可以贊天地之化育可
以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
人人親其親長其長而天下平
===
易
美在其中而暢於四支發於事業美之至
也
觀其所恆而天地萬物之情可見矣
易其至矣乎夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業
也知崇禮卑崇效天卑法地天地設位
而易行乎其中矣成性存存道義之門
艮止也兌說也
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

立則見其參於前也，在輿則見其倚於衡也，夫然後行。

唯天下至誠，為能盡其性；能盡其性，則能盡人之性；能盡人之性，則能盡物之性；能盡物之性，則可以贊天地之化育；可以贊天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。

人人親其親，長其長，而天下平。

易

美在其中，而暢於四支，發於事業，美之至也。

觀其所恆，而天地萬物之情可見矣。

易，其至矣乎！夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。

艮，止也；兌，說也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When standing, see these principles present before you; when riding in a carriage, see them resting against its crossbar. Only then will your conduct be effective.

Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize his own nature. Able fully to realize his own nature, he can fully realize the nature of others. Able fully to realize the nature of others, he can fully realize the nature of things. Able fully to realize the nature of things, he can assist in the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth. Able to assist in the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, he can form a triad with Heaven and Earth.

If everyone treats his own parents with affection and his own elders with respect, all under Heaven will be at peace.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Beauty resides within, flows freely through the four limbs, and manifests itself in undertakings: this is beauty at its utmost.

By observing what endures, one can discern the true circumstances of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things.

How consummate are the Changes! The Changes are the means by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their undertakings. Wisdom is lofty; ritual propriety is humble. The lofty emulates Heaven; the humble takes Earth as its model. Heaven and Earth assume their positions, and change operates between them. Preserving continually the nature one has perfected is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.

Gen signifies stopping; Dui signifies joy.

Book of Documents (Shu)

text:
私藏應禁軍器
失時不修隄防
第叁場
策五道
問前代臣子於其祖宗之功德每敷揚而
不已非特以歌詠鴻休蓋將垂無窮之
憲也詩書所載如益之賛堯皐陶之美
舜五子之述禹雅頌之所以稱湯與文
武者盛矣嗣是而後若漢祖唐宗宋之
===
藝祖其臣子之所稱頌者固亦郁乎可
觀然不能無侈辭焉今可悉舉而言之
歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺
天眷命肇造區夏
聖德神功超百王而獨盛其在當日如儒臣宋
濂所敘之六者為得其精要而其餘見
於諸臣之所對揚父老之所傳誦洋洋
乎真足以被韶濩而鳴無窮也
punctuated:
私藏應禁軍器。

失時不修隄防。

第叁場
策五道

問：前代臣子於其祖宗之功德，每敷揚而不已，非特以歌詠鴻休，蓋將垂無窮之憲也。《詩》《書》所載，如益之賛堯、皐陶之美舜、五子之述禹、雅頌之所以稱湯與文武者，盛矣。嗣是而後，若漢祖、唐宗、宋之藝祖，其臣子之所稱頌者，固亦郁乎可觀，然不能無侈辭焉。今可悉舉而言之歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝膺天眷命，肇造區夏，聖德神功，超百王而獨盛。其在當日，如儒臣宋濂所敘之六者，為得其精要，而其餘見於諸臣之所對揚、父老之所傳誦，洋洋乎真足以被韶濩而鳴無窮也。
translation_en:
Privately possessing prohibited military weapons.

Failing to repair dikes and embankments at the proper time.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Subjects of former dynasties continually expounded and celebrated the achievements and virtues of their dynasties’ ancestral sovereigns. They did so not merely to sing of their magnificent beneficence, but to transmit models for all time. The examples recorded in the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents are abundant: Yi’s praise of Yao, Gao Yao’s celebration of Shun, the five sons’ account of Yu, and the praise of Tang, Wen, and Wu in the Court Hymns and Eulogies. Thereafter, the praises that subjects offered to Gaozu of Han, Taizong of Tang, and the illustrious progenitor of Song were likewise rich and impressive, yet could not be free of exaggeration. Can you now enumerate and discuss them all?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s gracious mandate and founded his realm in the Chinese lands. His sagely virtue and divine achievements surpassed those of all earlier kings in their unrivaled splendor. Among accounts from his own day, the six matters set forth by the scholarly official Song Lian captured their essential significance. The rest appear in the reverent celebrations of his ministers and in the accounts transmitted and recited by local elders. So abundant are these that they truly deserve to be set to the music of the Shao and Huo and resound for all eternity.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其於潔淨精微温柔敦厚之敎亦似若
有戾者果何與夫秦漢而下續易續詩
擬易補亡何其紛紛也攷其旨歸不知
亦可以與於斯乎否邪夫易貴神解詩
貴性情未易言也然大儒易有易傳詩
有詩傳而太極圖通書而離騷又皆各
爲之註其於微詞奧義果可以得其要
領而無遺恨否乎諸士子楚產也又皆
究心於此者幸以其所得者以告我
===
問士君子之持身處事以風節爲難而尤
必以和平爲極審是二者兼濟而時有
權衡焉可也古之人若延陵著讓而才
近伯夷抗言存趙而終身不見寬大之
主高其義矣尚自爲之逃故人物色致
其誠矣意不爲之屈得無嫌於隘歟直
節寢謀不無褊心忿疾之疎雅志澄清
或啟東京清議之釁經略中原者急於
成功而發憤績偉澶淵者安於峭直而
punctuated:
其於潔淨精微、温柔敦厚之敎，亦似若有戾者，果何與？夫秦漢而下，續易、續詩、擬易、補亡，何其紛紛也！攷其旨歸，不知亦可以與於斯乎，否邪？夫易貴神解，詩貴性情，未易言也。然大儒，易有《易傳》，詩有《詩傳》，而《太極圖》《通書》，而《離騷》，又皆各爲之註。其於微詞奧義，果可以得其要領而無遺恨否乎？諸士子楚產也，又皆究心於此者，幸以其所得者以告我。

問：士君子之持身處事，以風節爲難，而尤必以和平爲極。審是二者兼濟，而時有權衡焉，可也。古之人，若延陵著讓而才近伯夷，抗言存趙而終身不見，寬大之主高其義矣，尚自爲之逃；故人物色致其誠矣，意不爲之屈，得無嫌於隘歟？直節寢謀，不無褊心忿疾之疎；雅志澄清，或啟東京清議之釁。經略中原者急於成功而發憤，績偉澶淵者安於峭直而
translation_en:
…why, indeed, do these also seem to run counter to the teachings of purity and subtle refinement, and of gentleness and generous sincerity? From the Qin and Han onward, how numerous have been the continuations of the Changes and the Odes, the imitations of the Changes, and the attempts to supply lost texts! Examining their underlying purport, one wonders whether they too may participate in these teachings. The Changes prizes inspired understanding; the Odes prizes authentic feelings and disposition. These are not easy matters to discuss. Yet the great Confucian scholar produced a Commentary on the Changes and a Commentary on the Odes, and also annotated the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, the Comprehensive Writings, and Encountering Sorrow. Can their subtle language and profound meanings truly be grasped in their essentials, leaving nothing to regret? You examination candidates are natives of Chu and have all devoted yourselves to these matters. I hope you will tell me what you have learned.

Question: For a gentleman, maintaining integrity in personal conduct and the handling of affairs is difficult; yet above all he must take equanimity and harmony as his highest standard. It is fitting to ensure that these two qualities complement one another, weighing their relative claims as circumstances require. Among the men of antiquity, Yanling was renowned for yielding his claim, yet his talents approached those of Bo Yi [?]; another spoke out boldly to preserve Zhao, yet refused an audience for the rest of his life. A magnanimous ruler esteemed a man's righteousness, yet the man still fled from him; an old friend sought another out by his appearance and conveyed his sincerity, yet that man's resolve would not bend. Might such conduct be open to the charge of narrowness? Unbending integrity that thwarted a scheme was not entirely free of the failings of a constricted mind and angry resentment; a lofty ambition to purify public life may have occasioned the strife surrounding the morally critical public opinion of the Eastern Han. The man who planned the recovery of the Central Plain was impatient for success and gave vent to his indignation; the man whose achievements at Chanyuan were great remained content in his severe uprightness and…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
蒙譏得無嫌於激歟乃若志在爲韓心
不仕宋南陽嘯歌以俟時洛城從容而
論德其立節固未嘗不高也周旋京師
危言激論者實一時名賢之首充使條
例謂青苗且可放過者曾無損大賢盛
德之光或則又處平原一相而獨全正
類於嚴迫之時爲轉運使副而善沮新
法於盛行之日人亦不得而尤焉然上
不至於矯異而下不蹈夫詭隨者何哉
===
===
豈其所以致嚴者出於不得已而非有
意歟抑持心之平而適用之周歟或時
有難易事有可否而不容執一論也夫
危行峻詞易以招尤而和厚溫醇類多
失已君子蓋兩病之處二者之間而不
失其必有道乎願明言之
問學莫先于尚友尚友必自鄉始楚稱大
藩宦于斯者有遺澤焉產于斯者有遺
範焉固不能以悉數也姑舉其著者言
punctuated:
蒙譏，得無嫌於激歟？乃若志在爲韓，心不仕宋，南陽嘯歌以俟時，洛城從容而論德，其立節固未嘗不高也。周旋京師，危言激論者，實一時名賢之首；充使條例，謂青苗且可放過者，曾無損大賢盛德之光。或則又處平原一相，而獨全正類於嚴迫之時；爲轉運使副，而善沮新法於盛行之日，人亦不得而尤焉。然上不至於矯異，而下不蹈夫詭隨者，何哉？豈其所以致嚴者，出於不得已而非有意歟？抑持心之平而適用之周歟？或時有難易，事有可否，而不容執一論也。夫危行峻詞，易以招尤，而和厚溫醇，類多失已，君子蓋兩病之。處二者之間而不失，其必有道乎？願明言之。
問：學莫先于尚友，尚友必自鄉始。楚稱大藩，宦于斯者有遺澤焉，產于斯者有遺範焉，固不能以悉數也。姑舉其著者言
translation_en:
…incurred criticism: might this not verge on excessive vehemence? As for those whose resolve was to serve Han, whose hearts rejected service under Song, who sang aloud in Nanyang while awaiting their time, or who discoursed calmly on virtue in Luocheng, their maintenance of moral principle was certainly lofty. The man who moved about the capital, speaking uncompromisingly and arguing vehemently, was foremost among the eminent worthies of his day. The man who served in the office for financial regulations [?] and said that the Green Sprouts measure might for the time being be allowed to pass did not thereby diminish the radiance of his great virtue. Another, serving as minister at Pingyuan [?], alone preserved upright men in a time of harsh repression; another, serving as transport commissioner or vice commissioner, skillfully checked the New Policies when they were being widely implemented. Neither could be faulted. How did they avoid, at one extreme, affected singularity and, at the other, unprincipled compliance? Was their severity born of necessity rather than deliberate intent? Or was it because they maintained an even temper of mind and adapted comprehensively to circumstances? Perhaps times differ in difficulty, and actions in their acceptability, so that no single judgment can apply to all. Upright conduct and stern words readily attract blame, while a gentle, generous, warm, and mild manner often leads one to compromise oneself. The gentleman surely regards both as faults. Must there not be a way to stand between these two without going astray? Please explain it clearly.
Question: In learning, nothing takes precedence over seeking the fellowship of worthy men, and that fellowship must begin with one’s own region. Chu is known as a great province. Those who held office here left a legacy of beneficence; those born here left examples for posterity. They certainly cannot all be enumerated. Let us therefore select the most distinguished and discuss…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之令儀令色而爲周名臣無喜無怒而
爲楚賢相首居公位而舉奏貪汙官至
宰相而不營産業其德量忠儉可得而
言歟功著烏林威行南服綏懷遠近恩
孚江漢之衆措置屯田不忘恢復之圖
其得失成敗可得而言歟教興庠序禮
定婚姻復州惠愛江陵滅火其循良在
人至今膾炙也然而有可施於今者何
歟令夷陵者終成相業謫道州者克退
===
虜兵衡岳開雲長沙賦鵩其氣節在人
至今興起也然而有幸有不幸者何歟
勳烈盛于周宣中興之日道學開于有
宋全盛之時講學岳麓讀書石鼓要其
體用果孰爲得失邪制誥典贍經史博
通以文章魁三試之選以兄弟獲聯榜
之榮攷其學業果孰爲高下邪或負社
稷之器或稱氷鑑之明然則古人之自
任與夫古人之知人要非浪言也不知
punctuated: 之。令儀令色而爲周名臣，無喜無怒而爲楚賢相；首居公位而舉奏貪汙，官至宰相而不營産業，其德量忠儉可得而言歟？功著烏林，威行南服；綏懷遠近，恩孚江漢之衆；措置屯田，不忘恢復之圖，其得失成敗可得而言歟？教興庠序，禮定婚姻，復州惠愛，江陵滅火，其循良在人，至今膾炙也。然而有可施於今者何歟？令夷陵者終成相業，謫道州者克退虜兵，衡岳開雲，長沙賦鵩，其氣節在人，至今興起也。然而有幸有不幸者何歟？勳烈盛于周宣中興之日，道學開于有宋全盛之時，講學岳麓，讀書石鼓，要其體用，果孰爲得失邪？制誥典贍，經史博通，以文章魁三試之選，以兄弟獲聯榜之榮，攷其學業，果孰爲高下邪？或負社稷之器，或稱氷鑑之明，然則古人之自任與夫古人之知人，要非浪言也。不知
translation_en:
…them. One became a renowned minister of Zhou through his fine deportment and dignified countenance; another became a worthy chief minister of Chu, showing neither joy nor anger. One, upon first occupying the position of a duke, impeached corrupt officials; another rose to chief minister without building up private estates. Can you discuss their virtue, magnanimity, loyalty, and frugality? One distinguished himself at Wulin and extended his authority throughout the southern territories; another pacified and won over those far and near, his benevolence securing the trust of the people of the Jiang and Han rivers; another organized agricultural colonies, never forgetting his plans for recovery of the lost territories. Can you discuss their merits and shortcomings, successes and failures? They fostered education in local schools, regulated marriage through ritual, bestowed benevolent care upon Fuzhou, and extinguished fires in Jiangling. Their benevolent administration remains on people’s lips even today. Yet which of their practices could be applied today? The man who served as magistrate of Yiling ultimately achieved distinction as chief minister; the man banished to Daozhou succeeded in repelling enemy troops. Clouds parted at Mount Heng; the Rhapsody on the Owl was composed at Changsha. Their moral courage and integrity still inspire people today. Yet why were some fortunate and others unfortunate?

Outstanding achievements flourished during the restoration under King Xuan of Zhou, and the Learning of the Way began to flourish when the Song dynasty was at its height. They lectured at Yuelu and studied at Shigu. Considering the underlying substance and practical application of their learning, who truly succeeded and who fell short? Some composed imperial proclamations of classical elegance and richness; some possessed comprehensive knowledge of the Classics and histories. One took first place in all three examinations through his literary accomplishments; brothers gained the honor of appearing together on the list of successful candidates. Examining their scholarly attainments, who truly ranked higher and who lower? Some possessed the capacity to uphold the state; others were praised for discernment as clear as ice or a mirror. Thus, the responsibilities the ancients assumed and their ability to judge others were assuredly no matters of idle talk. I do not know…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其人亦可以當之而無愧否乎此皆諸
士子之所習聞者也或宦于斯或產于
斯請詳言其人而評品之以觀尚友之
學
問書曰有備無患詩曰迨天之未陰雨綢
繆牖戶蓋言預也昔者堯水湯旱雖以
七年九年而民無捐瘠也其法無傳焉
不知何道以致之邪比楚大饑前此未
有也徙鬻溝壑所不忍聞諸司多方區
===
畫極力救援帑藏竭矣賑濟行矣雖皆
其焦頭爛額之力而民之瘡痍未瘳今
幸穡功甫告蠲免溥及民賴以活而曲
徙之策尤不可不預為之講也試與諸
士言之積逋淫禁何以紓之而軍儲藩
賦何所取足近鬻遠竄何以復之而資
糧贖金何以能辦刑何以省而使輕重
適中徭何以輕而使欺隱精覈倉以貯
之何法最良而秋出歲盤民何以不困
punctuated:
其人亦可以當之而無愧否乎？此皆諸士子之所習聞者也。或宦于斯，或產于斯，請詳言其人而評品之，以觀尚友之學。

問：書曰：「有備無患。」詩曰：「迨天之未陰雨，綢繆牖戶。」蓋言預也。昔者堯水湯旱，雖以七年九年，而民無捐瘠也。其法無傳焉，不知何道以致之邪？比楚大饑，前此未有也。徙鬻溝壑，所不忍聞。諸司多方區畫，極力救援，帑藏竭矣，賑濟行矣。雖皆其焦頭爛額之力，而民之瘡痍未瘳。今幸穡功甫告，蠲免溥及，民賴以活，而曲徙之策尤不可不預為之講也。試與諸士言之：積逋淫禁，何以紓之，而軍儲藩賦何所取足？近鬻遠竄，何以復之，而資糧贖金何以能辦？刑何以省而使輕重適中？徭何以輕而使欺隱精覈？倉以貯之，何法最良，而秋出歲盤，民何以不困？
translation_en:
…whether those men could indeed merit these descriptions without shame? These are all matters with which you candidates are familiar. Some served as officials here; others were born here. Please discuss these men in detail and assess them, so that we may observe your learning in taking the worthy men of antiquity as friends.

Question: The Book of Documents says, “With preparation, there is no calamity.” The Book of Odes says, “Before the heavens grow overcast and rainy, bind fast the windows and doors.” These speak of preparedness. In antiquity there were floods under Yao and drought under Tang. Though these lasted seven or nine years, the people did not perish or waste away. The methods used have not been transmitted. By what means, then, was this achieved? Recently Chu suffered a great famine, unprecedented in its severity. People migrated, sold themselves or their family members, and perished in ditches—things one cannot bear to hear. The various offices devised plans by every means and exerted themselves fully in relief. The treasuries were exhausted, and relief was distributed. Yet, despite all their desperate exertions—as though scorching their heads and burning their brows—the people's wounds have not healed. Fortunately, the harvest has now just been brought in, and tax remissions have been widely extended; the people depend upon these to survive. But preventive measures—bending the chimney and moving the firewood away—must especially be discussed beforehand. Let us consider these matters with you candidates. How can accumulated arrears and excessive prohibitions [?] be alleviated, and from what sources can military provisions and the revenues due to the princely establishments be supplied in full? How can those sold nearby or driven far away be restored to their homes, and how can provisions for their journey and money for their redemption be obtained? How can punishments be reduced while ensuring that their severity is appropriate? How can labor services be lightened while fraud and concealment are thoroughly investigated? What is the best system for storing grain in granaries, and how can the people be spared hardship from autumn disbursements and annual stocktaking [?]?

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之專切有若或參之者矣夫立而見其參焉其
不離於須臾者乎有時而在輿也則見其倚於
吾之衡焉亦非有象也精神之會悟有若或倚
之者矣在輿而見其倚焉其不違於頃刻者乎
如是則方其未言未行也旣能致夫敬信之極
由是而有言有行也自可妙夫感通之機因諸
心而時措之則天下無不盡同之理本諸身而
順應之則天下無不可與之人惟無言也發之
則皆忠信而人易知易知則有親焉其可以通
===
天下之志者此矣惟無行也履之則皆篤敬而
人易從易從則有功焉其可以一天下之動者
此矣夫何有於蠻貊而况州里有不可行也哉
使或行有未得必吾存誠之功有未至耳子張
盍亦反求諸身而考其言行乎甞觀易曰中孚
吉信及豚魚也夫以豚魚之物中孚尚可感之
况人乎哉故誠能動物人心自然之天不容人
為參焉者也子張學求務外夫子所以敎之者
至矣而猶不免難與為仁者豈鞭辟近裏之功
punctuated:
之專切，有若或參之者矣。夫立而見其參焉，其不離於須臾者乎？有時而在輿也，則見其倚於吾之衡焉，亦非有象也。精神之會悟，有若或倚之者矣。在輿而見其倚焉，其不違於頃刻者乎？如是，則方其未言未行也，旣能致夫敬信之極；由是而有言有行也，自可妙夫感通之機。因諸心而時措之，則天下無不盡同之理；本諸身而順應之，則天下無不可與之人。惟無言也，發之則皆忠信，而人易知；易知則有親焉，其可以通天下之志者此矣。惟無行也，履之則皆篤敬，而人易從；易從則有功焉，其可以一天下之動者此矣。夫何有於蠻貊，而况州里有不可行也哉？使或行有未得，必吾存誠之功有未至耳。子張盍亦反求諸身而考其言行乎？
甞觀《易》曰：「中孚，吉。」信及豚魚也。夫以豚魚之物，中孚尚可感之，况人乎哉？故誠能動物，人心自然之天，不容人為參焉者也。子張學求務外，夫子所以敎之者至矣，而猶不免難與為仁者，豈鞭辟近裏之功
translation_en:
…with such concentrated intensity that it is as though something stood before him. When, standing, he sees it before him, does it not remain with him every instant? At times, when riding in a carriage, he sees it leaning against the crossbar before him; yet this, too, has no visible form. In the mind’s apprehension, it is as though something leaned there. When, riding in a carriage, he sees it leaning there, does it not remain with him every moment? Thus, even before speaking or acting, he can already bring reverence and trustworthiness to their utmost. When he then speaks or acts, he can naturally master the subtle workings of influence and response. Drawing upon his heart and putting this into practice as circumstances require, he finds no principle under Heaven that is not shared in full. Grounding himself in his own person and responding appropriately, he finds no person under Heaven with whom he cannot associate. So long as he does not speak, there is nothing to consider; once he speaks, his words are all loyal and trustworthy, and others readily understand him. Readily understanding him, they feel affection for him: this is how he can bring the aspirations of all under Heaven into communication. So long as he does not act, there is nothing to consider; once he acts, his conduct is all earnest and reverent, and others readily follow him. Readily following him, they accomplish things: this is how he can unite the actions of all under Heaven. What difficulty, then, could there be even among the Man and Mo peoples? How much less could such conduct fail to prevail in one’s own district and village! If his conduct should fail to achieve its purpose, it must simply be that his efforts to preserve sincerity have not yet reached their utmost. Zizhang, why not turn back to yourself and examine your words and deeds?
I have read in the Book of Changes: “Inner Sincerity: auspicious.” Trustworthiness extends even to pigs and fish. If inner sincerity can move even creatures such as pigs and fish, how much more can it move human beings! Thus sincerity can move other beings: this is the spontaneous operation of Heaven within the human heart, admitting no admixture of human contrivance. Zizhang’s learning sought its object outside himself. The Master’s teaching for him was most thorough; yet he still could not escape the judgment that it was difficult to practice humaneness alongside him. Could it be that his effort to discipline himself and penetrate inward…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
終不勝其好高之病與雖然一聞夫子之訓而
卽書諸紳晚年執德信道之機聖門若子張者
不易得也
唯天下至誠爲能盡其性能盡其性則能
盡人之性能盡人之性則能盡物之性
能盡物之性則可以贊天地之化育可
以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
劉旦
同考試官教諭包批至誠盡人物之性而至於參
===
天地皆其盡性之能事也此篇明簡意盡深得其旨錄之以式學者
同考試官教諭周批發明中庸言天道之意殆盡
考試官教諭姜批理融詞到佳作也
考試官教授陸批潔整
中庸舉聖人之盡性而因推極其盛焉夫聖人
者誠而已矣由其身而達於天地則其盛極矣
謂非聖人之能事哉中庸二十二章言天道也
其意蓋曰天地萬物本吾一體人惟誠有未至
則不能盡性而始與天地不相似矣唯天下至
punctuated:
終不勝其好高之病與？雖然，一聞夫子之訓而卽書諸紳，晚年執德信道之機，聖門若子張者不易得也。

「唯天下至誠爲能盡其性，能盡其性則能盡人之性，能盡人之性則能盡物之性，能盡物之性則可以贊天地之化育，可以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣。」
劉旦

同考試官教諭包批：「至誠盡人物之性而至於參天地，皆其盡性之能事也。此篇明簡意盡，深得其旨，錄之以式學者。」
同考試官教諭周批：「發明中庸言天道之意殆盡。」
考試官教諭姜批：「理融詞到，佳作也。」
考試官教授陸批：「潔整。」

中庸舉聖人之盡性，而因推極其盛焉。夫聖人者，誠而已矣。由其身而達於天地，則其盛極矣，謂非聖人之能事哉？中庸二十二章言天道也。其意蓋曰：天地萬物，本吾一體。人惟誠有未至，則不能盡性，而始與天地不相似矣。唯天下至
translation_en:
…ultimately fail to overcome his tendency to aspire too high? Even so, upon hearing the Master's instruction, he immediately wrote it on his sash. This was the germ of his holding firmly to virtue and trusting in the Way in his later years. Among the Master's disciples, someone like Zizhang was not easily found.

“Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize his own nature. Able fully to realize his own nature, he can fully realize the nature of other people. Able fully to realize the nature of other people, he can fully realize the nature of things. Able fully to realize the nature of things, he can assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth. Able to assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, he can form a triad with Heaven and Earth.”
Liu Dan

Comment by Associate Examiner Bao, Instructor: “Through utmost sincerity, fully realizing the nature of people and things and ultimately forming a triad with Heaven and Earth—all these are accomplishments of fully realizing one's nature. This essay is clear and concise, yet exhausts the meaning and profoundly grasps the passage's purport. It is recorded here as a model for students.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “It elucidates almost exhaustively the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean's discussion of the Way of Heaven.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Its principles are thoroughly integrated and its language fully achieves its purpose: an excellent composition.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: “Clean and orderly.”

The Doctrine of the Mean sets forth the sage's full realization of his nature and proceeds to trace its greatness to the utmost. What makes a sage is simply sincerity. Extending from his own person to Heaven and Earth, this greatness reaches its utmost. Could this be called anything other than the sage's accomplishment? Chapter twenty-two of the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way of Heaven. Its meaning is essentially this: Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things fundamentally form one body with me. It is only because people's sincerity falls short that they cannot fully realize their nature and thus cease to resemble Heaven and Earth. Only the utmost under Heaven …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
誠也本之則純粹之精全之則湛一之體其寂
也誠之復也而貞靜立矣其感也誠之通也而
無妄行矣使其有一毫焉而或以殽之有一息
焉而或以貳之則非誠矣豈可以言至乎夫德
無不實則性無不盡以言乎其立本也而化自
我出以言乎其經綸也而典自我惇備道全美
蓋不異於繼善成性之初也已性盡矣由是及
之而盡人之性也則輔翼之以牖其衷而五敎
敷焉五刑弼焉各足而已矣大同之化蓋吾錫
===
類之仁也人性盡矣由是推之而盡物之性也
則區別之以遂其殖而物生阜焉民用興焉各
順而已矣曲成之道蓋吾物與之體也至誠而
至此吾見天統氣焉以職生也地統形焉以職
成也至誠統道焉以職敎也裁成輔相是曰成
能不可以贊天地之化育乎化育可贊吾見天
以覆焉而位于上也地以載焉而位于下也至
誠以化成焉而位乎其中也出入彌綸是曰合
德不可以與天地參乎是則聖人之能事如此
punctuated: 誠也，本之則純粹之精，全之則湛一之體。其寂也，誠之復也，而貞靜立矣；其感也，誠之通也，而無妄行矣。使其有一毫焉而或以殽之，有一息焉而或以貳之，則非誠矣，豈可以言至乎？夫德無不實，則性無不盡。以言乎其立本也，而化自我出；以言乎其經綸也，而典自我惇。備道全美，蓋不異於繼善成性之初也已。性盡矣，由是及之而盡人之性也，則輔翼之以牖其衷，而五敎敷焉，五刑弼焉，各足而已矣。大同之化，蓋吾錫類之仁也。人性盡矣，由是推之而盡物之性也，則區別之以遂其殖，而物生阜焉，民用興焉，各順而已矣。曲成之道，蓋吾物與之體也。至誠而至此，吾見天統氣焉，以職生也；地統形焉，以職成也；至誠統道焉，以職敎也。裁成輔相，是曰成能，不可以贊天地之化育乎？化育可贊，吾見天以覆焉而位于上也，地以載焉而位于下也，至誠以化成焉而位乎其中也。出入彌綸，是曰合德，不可以與天地參乎？是則聖人之能事如此
translation_en:
…sincerity. At its root is an essence of unalloyed purity; in its wholeness is a clear and undivided substance. In stillness, sincerity returns to itself, and steadfast tranquillity is established; in response to things, sincerity flows forth, and action free from falsity proceeds. Were even the slightest admixture to adulterate it, or even a moment’s dividedness to interrupt it, it would no longer be sincerity. How could it be called utmost sincerity? When virtue is wholly real, one’s nature is fully realized. In establishing the foundation, transformation issues from oneself; in ordering affairs, the enduring norms are strengthened through oneself. Complete in the Way and perfect in excellence, one is no different from the original state in which goodness is continued and nature is brought to completion.

Once one’s own nature is fully realized, one extends this to realize fully the nature of other people. One supports and assists them, opening their inner understanding: the five teachings are spread, and the five punishments lend support, so that each person attains fulfillment. The transformation that brings about Great Unity is indeed my benevolence in extending blessings to others of my kind. Once human nature is fully realized, one extends this further to realize fully the nature of things. One distinguishes their different kinds so that each may flourish: living things become abundant, and resources for the people’s use increase, so that each follows its proper course. The Way of bringing each thing to fulfillment is indeed my embodiment of the understanding that all things are my companions.

When utmost sincerity reaches this point, I see Heaven governing vital energy and taking charge of generation; Earth governing physical forms and taking charge of completion; and utmost sincerity governing the Way and taking charge of teaching. Giving due shape and completion, assisting and supporting—this is called fulfilling their capacities. Can it not assist the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth? Since that work can be assisted, I see Heaven covering all and occupying its place above, Earth bearing all and occupying its place below, and utmost sincerity transforming and bringing all to completion while occupying its place between them. Moving within and beyond, embracing and ordering all—this is called uniting in virtue. Can it not form a triad with Heaven and Earth? Such, then, are the sage’s accomplishments…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
豈可以易能邪故曰天之道也抑嘗聞夫子之
賛易也於乾則曰大於坤則曰至而其於堯也
則亦賛之曰大由是觀之子思之言蓋有所本
也已夫天生物而靈於人天生人而靈於聖人
非故以寵異之也亦以參賛之道責之聖人而
已吾故曰其始也以聖人爲天地之心而其終
也以聖人爲天地之用
人人親其親長其長而天下平
蕭廷節
===
同考試官教諭宋批〔能體貼孟子言道在邇而事在易之意〕
同考試官教諭楊批〔過接處有氣力〕
考試官教諭姜批〔發揮詳盡〕
考試官教授陸批〔明切〕
大賢指言孝弟之裕於治示人知所求也夫孝
弟人道之大也達之天下而治平不外是矣何
必求之遠且難哉孟子懼人求道之失也故言
此以曉之蓋曰天下無性外之道而亦無道外
之治求之遠且難者失之矣然而有至近至易
punctuated:
豈可以易能邪？故曰：「天之道也。」抑嘗聞夫子之賛易也，於乾則曰大，於坤則曰至，而其於堯也，則亦賛之曰大。由是觀之，子思之言蓋有所本也已。夫天生物而靈於人，天生人而靈於聖人，非故以寵異之也，亦以參賛之道責之聖人而已。吾故曰：其始也，以聖人爲天地之心；而其終也，以聖人爲天地之用。

人人親其親，長其長，而天下平。
蕭廷節

同考試官教諭楊批〔過接處有氣力〕
考試官教諭姜批〔發揮詳盡〕
考試官教授陸批〔明切〕

大賢指言孝弟之裕於治，示人知所求也。夫孝弟，人道之大也，達之天下，而治平不外是矣，何必求之遠且難哉？孟子懼人求道之失也，故言此以曉之。蓋曰：天下無性外之道，而亦無道外之治，求之遠且難者失之矣。然而有至近至易
translation_en:
…How could such an achievement be easy? Hence the saying, “It is the Way of Heaven.” Moreover, I have heard that when the Master praised the Changes, he called Qian “great” and Kun “supreme”; when speaking of Yao, he likewise praised him as “great.” Viewed in this light, Zisi’s words surely had a foundation. Heaven gives birth to all things, and their spiritual intelligence finds its fullest expression in human beings; Heaven gives birth to human beings, and their spiritual intelligence finds its fullest expression in sages. This is not a deliberate bestowal of special favor upon them: it is simply to charge sages with the Way of standing alongside Heaven and Earth and assisting their work. Thus I say: at the outset, the sage is the heart of Heaven and Earth; in the end, the sage is the instrument through which Heaven and Earth act.

“If everyone loved their own parents and respected their own elders, all under Heaven would be at peace.”
Xiao Tingjie

Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “He aptly grasps Mencius’s meaning that the Way lies near at hand and its practice lies in what is easy.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The transitions have force.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The exposition is thorough.”
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: “Clear and incisive.”

The great worthy expressly states how filial devotion and fraternal respect amply suffice for good government, showing people where to direct their efforts. Filial devotion and fraternal respect are fundamental to the human Way. Extend them throughout all under Heaven, and nothing beyond them is needed for good government and peace. Why seek these in what is distant and difficult? Mencius feared that people would go astray in seeking the Way, and therefore spoke these words to enlighten them. His meaning is this: in all under Heaven, there is no Way outside human nature, nor any good government outside the Way. Those who seek it in what is distant and difficult have missed it. Yet there is what is nearest at hand and easiest…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
者在焉果何以言乎今夫親長在人本甚邇也
親之長之在人為甚易也誠使天下之人皆知
親之不可以不親也于是乎各親其親焉以隆
一本之恩以篤天性之愛蓋油然孝思達焉而
不獨親其親矣皆知長之不可以不長也于是
乎各長其長焉以廣因心之敬以敦友于之情
蓋油然弟道成焉而不獨長其長矣若此者是
蓋率其人道之常似無與於天下之治也然而
天下雖大合親長而有以盡其人民生雖異舉
===
愛敬而莫不同其性今人人親其親長其長則
懿德以孚而天下之為子者莫不知有孝也民
彝以顯而天下之為弟者無不敬其兄也惇本
尚行而篤實之風以行蓋百姓以親五品以遜
熙然大順之治于是昭焉遷善敏德而仁讓之
俗以成蓋各安其分各止其所皡乎合同之化
于斯溥焉雖不期於治而天下自無不平者矣
夫平天下其要不越乎孝弟而事實本於家庭
此之謂道之邇也此之謂事之易也而人顧求
punctuated: 者在焉，果何以言乎？今夫親長，在人本甚邇也；親之長之，在人為甚易也。誠使天下之人皆知親之不可以不親也，于是乎各親其親焉，以隆一本之恩，以篤天性之愛，蓋油然孝思達焉，而不獨親其親矣。皆知長之不可以不長也，于是乎各長其長焉，以廣因心之敬，以敦友于之情，蓋油然弟道成焉，而不獨長其長矣。若此者，是蓋率其人道之常，似無與於天下之治也。然而天下雖大，合親長而有以盡其人；民生雖異，舉愛敬而莫不同其性。今人人親其親、長其長，則懿德以孚，而天下之為子者莫不知有孝也；民彝以顯，而天下之為弟者無不敬其兄也。惇本尚行，而篤實之風以行，蓋百姓以親，五品以遜，熙然大順之治于是昭焉；遷善敏德，而仁讓之俗以成，蓋各安其分，各止其所，皡乎合同之化于斯溥焉。雖不期於治，而天下自無不平者矣。夫平天下，其要不越乎孝弟，而事實本於家庭。此之謂道之邇也，此之謂事之易也，而人顧求
translation_en:
…there is something closest at hand and easiest to accomplish. How, indeed, can this be explained? Parents and elders are, for everyone, very close at hand; loving one’s parents and honoring one’s elders are, for everyone, very easy. If all people under Heaven truly understood that parents must be loved, each would love their own parents, deepening the affection owed to the common source of their being and strengthening the love inherent in their nature. Filial feeling would then flow forth spontaneously, and they would not love only their own parents. If all understood that elders must be honored, each would honor their own elders, extending the reverence arising from the heart and strengthening fraternal affection. The way of brotherly deference would then develop spontaneously, and they would not honor only their own elders.

Such conduct merely follows the constant norms of human relationships and seems to have no bearing on governing all under Heaven. Yet, vast though the world is, parents and elders together encompass all its people; diverse though people’s lives are, all share the same nature when it comes to love and reverence. If everyone now loved their own parents and honored their own elders, fine virtue would inspire trust, and no son under Heaven would fail to understand filial devotion. The enduring norms of human relations would become manifest, and no younger brother under Heaven would fail to respect his elder brother. By strengthening the foundations and esteeming proper conduct, a spirit of sincerity and earnestness would spread: the people would be affectionate, the five human relationships harmonious, and a flourishing order of perfect concord would thus become evident. By turning toward goodness and diligently cultivating virtue, customs of benevolence and deference would take shape: everyone would rest content in their allotted role and remain in their proper place, and the radiant transforming influence of unity and concord would spread everywhere. Even without deliberately seeking good government, all under Heaven would naturally be at peace.

The essentials of bringing peace to all under Heaven extend no further than filial devotion and brotherly deference, and their actual practice is rooted in the household. This is what is meant by the Way’s being close at hand; this is what is meant by the task’s being easy. Yet people instead seek…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
謂黃裳者固有得於黃中通理正位居體之義
矣然是德也豈固有內外之殊邪蓋君子得於
天者旣純粹而不雜故其存於中者自靜正而
无偏渾然至中而天下之大本以立也秩然有
理而隨事之精詳不亂也其在於中也不旣美
乎由是情深而文明而見諸四體者莫非溫恭
之度有孚顒若蓋不言而喻矣四支之暢非中
之流通乎德盛而化神而布諸事業者莫非篤
恭之效至誠无息蓋不見而章矣事業之發非
===
德之宣著乎若此者何以見美之至邪蓋德未
純於中者固不可以言美中之未盛於外者亦
不足以言至也今誠中而發外焉則是統會於
一心者雖甚微而昭著于天下則甚大體用以
一天德王道于是而終矣其寂也立天下之有
而其感也成天下之化內外以合盛德大業于
此而至矣德之美也孰有加於此哉故曰美之
至也文言以此而復釋之則黃裳之義无餘蘊
矣而元吉之獲不亦可徵也邪抑此以坤道言
punctuated: 謂黃裳者，固有得於黃中通理、正位居體之義矣。然是德也，豈固有內外之殊邪？蓋君子得於天者旣純粹而不雜，故其存於中者自靜正而无偏，渾然至中，而天下之大本以立也；秩然有理，而隨事之精詳不亂也。其在於中也，不旣美乎？由是情深而文明，而見諸四體者莫非溫恭之度，有孚顒若，蓋不言而喻矣。四支之暢，非中之流通乎？德盛而化神，而布諸事業者莫非篤恭之效，至誠无息，蓋不見而章矣。事業之發，非德之宣著乎？若此者，何以見美之至邪？蓋德未純於中者，固不可以言美；中之未盛於外者，亦不足以言至也。今誠中而發外焉，則是統會於一心者雖甚微，而昭著于天下則甚大。體用以一，天德王道于是而終矣；其寂也立天下之有，而其感也成天下之化，內外以合，盛德大業于此而至矣。德之美也，孰有加於此哉？故曰：「美之至也。」文言以此而復釋之，則黃裳之義无餘蘊矣，而元吉之獲不亦可徵也邪？抑此以坤道言
translation_en:
…what is meant by “a yellow lower garment” indeed grasps the meaning of being yellow at the center and penetrating the underlying patterns, occupying the correct position and abiding in the proper embodiment. Yet does this virtue inherently admit a distinction between inner and outer? What the gentleman receives from Heaven is pure and unmixed; hence what he preserves within is naturally still and correct, without partiality. Wholly integrated in perfect centrality, it establishes the great foundation of all under Heaven; orderly and patterned, it remains precise and detailed in responding to each affair, without confusion. Is it not already beautiful as it resides within?

From this, his feelings are deep and his cultivated qualities shine forth. What appears in his four limbs invariably displays a warm and reverent bearing. Possessing sincerity and a dignified presence, he makes himself understood without speaking. Is not this free expression through the four limbs the circulation of what lies within? His virtue is abundant and his transforming influence wondrous. What he extends to his undertakings invariably manifests the effects of earnest reverence. Perfectly sincere and unceasing, he becomes illustrious without displaying himself. Is not the unfolding of his undertakings the manifest expression of his virtue?

How does this reveal beauty at its utmost? If virtue is not pure within, one certainly cannot speak of beauty; if what lies within does not flourish outwardly, neither is it sufficient to speak of the utmost. Now, with sincerity within finding expression without, what is gathered together in a single heart, though exceedingly subtle, becomes exceedingly great when manifested throughout the world. Substance and function are thereby united, and heavenly virtue and the kingly Way attain their consummation here. In its stillness it establishes all that exists under Heaven; in its responsiveness it accomplishes the transformations of all under Heaven. Inner and outer are thereby joined, and abundant virtue and great undertakings reach their utmost here. What could surpass this beauty of virtue? Thus it is said: “Beauty at its utmost.”

When the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) further explains it in these terms, the meaning of “a yellow lower garment” has no hidden implications left unexplored. And does not the attainment of supreme good fortune thereby become verifiable? Yet this speaks in terms of the Way of Kun…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之故有取于中順之德然其於乾又曰剛健豈
聖人之道有不同邪蓋天地之化動靜相生故
其變无窮聖人之德剛柔成性故其化无外此
固乾坤合體之妙而聖人參賛之功所由以盛
也讀易者默而識之思過半矣
易其至矣乎夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業
也知崇禮卑崇效天卑法地天地設位
而易行乎其中矣成性存存道義之門
高斅
===
同考試官教諭宋批通篇體製明整迥異諸作且
首尾見易道之至深得夫子賛易之旨
同考試官教諭楊批潔淨精微誠易作也
考試官教諭姜批不鑿不浮可以為式
考試官教授陸批簡而盡
大傳賛易道之至必詳夫用易者以見之也夫
德崇業廣聖人盡道之極也而皆資夫易焉不
可以見易道之至乎且昔者聖人之作易也將
以順性命之理而人以卜筮小之不知易者也
punctuated:
之，故有取于中順之德。然其於乾又曰剛健，豈聖人之道有不同邪？蓋天地之化，動靜相生，故其變无窮；聖人之德，剛柔成性，故其化无外。此固乾坤合體之妙，而聖人參賛之功所由以盛也。讀易者默而識之，思過半矣。
「易其至矣乎！夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。」
高斅
同考試官教諭宋批：通篇體製明整，迥異諸作。且首尾見易道之至，深得夫子賛易之旨。
同考試官教諭楊批：潔淨精微，誠易作也。
考試官教諭姜批：不鑿不浮，可以為式。
考試官教授陸批：簡而盡。
大傳賛易道之至，必詳夫用易者以見之也。夫德崇業廣，聖人盡道之極也，而皆資夫易焉，不可以見易道之至乎？且昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，而人以卜筮小之，不知易者也。
translation_en:
…thus, it draws upon the virtues of centrality and compliance. Yet concerning Qian it also speaks of firmness and vigor. Could there be differences within the Way of the sage? In the transforming processes of Heaven and Earth, movement and stillness generate one another, so their changes are inexhaustible. In the sage’s virtue, firmness and yielding constitute his nature, so his transforming influence excludes nothing. This is indeed the subtle wonder of Qian and Kun united as one, and the means by which the sage’s achievement in participating in and assisting their transforming work flourishes. Those who read the Changes and silently comprehend this will have grasped more than half of its meaning.
“How consummate are the Changes! The Changes are that by which the sage exalts his virtue and enlarges his undertakings. Wisdom is lofty; ritual propriety is humble. Loftiness emulates Heaven; humility models itself on Earth. Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and change operates between them. Continually preserving one’s fully realized nature is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.”
Gao Xiao 高斅
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: The entire composition is clear and orderly in form, markedly different from the other essays. Moreover, from beginning to end it reveals the consummate character of the Way of the Changes, profoundly grasping the Master’s intent in praising the Changes.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Pure, precise, and subtle: truly an essay worthy of the Changes.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Neither forced nor superficial; it may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: Concise yet comprehensive.
In praising the consummate character of the Way of the Changes, the Great Commentary must explain in detail those who put the Changes into practice in order to make this evident. To exalt virtue and enlarge undertakings is for the sage to realize the utmost reaches of the Way. Yet both depend upon the Changes. Does this not reveal the consummate character of the Way of the Changes? Moreover, when the sages of antiquity composed the Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and Heaven’s decree. Those who diminish it by treating it merely as divination by turtle shell and milfoil do not understand the Changes.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
故夫子賛之曰易之爲書也其至矣乎夫何以
見之也蓋日新之謂盛德而聖人之德不可及
矣然所以崇者易崇之也富有之謂大業而聖
人之業不可限矣然所以廣者易廣之也是故
德莫大於智業莫要於禮也聖人以易窮理而
智於是崇焉以易循理而禮於是卑焉智禮極
其崇卑則知行益見其明實矣是故莫髙者天
莫卑者地也聖人之智崇也足以效乎天焉其
禮卑也足以法乎地焉崇卑象乎天地則德業
===
益見其崇廣矣盍自天地而觀之乎彼天尊地
卑而乾坤有以奠其位則陽變陰化而推行有
以妙其機故易行乎其中矣聖人智禮兼盡則
性達於天而全於已者既能存至誠无息之體
由是理本於一而散於萬者自可妙時出无窮
之化由當然而有所謂道焉道本此出蓋推行
而无盡也由裁制而有所謂義焉義從此出蓋
充足而有餘也豈非道義之門乎道義出於成
性之餘其與變化行於天地設位之中也一矣
punctuated: 故夫子賛之曰：「易之爲書也，其至矣乎！」夫何以見之也？蓋日新之謂盛德，而聖人之德不可及矣；然所以崇者，易崇之也。富有之謂大業，而聖人之業不可限矣；然所以廣者，易廣之也。是故德莫大於智，業莫要於禮也。聖人以易窮理，而智於是崇焉；以易循理，而禮於是卑焉。智禮極其崇卑，則知行益見其明實矣。是故莫髙者天，莫卑者地也。聖人之智崇也，足以效乎天焉；其禮卑也，足以法乎地焉。崇卑象乎天地，則德業益見其崇廣矣。盍自天地而觀之乎？彼天尊地卑，而乾坤有以奠其位，則陽變陰化，而推行有以妙其機，故易行乎其中矣。聖人智禮兼盡，則性達於天，而全於已者既能存至誠无息之體；由是理本於一，而散於萬者自可妙時出无窮之化。由當然而有所謂道焉，道本此出，蓋推行而无盡也；由裁制而有所謂義焉，義從此出，蓋充足而有餘也。豈非道義之門乎？道義出於成性之餘，其與變化行於天地設位之中也一矣。
translation_en:
Thus the Master praised it, saying: “As a book, the Changes is surely consummate!” How can this be seen? Daily renewal is called flourishing virtue, and the sage’s virtue cannot be matched. Yet what exalts it is the Changes. Abundant possession is called great achievement, and the sage’s achievement cannot be bounded. Yet what broadens it is the Changes. Thus, in virtue nothing is greater than wisdom, and in achievement nothing is more essential than ritual propriety. Through the Changes, the sage exhaustively investigates principle, and his wisdom thereby becomes exalted; through the Changes, he follows principle, and his ritual propriety thereby becomes lowly. When wisdom and ritual propriety attain the utmost in exaltation and lowliness, his knowledge and conduct become ever more manifest in their clarity and substance.

Thus nothing is higher than Heaven, and nothing lower than Earth. The exaltation of the sage’s wisdom suffices to emulate Heaven; the lowliness of his ritual propriety suffices to model itself on Earth. When their exaltation and lowliness take Heaven and Earth as their pattern, his virtue and achievement become ever more manifest in their exaltation and breadth. Why not consider this through Heaven and Earth? Heaven is exalted and Earth lowly, and Qian and Kun thereby establish their positions. Yang changes and yin transforms, and their ongoing operation gives wondrous play to the workings of change. Thus change proceeds within them.

When the sage fully realizes both wisdom and ritual propriety, his nature reaches Heaven, and what is complete within himself [?] can preserve the substance of utmost sincerity, which never ceases. Consequently, principle, rooted in the one and dispersed among the myriad things, can wondrously bring forth inexhaustible transformations as their times arise. From what ought to be comes what is called the Way: the Way issues from this source, proceeding without end. From discerning and determining comes what is called righteousness: righteousness issues from this source, abundant and more than sufficient. Is this not the gateway of the Way and righteousness? The Way and righteousness issue as the abundant consequence of bringing one’s nature to completion; this is one with the operation of change and transformation amid Heaven and Earth once their positions are established.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
此固聖人德崇而業廣也然皆本之易夫易豈
不至矣乎抑此亦聖人窮理盡性以至於命也
蓋崇德者窮理之始也廣業者盡性之終也成
性存而與天地合則又至於命矣然皆以用易
爲言豈聖人一一而取諸易哉蓋易固待聖人
而後用而聖人齊戒神明其德蓋自有心易之
妙也其言用易者此固聖人教人以學易之本
心也
書
===
惟學遜志務時敏厥修乃來允懷于兹道
積于厥躬惟斅學半念終始典于學厥
德修罔覺
劉旦

藹然溢於言表
同考試官教諭周 批 格整詞潔
考試官教諭姜 批 詳盡
考試官教授陸 批 舂容
punctuated:
此固聖人德崇而業廣也，然皆本之易。夫易豈不至矣乎？抑此亦聖人窮理盡性以至於命也。蓋崇德者，窮理之始也；廣業者，盡性之終也。成性存而與天地合，則又至於命矣。然皆以用易爲言，豈聖人一一而取諸易哉？蓋易固待聖人而後用，而聖人齊戒，神明其德，蓋自有心易之妙也。其言用易者，此固聖人教人以學易之本心也。

書

惟學遜志，務時敏，厥修乃來。允懷于兹，道積于厥躬。惟斅學半，念終始典于學，厥德修罔覺。

劉旦

translation_en:
This indeed is how the sage’s virtue becomes exalted and his accomplishments extensive; yet all of it is rooted in the Changes. Are not the Changes utterly consummate? This, too, is the sage’s fathoming of principle and full realization of his nature, thereby reaching Heaven’s mandate. For exalting virtue is the beginning of fathoming principle, and extending accomplishments is the culmination of fully realizing one’s nature. When one preserves one’s perfected nature and accords with Heaven and Earth, one further reaches Heaven’s mandate. Yet these things are all spoken of as applying the Changes. Does this mean that the sage takes each and every thing from the Changes? The Changes indeed await the sage before being put to use, while the sage purifies himself and fasts, making his virtue spiritually luminous: he possesses within himself the subtle workings of the Changes in his own mind. To speak of applying the Changes thus expresses the sage’s original intention in teaching people to study the Changes.

Teaching is half of learning. Keep your thoughts, from beginning to end, constantly upon learning, and your virtue will develop without your noticing it.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大臣告君爲學在協體用而詣其極也夫學以
立體教以達用也大臣告君而極言之玆其爲
聖學之要乎想昔傅說之意若曰帝王之治本
於道帝王之道本於心吾王圖治莫要于學矣
然豈可以或偏乎吾王一身所以作則萬邦也
學不豫則無以爲感化之原而道因之以日遠
矣必於學也存之以虛以遜其志體之以健以
敏其功則其心足以有受也其力足以有爲也
而道以修而來矣然道無終窮也于是而自足
===
焉所得不亦狹乎必於此而篤信焉以致其專
而念玆在玆合久暫而一致也斯則光明得於
緝煕逢原本於深造而道之在我者蓋有以統
會之而無遺者矣豈徒恭默之爲思也乎然猶
未也吾王之心欲以康擾兆民也教未施則無
以徵聖修之極而德由之以弗崇矣必於教也
以吾之天叙以惇典焉以吾之天秩以庸禮焉
則其以成物也亦所以成己也而學居其半矣
然學無止法也于此而自息焉所得豈能至乎
punctuated: 大臣告君，爲學在協體用而詣其極也。夫學以立體，教以達用也。大臣告君而極言之，玆其爲聖學之要乎！想昔傅說之意若曰：帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心，吾王圖治，莫要于學矣。然豈可以或偏乎？吾王一身，所以作則萬邦也。學不豫，則無以爲感化之原，而道因之以日遠矣。必於學也，存之以虛，以遜其志；體之以健，以敏其功，則其心足以有受也，其力足以有爲也，而道以修而來矣。然道無終窮也，于是而自足焉，所得不亦狹乎？必於此而篤信焉，以致其專，而念玆在玆，合久暫而一致也。斯則光明得於緝煕，逢原本於深造，而道之在我者，蓋有以統會之而無遺者矣。豈徒恭默之爲思也乎？然猶未也。吾王之心，欲以康擾兆民也。教未施，則無以徵聖修之極，而德由之以弗崇矣。必於教也，以吾之天叙以惇典焉，以吾之天秩以庸禮焉，則其以成物也，亦所以成己也，而學居其半矣。然學無止法也，于此而自息焉，所得豈能至乎？
translation_en:
A great minister tells his ruler that learning consists in harmonizing substance and function and bringing them to their utmost realization. Learning establishes substance; teaching brings function into effect. When a great minister addresses his ruler and expounds this fully, is this not the essential principle of sagely learning? We may imagine that Fu Yue’s meaning in former times was as follows: The government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and their Way is rooted in the heart. For our king, in seeking good government, nothing is more essential than learning. Yet how could this admit of any one-sidedness? Our king, in his own person, serves as the model for the myriad states. Unless learning is undertaken in advance, there will be no source of transformative influence, and the Way will consequently grow more distant day by day. In learning, you must preserve an open mind, making your resolve humble, and embody vigor, making your efforts diligent. Then your heart will be capable of receiving instruction, and your strength capable of accomplishment; through cultivation, the Way will come to you. Yet the Way has no end or limit. If you become content with yourself at this point, will your attainment not be narrow? You must therefore hold firmly to it in faith, making your dedication undivided: keep your thoughts upon it and remain intent upon it, maintaining the same constancy over long periods and brief moments alike. Thus illumination is attained through continuous cultivation, and finding the source wherever one turns rests upon profound study. The Way within oneself can then be comprehensively integrated, with nothing omitted. Could this be merely a matter of pondering in reverent silence?

Yet this is still not all. Our king’s heart desires to bring peace and order to the countless people. Unless teaching is put into practice, there will be no means of demonstrating the utmost attainment of sagely cultivation, and virtue will consequently fail to become exalted. In teaching, you must employ the Heaven-established relationships within yourself to strengthen the constant norms, and employ the Heaven-established distinctions within yourself to put ritual propriety into practice. Then bringing others to fulfillment will also be the means of fulfilling yourself, and learning will constitute half of the process. Yet learning admits of no stopping point. If you rest from your efforts here, how can your attainment reach its utmost?

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭姜批文有法度亦善說經者
考試官教授陸批詞理俱到
大臣述前聖之致治建三宅之官而任之職也
蓋三宅所以總治者也前聖舉而任之職焉其
知恤也為可見矣宜周公述之以為成王告也
意謂人君以圖治為先圖治以任賢為要是故
昔者文王武王之立政也設官分職以為民極
所以詔爵而詔祿者有以極法制之備體國經
治以圖化理所以敘位而班秩者有以盡典則
===
之詳政莫大于天事也則宅乃事者有所謂常
任之任人焉政莫大于天法也則宅乃準者有
所謂有司之準夫焉政莫大于夫民也則宅乃
牧者有所謂常伯之牧夫焉是則三宅之官也
而其職果何如哉量才以授之而總之官聯以
會其要度德以任之而明之法守以考其成任
人使掌事典以經邦國而咸熙之績著焉所以
理天事者係之矣準人使掌刑典以平邦國而
明允之公勅焉所以守天法者係之矣牧夫使

大臣述前聖之致治，建三宅之官而任之職也。
蓋三宅所以總治者也。前聖舉而任之職焉，其知恤也為可見矣，宜周公述之以為成王告也。

Examiner Jiang, School Instructor, comments: “The composition follows sound rules and also shows skill in expounding the Classics.”
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
A great minister recounts how the former sage kings achieved good government by establishing the offices of the Three Appointments and entrusting their holders with duties.
The Three Appointments were the means of overseeing government as a whole. The former sage kings selected men and entrusted them with these duties, thereby demonstrating their understanding of what required care. It was fitting that the Duke of Zhou should recount this to admonish King Cheng.
The meaning is that a ruler’s first concern is to seek good government, and that employing worthy men is essential to this pursuit. Thus, when Kings Wen and Wu established their government, they instituted offices and apportioned duties, providing a standard for the people. In proclaiming ranks and stipends, they brought laws and institutions to completeness. They organized the state and ordered its government to bring about moral transformation and good order; in arranging official positions and distributing grades of rank, they made the established rules fully detailed.
Nothing in government is greater than Heaven’s affairs: thus, among those appointed to handle affairs were the so-called regular officeholders, the men entrusted with affairs. Nothing in government is greater than Heaven’s laws: thus, among those appointed to uphold standards were the so-called responsible officials, the men entrusted with standards. Nothing in government is greater than the people: thus, among those appointed to shepherd them were the so-called regular chiefs, the shepherds of the people. These, then, were the offices of the Three Appointments. What, precisely, were their duties?
Men were granted office according to an assessment of their abilities, and their work was coordinated through the interconnection of offices to bring its essentials together. They were appointed according to an assessment of their virtue, and the rules they were to uphold were made clear so that their achievements could be examined. Those entrusted with affairs were charged with administering the canons of affairs to order the realm, making manifest the achievement of universal prosperity: on them depended the management of Heaven’s affairs. Those entrusted with standards were charged with administering the penal canons to bring equity to the realm, thereby establishing an impartiality that was discerning and just [?]: on them depended the upholding of Heaven’s laws. title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
掌教典以和邦國而保惠之化洽焉所以子天
民者係之矣官常之所定各有攸司而天工之
代惟其任也體統之所存各專其業而帝載之
熈斯其職也非所以作三事乎吁此文武之以
人立政莫有要于此者也不可以見其知恤乎
成王宜知所法矣雖然知恤固用人之道而君
心則知恤之原故文武之所以知恤者其本尤
在于正心也蓋其緝熈敬止敬義夾持則本源
澄徹而用人之本端矣其知恤也固有自哉然
===
則成王欲法文武之知恤又當于其心焉圖之
詩
充耳琇瑩會弁如星
許宏用
同考試官教諭阮批義正而詞足以發之可謂得
風人之趣矣子亦可言詩者
同考試官教諭林批簡嚴得體
同考試官學正何批講琇瑩如星處縝密
考試官教諭姜批詞莊
punctuated:
掌教典以和邦國，而保惠之化洽焉，所以子天民者係之矣。官常之所定，各有攸司，而天工之代，惟其任也；體統之所存，各專其業，而帝載之熈，斯其職也。非所以作三事乎？吁！此文武之以人立政，莫有要于此者也，不可以見其知恤乎？成王宜知所法矣。雖然，知恤固用人之道，而君心則知恤之原，故文武之所以知恤者，其本尤在于正心也。蓋其緝熈敬止，敬義夾持，則本源澄徹，而用人之本端矣。其知恤也固有自哉！然則成王欲法文武之知恤，又當于其心焉圖之。

詩
充耳琇瑩，會弁如星。
許宏用

translation_en:
…to administer the statutes of instruction in order to harmonize the realm, so that the transforming influence of protection and kindness reaches everywhere: on this depends the nurturing of Heaven’s people as one’s children. The established duties of office each have their particular charge, and carrying out Heaven’s work on its behalf is their responsibility. Within the governing hierarchy, each attends exclusively to his own business, and bringing the Supreme Lord’s undertakings to flourishing completion is his duty. Is this not how the three kinds of service are accomplished? Ah! In Kings Wen and Wu’s establishment of government through the right men, nothing was more essential than this. Does this not reveal their understanding of what required care? King Cheng should recognize what he ought to emulate.

Nevertheless, understanding what requires care is indeed the way to employ men, but the ruler’s heart is the source of that understanding. Thus, the foundation of Kings Wen and Wu’s understanding lay above all in rectifying their hearts. By continuing in luminous virtue and abiding in reverence, sustained on either side by reverence and righteousness, they made the source clear and pure and set right the foundation for employing men. Their understanding assuredly had its source! Therefore, if King Cheng wished to emulate Kings Wen and Wu’s understanding of what required care, he too had to seek it within his own heart.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授陸批〔雅重〕
詩人美賢侯服飾之盛見其德之稱也夫有其
服而無其德君子謂之弗衷詩人以是美武公
其賢於人遠矣此美武公作也蓋曰人君之有
身也以受命也而其有威儀也所以定命也觀
我公之服飾而知其不苟矣今夫瑱之於身所
以揜其聰也瑱而以琇瑩爲之取其縝密焉以
近於玉也取其堅貞焉以類乎德也吾見瑱以
充耳纊以垂瑱純澤而無瑕粹然精華之旁達
===
蓋與衡紞紘綖而竝麗者矣雖位宁有典倚几
有諫公其聽於無聲矣乎今夫弁之於身所以
莊其首也會弁而以玉飾之比之以五色昭其
物也綦之以三采昭其文也吾見玉以華弁采
以間玉溫潤而有光煥然精彩之炫耀有若明
星麗天之在上者矣蓋告朔則服眡朝則服公
其望之儼然矣乎由此觀之充耳可有也會弁
可有也而公之德不可有也此其所以爲有斐
也與抑疑之昔者哀公問舜冠於夫子夫子不
punctuated:
考試官敎授陸批〔雅重〕。

詩人美賢侯服飾之盛，見其德之稱也。夫有其服而無其德，君子謂之弗衷。詩人以是美武公，其賢於人遠矣。此美武公作也。蓋曰：人君之有身也，以受命也；而其有威儀也，所以定命也。觀我公之服飾，而知其不苟矣。今夫瑱之於身，所以揜其聰也。瑱而以琇瑩爲之，取其縝密焉，以近於玉也；取其堅貞焉，以類乎德也。吾見瑱以充耳，纊以垂瑱，純澤而無瑕，粹然精華之旁達，蓋與衡紞紘綖而竝麗者矣。雖位宁有典，倚几有諫，公其聽於無聲矣乎！今夫弁之於身，所以莊其首也。會弁而以玉飾之，比之以五色，昭其物也；綦之以三采，昭其文也。吾見玉以華弁，采以間玉，溫潤而有光，煥然精彩之炫耀，有若明星麗天之在上者矣。蓋告朔則服，眡朝則服，公其望之儼然矣乎！由此觀之，充耳可有也，會弁可有也，而公之德不可有也。此其所以爲有斐也與！抑疑之：昔者哀公問舜冠於夫子，夫子不
translation_en:
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: 〔Elegant and dignified.〕

The poet praises the splendor of the worthy lord’s dress and ornaments, showing how they accord with his virtue. For one who possesses such dress but lacks the corresponding virtue is deemed by the gentleman to be ill-matched to it. That the poet praises Duke Wu in these terms shows how far his worth surpassed that of others. This poem was composed in praise of Duke Wu. Its meaning is this: a ruler has his person in order to receive Heaven’s mandate; he possesses an imposing and dignified bearing in order to secure that mandate. Observing our lord’s dress and ornaments, we know that he is careless in nothing.

Now, the ear pendants worn upon the person serve to screen his hearing. In making these pendants from lustrous stones, one values their fine, close texture, which approaches that of jade, and their firmness and constancy, which resemble virtue. I see the pendants placed beside the ears, suspended from floss silk: pure in luster and without flaw, their refined brilliance radiates on every side. They shine together with the cap’s crosspiece, suspension cords, fastening cords, and covering. Though established rules attend his standing in the court, and admonitions attend his leaning upon the armrest, does not our lord hear even where there is no sound?

Now, the ceremonial cap worn upon the person serves to dignify the head. The cap’s seams are ornamented with jade: the pieces are arranged in five colors to display their substance, and strung with cords of three colors to display their pattern. I see jade adorning the cap, with colored cords interspersed among it: warm and lustrous, it shines with dazzling brilliance, like bright stars set in the heavens above. He wears it when announcing the new moon and wears it when holding court. How solemn our lord appears to those who behold him!

Viewed in this light, ear pendants may be possessed, and a cap with ornamented seams may be possessed, but our lord’s virtue cannot be possessed so readily. Is this not what makes him ‘so refined’? Yet a doubt arises: formerly, Duke Ai asked the Master about Shun’s cap, and the Master did not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
對蓋以舜德好生舍此不問而冠是問是以不
對而詩人獨拳拳於充耳會弁以詠歌焉何邪
曰吾嘗以抑之雅與夫左史倚相所聞者觀之
武公其蓋幾於知道矣無我老耄之箴其猶在
九十有五之後乎夫服以昭德服之不衷身之
災也夫子之諷諫也其亦詩人之詠頌乎觀夫
子而後可以言詩
明昭有周式序在位載戢干戈載櫜弓矢
我求懿德肆于時夏允王保之
===
李正時
