考試官教諭姜批：駢儷典則，可取。
考試官教授陸批：得體。
太平興國二年正月某日，臣某等伏蒙聖恩錫宴及綠袍鞾笏、詩二章者。伏以羲畫堯言，麗珠璣於北斗；周篚商鼎，出珍綺於上方。氣協雲龍，惠均苹鹿。際龍飛之景運，煥奎聚之人文。臣某等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言：虞帝闢門，明山彝以作服；殷宗審象，賴麴糱以交修。惟上下之志通，故地天之道泰。賡歌不聞於喜起，幽側安
translation_en:
…the second year of the Taiping Xingguo reign (977).
By Xu Hongyong.
Associate Examiner Ruan, Instructor, comments: “The allusions are apt and substantive, and the diction classical and elegant. This is more than mere skill in four-and-six parallel prose. Is it not an outstanding piece of writing!”
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The fine phrases grow ever more marvelous as they unfold. Reading this work is like hearing the music of Shao and Huo: one cannot help feeling one's mind open and clear. Worth selecting, worth selecting!”
Associate Examiner He, Director of Studies, comments: “The gratitude expressed in this memorial overflows beyond its words.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The parallel prose conforms to classical standards and merits selection.”
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: “Appropriate to the form.”
On a certain day of the first month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo, your servants, So-and-so and others, humbly received Your Majesty's gracious gifts of a banquet, green robes, boots, audience tablets, and two poems. We reverently reflect: like Fuxi's diagrams and Yao's words, your writings shine as pearls and gems beside the Northern Dipper; like the Zhou baskets of gifts and the Shang cauldrons, precious treasures and patterned silks issue from the imperial repositories. Our vital energies accord like clouds following the dragon; your bounty extends equally to us, as to the deer feeding on mugwort in the ode. Encountering the splendid fortune of your dragon's ascent to the throne, we behold the brilliance of literary culture, as when the stars gather in the constellation Kui. Your servants, So-and-so and others, truly joyful and truly delighted, bow our heads to the ground and knock our foreheads upon it, submitting these words:
The emperor of Yu opened his gates to worthy men and displayed the mountain and ritual-vessel emblems in making ceremonial robes. The Shang king examined the portrait of the man he sought and relied upon his minister as upon yeast and malt, that ruler and minister might cultivate one another. Only when the intentions of those above and below communicate does the Way of Earth and Heaven attain the harmony of the hexagram Tai. If the answering songs of rejoicing and rising to service are no longer heard, how can those hidden away in humble stations …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
望於明揚雖拊髀以興思豈借才於異代
顧玆
希典實出
昌朝伏念臣某等菲葑下體糟粕斷經技空
拙於雕蟲才僅施於襪線詎意網羅之盛
選濫塵麟鳳之兼收需雲著象於六爻章
天抒歌於四始履傳飾足畢讚牧身懽授
粲於緇衣記對命於玉藻嬰心入寐顧影
生慚被褐敢負於懷珠囊螢自分於食藿
===
同岱畎之絲枲獲貢
王廷比野人之藻芹豈甘田畝文非韓愈詎
懷龍虎之榮策愧仲舒孰抱天人之業不
謂縉紳之盛事聿振
醇世之希聲心敢侈于五榮
恩獨殊於九宴歌擊筑於漢祖惜霸心其猶存
忘設醴于穆生歎明時之不值弊衣空泣
於寶應折俎粗寵於宣徽開聞喜於曲江
徒炫醵金之會兆先幾於神柳但符尚象
punctuated: 望於明揚。雖拊髀以興思，豈借才於異代？顧玆希典，實出昌朝。伏念臣某等，菲葑下體，糟粕斷經；技空拙於雕蟲，才僅施於襪線。詎意網羅之盛選，濫塵麟鳳之兼收。需雲著象於六爻，章天抒歌於四始。履傳飾足，畢讚牧身；懽授粲於緇衣，記對命於玉藻。嬰心入寐，顧影生慚。被褐敢負於懷珠，囊螢自分於食藿。同岱畎之絲枲，獲貢王廷；比野人之藻芹，豈甘田畝？文非韓愈，詎懷龍虎之榮；策愧仲舒，孰抱天人之業？不謂縉紳之盛事，聿振醇世之希聲。心敢侈于五榮，恩獨殊於九宴。歌擊筑於漢祖，惜霸心其猶存；忘設醴于穆生，歎明時之不值。弊衣空泣於寶應，折俎粗寵於宣徽。開聞喜於曲江，徒炫醵金之會；兆先幾於神柳，但符尚象
translation_en:
…hope to be recognized and raised to office. Though a ruler might slap his thigh in longing for worthy men, why borrow talent from another age? This rare ceremony indeed proceeds from a flourishing court. We humbly reflect that we, your servants So-and-so, are like the lowly roots of radishes and turnips, possessing only the dregs and fragments of the Classics. Our skill is vainly spent on clumsy literary ornament; our talent is as slight as thread for sewing stockings. How could we have expected that your magnificent search for worthy men would indiscriminately admit us among the qilin and phoenixes?

The clouds of the hexagram Waiting present their image through its six lines; songs displaying Heaven’s pattern find expression in the four beginnings of the Book of Odes. The commentary on Treading speaks of adorning the feet, while Bi praises the nurturing of the person [?]. We rejoice at the provision of food in “Black Robes,” and record our response to your command according to “Jade Pendants.” These thoughts cling to our hearts even in sleep; looking upon our own shadows, we feel ashamed. Though clothed in coarse cloth, how dare we betray the pearl cherished within? Studying by bagged fireflies, we accept our humble fare of bean leaves. Like the silk and hemp from the valleys of Mount Dai, we have been presented as tribute to the royal court. Like a rustic offering water plants and celery, how could we be content to remain among the fields?

Our writing is no match for Han Yu’s: how could we aspire to the glory of dragons and tigers? Our policy essays fall short of Dong Zhongshu’s: who among us possesses his mastery of Heaven and humanity? We never imagined that this splendid occasion for the gentry would revive the rare strains of an age of pure virtue. How dare our hearts presume upon the five glories? Your favor is uniquely distinguished among the nine banquets.

When a song was sung to the zhu before Gaozu of Han, it was regrettable that his ambition for hegemony still remained. When sweet wine was no longer provided for Mu Sheng, one could only lament his failure to encounter an enlightened age. In the Baoying reign, tears over tattered clothing were shed in vain; at the Xuanhui Court, portions of sacrificial meat conferred but modest favor [?]. The celebration of good examination news at Qujiang merely displayed the splendor of a feast funded by pooled contributions. The anticipation of an auspicious sign in the divine willow merely accorded with the practice of esteeming images [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
洪恩暢而冠蓋雲集金釀玉削俾襲鴈塔以
新題
鳳翥龍蟠忽燭雲霄而下濟魚躍式逢於雷
化鷺序幸竊於玉聯學豈儒宗叨荷韋彪
之珍襲賦非德諷竝受司馬之金莖復信
美馬周之飾羶耀握嘉孫樵之起鯁飽大
官之清馥恍新睹於膏梁釋韋布之卑微
懽初陪于履舄臣某等敢不曳婁拜賜煥
衣被於
===
日華什襲寶藏思對揚於
天藻飾先簠簋補效
袞衣操節肯變於伐檀勛名懼慙於濡鵜釀
經酣史敢廢淵源緯治經邦誓懷糜隕伏
願煥爛時歌於
舜旦璣衡長運於
堯尊
配地配天彌綸
至誠之功化
punctuated:
洪恩暢而冠蓋雲集，金釀玉削，俾襲鴈塔以新題。鳳翥龍蟠，忽燭雲霄而下濟；魚躍式逢於雷化，鷺序幸竊於玉聯。學豈儒宗，叨荷韋彪之珍襲；賦非德諷，竝受司馬之金莖。復信美馬周之飾羶，耀握嘉孫樵之起鯁。飽大官之清馥，恍新睹於膏梁；釋韋布之卑微，懽初陪于履舄。
臣某等敢不曳婁拜賜，煥衣被於日華；什襲寶藏，思對揚於天藻。飾先簠簋，補效袞衣；操節肯變於伐檀，勛名懼慙於濡鵜。釀經酣史，敢廢淵源；緯治經邦，誓懷糜隕。
伏願煥爛時歌於舜旦，璣衡長運於堯尊，配地配天，彌綸至誠之功化。
translation_en:
…Vast imperial grace spreads abroad, and officials in their caps and carriages gather like clouds. With golden brew and carved jade [?], we are enabled to follow our predecessors with newly inscribed names upon the Wild Goose Pagoda. Phoenixes soar and dragons coil: suddenly their radiance lights the cloudy heavens and descends to aid us. Like leaping fish, we encounter the thunder that brings transformation; among the ordered ranks of egrets, we are fortunate to obtain an undeserved place in the jade-linked company of officials. How could our learning make us masters of the Confucian tradition? Yet we undeservedly receive the precious gifts associated with Wei Biao. Our rhapsodies offer no admonition through virtue, yet we likewise receive Sima’s golden stalk [?]. Again, truly admirable is Ma Zhou’s embellishment of rank fare [?]; the brilliance held in our hands commends Sun Qiao’s awakening of forthright speech [?]. Sated with the pure fragrance of food from the Court of Imperial Entertainments, we seem to encounter fine grain and rich meat for the first time. Leaving behind the lowly condition of leather belts and plain cloth, we rejoice to join, for the first time, the company of those in ceremonial footwear.
How could your servants, So-and-so and the others, fail to trail their robes and bow in acknowledgment of these gifts, splendidly clothed in the sun’s radiance? Wrapping them in many layers and treasuring them, we intend gratefully to proclaim the imperial literary grace. In adorning ourselves, we put ritual vessels first, and strive to mend the imperial dragon robe through our service. In maintaining our integrity, would we consent to change our principles in the face of the admonition in “Cutting Sandalwood”? In achievement and reputation, we fear the shame evoked by the “pelican wetting its wings.” Brewing the Classics and drinking deeply of the histories, how dare we neglect the sources of our learning? In ordering government and administering the realm, we pledge ourselves even unto death.
We humbly wish that songs of brilliance may ever resound in the dawn of Shun; that the celestial pivot and transverse jade tube may turn forever under the august rule of Yao; and that, matching Earth and matching Heaven, Your Majesty may encompass all through the accomplishments and transforming influence of perfect sincerity…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
九圍則殷人所以頌湯也曰宣哲惟人文
武惟后曰執競武王無競維烈則周公所
以美文武也夫其靈承帝事肇修人紀地
平天成萬世允賴俾三代盛隆昭揭日月
獨以詩書之載粲焉可睹也使萬世之下
歷選哲辟攷德論世煥在方冊猗乎盛矣
繇是以降神母夜號漢高崛起而史有寬
仁大度規模宏遠之稱信乎其為天授也
霍精晝謁唐宗肇業而史有比跡湯武庶
===
幾成康之稱蓋卓乎其不可及也神木兆
符日光啓運而藝祖聿興至其曰神武不
殺君道偉然其亦近於知言矣然漢之雜
霸唐之雜夷宋之卒於仁厚而不競也蓋
其侈詞則有之矣其可與二帝三王同日
語邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝體
神聖之上資握
天人之合贊奮起淮甸仗一劍以盪定羣雄掃
punctuated:
九圍，則殷人所以頌湯也。曰「宣哲惟人，文武惟后」，曰「執競武王，無競維烈」，則周公所以美文武也。夫其靈承帝事，肇修人紀，地平天成，萬世允賴，俾三代盛隆昭揭日月，獨以詩書之載粲焉可睹也。使萬世之下，歷選哲辟，攷德論世，煥在方冊，猗乎盛矣！
繇是以降，神母夜號，漢高崛起，而史有「寬仁大度，規模宏遠」之稱，信乎其為天授也。霍精晝謁，唐宗肇業，而史有「比跡湯武，庶幾成康」之稱，蓋卓乎其不可及也。神木兆符，日光啓運，而藝祖聿興。至其曰「神武不殺，君道偉然」，其亦近於知言矣。然漢之雜霸，唐之雜夷，宋之卒於仁厚而不競也，蓋其侈詞則有之矣，其可與二帝三王同日語邪？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，體神聖之上資，握天人之合贊，奮起淮甸，仗一劍以盪定羣雄，掃
translation_en:
…the nine regions: this was how the people of Yin praised Tang. The words, “Discerning and wise was the man; cultured and martial was the sovereign,” and “Mighty was King Wu; unmatched were his achievements,” were how the Duke of Zhou extolled Kings Wen and Wu. They reverently undertook the work of the Lord on High and first established the ordering of human relationships; the earth was brought into order and Heaven’s work accomplished, providing a sure foundation for all subsequent ages. The flourishing grandeur of the Three Dynasties thus shone as conspicuously as the sun and moon, yet it is only through the records of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents that it can be clearly seen. These allow people ten thousand generations later to survey the wise sovereigns in succession, examine their virtue, and assess their times, all brilliantly preserved in written volumes. Ah, how magnificent!
Thereafter, a divine mother cried out at night, and Gaozu of Han rose to power. The histories praise him as “generous and humane, magnanimous in disposition, with plans grand and far-reaching.” Truly, his authority was bestowed by Heaven. The spirit of Huo paid a visit in daylight [?], and Taizong of Tang established his enterprise. The histories praise him as “matching the deeds of Tang and Wu, and approaching Cheng and Kang.” Indeed, his eminence was beyond reach. A numinous tree foretold an auspicious sign, and sunlight inaugurated the dynastic fortune; then the founding emperor of Song arose. As for the words, “Divinely martial yet not given to killing, magnificent in the way of a ruler,” these too come close to a discerning judgment. Yet Han mingled its rule with the methods of hegemons, Tang mingled its rule with foreign ways, and Song ultimately proved humane and generous but lacking in strength. Extravagant praise there certainly has been, but can they be spoken of in the same breath as the Two Emperors and Three Kings?
We profoundly reflect that our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, possessed the supreme endowments of divine sagacity and commanded the combined support of Heaven and humankind. Rising in the Huai region, he relied on a single sword to subdue the contending warlords and sweep…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
濯函區歷一紀而隆成
帝業拯生人之塗炭還獫虜於漠荒星珠月璧
功格乾樞滄海崑崙仁漸坤軸自古功德
之隆未有臻於茲理者故其當時若
大誥三篇
祖訓一錄傳於父老家喻戶曉而超黃邁唐越
商踰夏見於劉基
方丘之頌
文武神聖功高千古見於王景平雲南之頌其
===
它諸臣蓋未易以更縷數也而惟宋濂
日曆之序六者執事以為得其精要誠是矣
一曰功高萬古二曰得國之正三曰獨稟
全智四曰敬天勤民五曰家法之嚴六曰
兵政有統此其與堯舜禹湯文武之盛德
大業曠世而同經眞足以凌耀古初而燕
休統緒矣然愚嘗莊誦而伏思之竊以兵
政有統懲藩鎭之不掉家法之嚴戒戚寺
之預政敬天勤民窺
punctuated: 濯函區，歷一紀而隆成帝業，拯生人之塗炭，還獫虜於漠荒。星珠月璧，功格乾樞；滄海崑崙，仁漸坤軸。自古功德之隆，未有臻於茲理者。故其當時，若《大誥》三篇、《祖訓》一錄，傳於父老，家喻戶曉。而「超黃邁唐，越商踰夏」，見於劉基《方丘之頌》；「文武神聖，功高千古」，見於王景《平雲南之頌》。其它諸臣，蓋未易以更縷數也。而惟宋濂《日曆》之序六者，執事以為得其精要，誠是矣。一曰功高萬古，二曰得國之正，三曰獨稟全智，四曰敬天勤民，五曰家法之嚴，六曰兵政有統。此其與堯舜禹湯文武之盛德大業，曠世而同經，眞足以凌耀古初而燕休統緒矣。然愚嘗莊誦而伏思之，竊以兵政有統，懲藩鎭之不掉；家法之嚴，戒戚寺之預政；敬天勤民，窺
translation_en: …cleansed the realm and, over a twelve-year cycle, brought his imperial enterprise to magnificent completion. He rescued the people from utter misery and drove the northern foes back into the desert wastes. With stars as pearls and the moon as jade, his achievements reached the pivot of Heaven; like the vast sea and Mount Kunlun, his benevolence suffused the axis of Earth. Since antiquity, no grandeur of achievement and virtue had attained such a height [?]. Thus, in his own time, works such as the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements and the single compilation of the Ancestral Instructions circulated among the elders and became known in every household. The words “surpassing the Yellow Emperor and outstripping Tang Yao, exceeding Shang and transcending Xia” appear in Liu Ji’s Eulogy on the Square Altar; “accomplished in civil and military affairs, divine and sagely, his achievements surpass those of a thousand ages” appears in Wang Jing’s Eulogy on the Pacification of Yunnan. The other ministers’ writings cannot readily be enumerated one by one. As for the six points in Song Lian’s preface to the Daily Record, you consider them to have captured the essential substance, and rightly so. The first is achievement surpassing all antiquity; the second, the legitimacy of his acquisition of the realm; the third, his unique endowment with complete wisdom; the fourth, reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people; the fifth, the strictness of his dynastic household rules; and the sixth, unified command of military administration. In these respects, his flourishing virtue and great undertaking followed the same enduring principles as those of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, though separated from them by ages. They truly sufficed to outshine remote antiquity and bring peace and felicity to the dynastic succession. Yet I, in my ignorance, have solemnly recited these words and humbly pondered them. I venture to think that “unified command of military administration” addressed the danger of military governors becoming impossible to control; “the strictness of his dynastic household rules” guarded against imperial relatives and eunuchs interfering in government; and in “reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people,” we glimpse…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
仁敬之廣運獨稟全智仰
勇智之天錫則信然矣至於比漢高以爲得國
之正也統華夷以爲功高萬古也蓋亦宋
濂一時之言君子猶以爲有遺論焉蓋自
古創業之君唐因隋資宋襲周業獨漢起
自布衣此所謂爲高於川洿爲深於丘陵
者也蓋亦難矣我
太祖不階尺土起自徒歩雖似於漢而義旗四
指志在弔伐
===
命將勿殺之戒昭昭乎天地臨之也斯亦以暴
天吏於天下矣愚竊以應天順人跡比湯
武而功則過之也自古創業之君止以驅
除禍亂雖其戡定之猷混一之業施鴻名
而騰茂烈然其敵皆以吾中國也我
太祖訊掃腥羶再造區夏驅禽獸而秩之彝典
剗左衽而還之冠裳使晦冥日月穢濁天
地得以復其開闢照臨之常愚竊以誠生
民之未有雖擬之盤古立極不過也
punctuated:
仁敬之廣運，獨稟全智，仰勇智之天錫，則信然矣。至於比漢高以爲得國之正也，統華夷以爲功高萬古也，蓋亦宋濂一時之言，君子猶以爲有遺論焉。蓋自古創業之君，唐因隋資，宋襲周業，獨漢起自布衣，此所謂爲高於川洿、爲深於丘陵者也，蓋亦難矣。我太祖不階尺土，起自徒歩，雖似於漢，而義旗四指，志在弔伐。命將勿殺之戒，昭昭乎天地臨之也，斯亦以暴天吏於天下矣。愚竊以應天順人，跡比湯武，而功則過之也。
自古創業之君，止以驅除禍亂，雖其戡定之猷、混一之業，施鴻名而騰茂烈，然其敵皆以吾中國也。我太祖訊掃腥羶，再造區夏，驅禽獸而秩之彝典，剗左衽而還之冠裳，使晦冥日月、穢濁天地，得以復其開闢照臨之常。愚竊以誠生民之未有，雖擬之盤古立極，不過也。
translation_en:
…the far-reaching exercise of benevolence and reverence; and, in his uniquely possessing complete wisdom, we look up to his Heaven-bestowed courage and wisdom: these claims are indeed true. But as for comparing him with Gaozu of Han to establish the legitimacy of his acquisition of the realm, and citing his unification of the Chinese and the non-Chinese to proclaim his achievements supreme for all ages, these were, after all, statements made by Song Lian on a particular occasion. The gentleman still considers that something remains unsaid.
Among the founding rulers of antiquity, the Tang drew upon the resources of the Sui, and the Song inherited the enterprise of the Zhou. Only the founder of the Han rose from the common people. This is what is meant by building a height in low-lying riverlands and excavating a depth among hills: it is indeed difficult. Our Taizu rose on foot, without so much as a foot of territory to serve as his stepping-stone. Although in this he resembled the founder of the Han, wherever his righteous banners advanced, his purpose was to relieve the suffering and punish the guilty. His injunction to his generals against killing was manifestly clear, with Heaven and Earth looking down upon it. By this he made himself known throughout the realm as Heaven’s officer. In my humble view, in responding to Heaven and following the wishes of the people, his deeds equaled those of Tang and King Wu, while his achievements surpassed theirs.
Founding rulers since antiquity merely eliminated calamity and disorder. Though their plans for pacification and their achievements in unification spread their great names and exalted their glorious deeds, their adversaries were all within our own Central Lands. Our Taizu swiftly swept away [?] the rank and rancid presence of the aliens and rebuilt the Chinese realm. He drove out the beasts and ordered the land according to enduring institutions; he eradicated the practice of fastening robes on the left and restored proper caps and robes. Thus the darkened sun and moon and the polluted Heaven and Earth could recover their normal order of illumination, established at the beginning of creation. In my humble view, there truly had been nothing like this since humankind began. Even to compare him with Pangu’s establishment of the cosmic order would not be excessive.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
至德之廣運禮樂之重光際天所覆極地所載
咸蒙
厚澤與
聖祖之功德先後一揆者真足以對揚
駿惠而庻播
休靈矣况於珥筆執經之彥
帷幄論思之老必有以默窺
彌綸天地之機緘宏鋪
幽賛神明之猷績以震天下以幸萬世有非
===
愚草茅之所能窺其萬一也雖然愚聞之
帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心自古
及今未有外心而可以爲盛德大業者也
觀我
太祖造觀心亭
召學士宋濂曰人心虚靈乘氣機出入操而
存之爲難朕罔敢自暇自逸我
皇上御製敬一箴曰敬怠純駁應驗頓殊徵諸
天人如鼓發桴大哉
punctuated:
至德之廣運，禮樂之重光，際天所覆，極地所載，咸蒙厚澤，與聖祖之功德先後一揆者，真足以對揚駿惠，而庻播休靈矣。况於珥筆執經之彥、帷幄論思之老，必有以默窺彌綸天地之機緘，宏鋪幽賛神明之猷績，以震天下，以幸萬世，有非愚草茅之所能窺其萬一也。
雖然，愚聞之：帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。自古及今，未有外心而可以爲盛德大業者也。觀我太祖造觀心亭，召學士宋濂曰：「人心虚靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」我皇上御製《敬一箴》曰：「敬怠純駁，應驗頓殊。徵諸天人，如鼓發桴。」大哉！
translation_en:
…the far-reaching operation of consummate virtue and the renewed splendor of rites and music: all beneath the canopy of Heaven and throughout the lands borne by Earth receive this abundant bounty. These achievements and virtues accord with those of the sagely ancestor, earlier and later alike. They truly suffice to acknowledge and extol this great beneficence and, it is hoped, to spread its auspicious influence. How much more must those eminent men who wield the writing brush and uphold the Classics, and those venerable counselors who deliberate in the imperial presence, be able silently to discern the hidden workings that encompass Heaven and Earth, and amply to expound the plans and achievements that imperceptibly assist the divine powers! They thereby inspire awe throughout the realm and bring blessings to myriad generations. Of these things, I, an ignorant man of the countryside, cannot glimpse even a ten-thousandth part.
Nevertheless, I have heard that the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and their Way is rooted in the mind. From antiquity to the present, no one has ever achieved flourishing virtue and great undertakings apart from the mind. Consider how our Taizu built the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind and summoned Academician Song Lian, saying: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. Holding fast to it and preserving it is difficult. I dare not allow myself leisure or ease.” Our reigning emperor’s imperially composed Admonition on Reverence and Unity states: “Reverence and negligence, purity and admixture—their responses and manifestations differ utterly. Test this against Heaven and humanity: it is like a drum responding to a drumstick [?].” How great indeed! …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭劉批周子契易道之源固有以接
孔孟不傳之緖而屈子以忠愛之情契詩人之旨是亦未可以詞人視之
子能考究經旨深發二子之奧而末又以易詩之理求之吾心非見
道明而造詣深者不能道此繼屈周而下者子非楚之豪傑也邪
考試官敎諭姜批是深悟易詩之旨者
考試官敎授陸批究對詳悉
悟於易者深於易者也深於易者道與器
而已矣悟於詩者深於詩者也深於詩者
性與情而已矣昔者易之未作也非無易
===
也而易具於天地此道器之所繇形也詩
之未作也非無詩也而詩藏於天地此性
情之所繇出也是故易也者其天地有形
之畫乎聖人因而作之以通聖明之德以
類萬物之情先天下以開物後天下以成
務合四聖而歷三古闡造化而行鬼神而
易之道始章故曰易之爲書廣大悉備此
之謂也夫詩也者其天地自然之音乎聖
人因而刪之庶民歌之則以貢其俗君子
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭劉批：周子契易道之源，固有以接孔孟不傳之緖；而屈子以忠愛之情契詩人之旨，是亦未可以詞人視之。子能考究經旨，深發二子之奧，而末又以易詩之理求之吾心，非見道明而造詣深者不能道此。繼屈周而下者，子非楚之豪傑也邪？
考試官敎諭姜批：是深悟易詩之旨者。
考試官敎授陸批：究對詳悉。
悟於易者，深於易者也。深於易者，道與器而已矣。悟於詩者，深於詩者也。深於詩者，性與情而已矣。昔者易之未作也，非無易也，而易具於天地，此道器之所繇形也。詩之未作也，非無詩也，而詩藏於天地，此性情之所繇出也。是故易也者，其天地有形之畫乎？聖人因而作之，以通聖明之德，以類萬物之情，先天下以開物，後天下以成務，合四聖而歷三古，闡造化而行鬼神，而易之道始章。故曰：「易之爲書，廣大悉備。」此之謂也。夫詩也者，其天地自然之音乎？聖人因而刪之，庶民歌之則以貢其俗，君子
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Master Zhou grasped the source of the Way of the Changes and thus was indeed able to take up the thread of transmission from Confucius and Mencius that had been broken. Master Qu, through his feelings of loyalty and devoted concern, grasped the intent of the poets; he too cannot be regarded merely as a literary writer. You have investigated the meaning of the classics and profoundly elucidated the mysteries of these two masters. At the end, moreover, you seek the principles of the Changes and the Odes within our own hearts. Without a clear understanding of the Way and profound attainment, one could not say this. As a successor to Qu and Zhou, are you not an outstanding man of Chu?

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: This is someone who deeply comprehends the meaning of the Changes and the Odes.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: The examination of the subject and the response are detailed and thorough.

Those who comprehend the Changes are those who have penetrated deeply into it. What they penetrate in the Changes is simply the Way and concrete things. Those who comprehend the Odes are those who have penetrated deeply into it. What they penetrate in the Odes is simply human nature and feelings. In ancient times, before the Changes was composed, it was not that there were no Changes: the Changes was already fully present in Heaven and Earth. This is how the Way and concrete things took form. Before the Odes was composed, it was not that there were no Odes: the Odes lay hidden within Heaven and Earth. This is whence human nature and feelings emerged.

Thus, is not the Changes the visible delineation of Heaven and Earth? The sages composed it accordingly, to communicate sagely and luminous virtue and to classify the dispositions of the myriad things, going before all under Heaven to disclose things and following after all under Heaven to complete affairs. Bringing together the work of four sages across the three ages of antiquity, it elucidated the transformations of creation and gave effect to the workings of ghosts and spirits. Only then did the Way of the Changes become manifest. Hence the saying, “As a book, the Changes is vast and great, complete in every respect.” This is what it means.

Now, is not the Odes the spontaneous sound of Heaven and Earth? The sage accordingly selected and edited it. When ordinary people sing its poems, they thereby present their customs; gentlemen …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賦之則以見其志邪正之所感也美刺之
所生也扶三綱而明五常動萬物而察庶
彙而詩之用始大故曰興於詩又曰不學
詩無以言此之謂也是故易之爲道也天
道也故夫不悟於易者則其學不足以知
天詩之爲道人道也故夫不悟於詩者則
其學不足以知人嗟乎學不足以知人不
足以知天如是而有作焉者皆妄也執事
有感於吾楚之有屈原周子而以易詩爲
===
===
問愚也抱遺經而究終始或者有一得焉
何可不就正之執事之前也夫周子之崛
起南服也學匪繇於師傳心不假於智索
其爲太極也建圖著書根極道要窺陰陽
五行之本推四時萬物之變使學者知主
靜之可以立極探性命鬼神之奧闡仁誠
義利之辨使學者知聖學之可以上達要
其淵源精粹以上繼孔孟之絶緒自今觀
之其曰無極太極無方無體之旨也動靜
punctuated:
賦之則以見其志，邪正之所感也，美刺之所生也。扶三綱而明五常，動萬物而察庶彙，而詩之用始大。故曰：「興於詩。」又曰：「不學詩，無以言。」此之謂也。是故易之爲道也，天道也，故夫不悟於易者，則其學不足以知天；詩之爲道，人道也，故夫不悟於詩者，則其學不足以知人。嗟乎！學不足以知人，不足以知天，如是而有作焉者，皆妄也。
執事有感於吾楚之有屈原、周子，而以易、詩爲問。愚也抱遺經而究終始，或者有一得焉，何可不就正之執事之前也？夫周子之崛起南服也，學匪繇於師傳，心不假於智索。其爲太極也，建圖著書，根極道要，窺陰陽五行之本，推四時萬物之變，使學者知主靜之可以立極；探性命鬼神之奧，闡仁誠義利之辨，使學者知聖學之可以上達。要其淵源精粹，以上繼孔孟之絶緒。自今觀之，其曰「無極太極」，無方無體之旨也；動靜
translation_en:
…when gentlemen recite them, they thereby reveal their aspirations. Here are the responses stirred by the wayward and the upright; here arise praise and criticism. Upholding the Three Bonds and illuminating the Five Constant Virtues, stirring the myriad things and discerning their many kinds, the Poetry thus came to exercise its great influence. Hence the sayings, “Be inspired by the Poetry,” and “Unless you study the Poetry, you will have no means of speaking.” This is what they mean. Thus the Way of the Changes is the Way of Heaven: those who fail to comprehend the Changes lack the learning needed to understand Heaven. The Way of the Poetry is the human Way: those who fail to comprehend the Poetry lack the learning needed to understand humanity. Alas! If one’s learning is insufficient to understand humanity or Heaven, any writings one produces in such a state are all misguided.
You, sir, reflecting upon the fact that our region of Chu produced Qu Yuan and Master Zhou, have posed a question concerning the Changes and the Poetry. Foolish though I am, I cherish the surviving classics and investigate their beginnings and ends. Perhaps I have gained some insight; how could I fail to submit it to you for correction? When Master Zhou rose to prominence in the southern regions, his learning did not derive from a teacher’s transmission, nor did his mind depend upon intellectual searching. In his treatment of the Supreme Ultimate, he constructed a diagram and composed a text, probing to the roots of the essentials of the Way. He investigated the foundations of yin and yang and the Five Phases, and traced the transformations of the four seasons and the myriad things, enabling learners to understand that making stillness central allows them to establish the ultimate standard. He explored the mysteries of human nature, destiny, and spirits, and elucidated the distinctions concerning humaneness and sincerity, righteousness and profit, enabling learners to understand that the learning of the sages permits them to attain higher understanding. In its essentials, his teaching was profound in its sources and refined in its substance, continuing the broken line of transmission from Confucius and Mencius. Viewed from the present, his words “the Non-Ultimate and the Supreme Ultimate” convey the meaning of being without spatial bounds or physical form; movement and stillness…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
互根一陰一陽之道也誠通誠復繼善成
性之義也五氣順布元亨利貞之體也綱
領宏濶而渾成條理整嚴而縝密雖不規
規於易也而易之道由是以粲然于世此
非易之遺乎胡五峯以為其功蓋在孔孟
之間者此也若文中子之賛易楊雄之太
玄祗見其妄矣而陸子靜猶詆非吾儒宗
旨何邪蓋太極非有也自其至中至正者
而強名之也無極非無也自其無聲無臭
===
者而推本之也是故不言無極則太極之
體近於有物不言太極則無極之眞淪於
空寂其安能以為萬化之根柢乎子靜之
學不免於禪矣善乎北溪陳氏之言曰手
為圖筆為書而孔氏之傳復續然則易之
在楚也非以此邪屈原之為楚宗臣也嫉
上官之猜構遭聰聽之瞶亂其為離騷也
抒衷以寤主洗志於放言攄其忠君愛國
之誠心以寫其繾綣惻怛之情使人知吾
punctuated:
互根，一陰一陽之道也；誠通誠復，繼善成性之義也；五氣順布，元亨利貞之體也。綱領宏濶而渾成，條理整嚴而縝密，雖不規規於易也，而易之道由是以粲然于世，此非易之遺乎？胡五峯以為其功蓋在孔孟之間者，此也。若文中子之賛易、楊雄之太玄，祗見其妄矣。而陸子靜猶詆非吾儒宗旨，何邪？蓋太極非有也，自其至中至正者而強名之也；無極非無也，自其無聲無臭者而推本之也。是故不言無極，則太極之體近於有物；不言太極，則無極之眞淪於空寂。其安能以為萬化之根柢乎？子靜之學不免於禪矣。善乎北溪陳氏之言曰：「手為圖，筆為書，而孔氏之傳復續。」然則易之在楚也，非以此邪？
屈原之為楚宗臣也，嫉上官之猜構，遭聰聽之瞶亂。其為離騷也，抒衷以寤主，洗志於放言，攄其忠君愛國之誠心，以寫其繾綣惻怛之情，使人知吾
translation_en:
…their being rooted in one another expresses the Way of alternating yin and yang. Sincerity’s permeation and return express the meaning of continuing goodness and completing the nature. The orderly distribution of the five vital energies embodies origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy. His overarching principles are broad and form an integrated whole; their articulation is orderly, rigorous, and meticulous. Although he does not confine himself narrowly to the Book of Changes, through this work the Way of the Changes shines forth in the world. Is this not the legacy of the Changes? This is why Hu Wufeng judged his achievement to stand between those of Confucius and Mencius. By comparison, Wenzhongzi’s Praise of the Changes and Yang Xiong’s Supreme Mystery reveal only their authors’ presumption. Yet Lu Zijing still disparaged his teaching as contrary to the fundamental tenets of our Confucian tradition. Why?
The Supreme Ultimate is not an existent thing: this name is provisionally assigned to that which is supremely central and supremely correct. The Non-Ultimate is not nothingness: the term traces things to their source in that which has neither sound nor scent. Thus, without speaking of the Non-Ultimate, the substance of the Supreme Ultimate comes close to being treated as a thing; without speaking of the Supreme Ultimate, the reality of the Non-Ultimate sinks into emptiness and quiescence. How could it then serve as the root of the myriad transformations? Zijing’s learning cannot escape the influence of Chan Buddhism. Well said are the words of Chen Beixi: “With his hand he made the diagram, and with his brush he wrote the text, and the transmission of Confucius was continued once again.” Is this not, then, how the Changes has its place in Chu?
Qu Yuan, an eminent minister of Chu, abhorred Shangguan’s jealous intrigues and suffered when his ruler’s discerning hearing was deafened and confused. In composing Encountering Sorrow (Li Sao), he poured out his innermost feelings to awaken his lord and purified his aspirations through unrestrained expression. He laid bare his sincere loyalty to his ruler and love for his state, conveying his enduring attachment and deep anguish, so that others might understand that his own…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
身之無所逃而不流於怨出其篤古博物
之偉詞以極其跌宕激發之氣使知吾情
之有以自遏而不涉於怒文約而詞微志
潔而行廉要其清忠狷潔雖與日月爭光
可也自今觀之其曰耿介祗敬之旨則雅
頌之奧也猖狂顛隕之詞則規誦之音也
虯鳳芷艾之譬則比興之義也彭咸伯夷
之思則廉狷之行也稱文小而指極大取
類邇而見義遠命意託物取諸其心雖以
===
迫切忍死而終不忘乎君臣之大義此非
詩之遺者乎淮南謂其國風好色而不淫
小雅怨誹而不亂而以離騷可謂兼之者
此也文中子之續詩束晳之補亡祗見其
不知量矣而楊雄乃撫其文作反離騷自
崏山投諸江流以弔之何邪蓋屈原之過
過於忠者也屈原之忠忠之過者也故有
原之地而無其才則不可以語騷有原之
才而無其心則不能以知騷雄乃自取於
punctuated: 身之無所逃，而不流於怨；出其篤古博物之偉詞，以極其跌宕激發之氣，使知吾情之有以自遏，而不涉於怒。文約而詞微，志潔而行廉，要其清忠狷潔，雖與日月爭光可也。自今觀之，其曰耿介祗敬之旨，則雅頌之奧也；猖狂顛隕之詞，則規誦之音也；虯鳳芷艾之譬，則比興之義也；彭咸伯夷之思，則廉狷之行也。稱文小而指極大，取類邇而見義遠。命意託物，取諸其心，雖以迫切忍死，而終不忘乎君臣之大義，此非詩之遺者乎？淮南謂其《國風》好色而不淫，《小雅》怨誹而不亂，而以《離騷》可謂兼之者，此也。文中子之續詩、束晳之補亡，祗見其不知量矣。而楊雄乃撫其文，作《反離騷》，自崏山投諸江流以弔之，何邪？蓋屈原之過，過於忠者也；屈原之忠，忠之過者也。故有原之地而無其才，則不可以語騷；有原之才而無其心，則不能以知騷。雄乃自取於
translation_en: …that there is no escape for one's own person, yet without lapsing into resentment. He brings forth magnificent language steeped in antiquity and wide knowledge of things, giving full expression to his surging, impassioned spirit, and making others understand that his feelings have a means of restraining themselves, without crossing into anger. His writing is concise and his language subtle; his aspirations are pure and his conduct incorruptible. In sum, his unsullied loyalty and principled purity may indeed vie in radiance with the sun and moon. Viewed from our own day, his expressions of upright integrity and reverence embody the profound meaning of the Elegantiae and Hymns; his words of wild wandering and downfall carry the sound of admonitory recitation; his analogies of dragons and phoenixes, angelica and mugwort embody the principles of comparison and evocative imagery; and his longing for Peng Xian and Bo Yi exemplifies incorruptible, uncompromising conduct. The things named in his writing are small, but their import is exceedingly great; his comparisons draw on things close at hand, yet disclose far-reaching meanings. In shaping his meaning and entrusting it to things, he draws upon his own heart. Though driven to extremity and enduring death, he never forgets the great moral obligation between ruler and minister. Is this not a legacy of the Odes? This is why the Prince of Huainan says that the Airs of the States delight in beauty without becoming licentious, and the Lesser Elegantiae voice resentment and criticism without becoming rebellious, and that Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) may be said to combine both qualities. Wenzhongzi's continuation of the Odes and Shu Xi's supplementation of its lost poems merely show that they did not know their own limits. Yet Yang Xiong, following its text [?], composed a Refutation of Encountering Sorrow (Fan Li sao) and cast it into the river from Mount Min to lament Qu Yuan. Why was this? For Qu Yuan's fault was an excess of loyalty; Qu Yuan's loyalty was loyalty carried to excess. Thus, someone in Qu Yuan's circumstances but lacking his talent cannot discuss Encountering Sorrow; someone possessing his talent but lacking his heart cannot understand it. Yet Yang Xiong brought upon himself…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
投閣之辱豈龍蛇之謂乎善乎臨川吳氏
之言曰詩亡而後楚騷作然則謂詩之在
楚也非以此邪厥後程子因之有易傳之
作朱子因之有本義之作有太極通書之
註其所以發天人之奧洞性命之原究事
物之賾統倫理之全粹乎亡以復加也使
學者知吾心之爲至靈可以窮神知化知
吾性之爲至善可以爲堯舜周公孔子知
吾道之爲至大可以位育天地起往聖於
一綫覺來學於無窮故當時有再開渾淪
之語至於光風霽月玉色金聲之稱未爲
知周子者也朱子之作詩傳自謂可以無
遺憾至其離騷之解則曰不敢直以詞人
視之也夫推原之爲心雖其志行或過於
中庸辭藻或離於經訓然使忠臣孝子怨
妾逐婦不幸而處其變則不肯以其身之
所遭而自懈於善幸而或悟其非則有以
復其民彝天性之常而各止其所此其與
punctuated: 投閣之辱，豈龍蛇之謂乎？善乎，臨川吳氏之言曰：「詩亡而後楚騷作。」然則謂詩之在楚也，非以此邪？厥後程子因之有《易傳》之作，朱子因之有《本義》之作，有《太極》《通書》之註。其所以發天人之奧，洞性命之原，究事物之賾，統倫理之全，粹乎亡以復加也。使學者知吾心之爲至靈，可以窮神知化；知吾性之爲至善，可以爲堯舜周公孔子；知吾道之爲至大，可以位育天地。起往聖於一綫，覺來學於無窮，故當時有再開渾淪之語。至於光風霽月、玉色金聲之稱，未爲知周子者也。朱子之作《詩傳》，自謂可以無遺憾；至其《離騷》之解，則曰：「不敢直以詞人視之也。」夫推原之爲心，雖其志行或過於中庸，辭藻或離於經訓，然使忠臣孝子、怨妾逐婦不幸而處其變，則不肯以其身之所遭而自懈於善；幸而或悟其非，則有以復其民彝天性之常，而各止其所。此其與
translation_en:
…the disgrace of throwing himself from a pavilion: could this be what is meant by the dragon and the serpent [?]? Well said are the words of Master Wu of Linchuan: “Only after the Poetry disappeared did the Songs of Chu arise.” Is this not why one says that the Poetry survived in Chu? Thereafter Master Cheng, building upon this, composed his Commentary on the Changes; Master Zhu likewise composed the Original Meaning of the Changes and commentaries on the Supreme Ultimate and the Penetrating the Changes. These works disclose the mysteries of Heaven and humanity, penetrate the source of human nature and destiny, investigate the intricacies of affairs and things, and encompass the entirety of ethical relations. Their purity admits of no further addition.

They enable learners to know that our minds possess the utmost spiritual responsiveness and can therefore fathom the numinous and understand transformation; that our nature is supremely good and that we can therefore become like Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius; and that our Way is supremely great and can therefore bring Heaven and Earth into their proper places and nurture their workings. They revive the sages of the past through a transmission hanging by a single thread and awaken learners for endless generations to come. Thus people at the time spoke of “opening primordial unity anew.” As for such praises as “a clear breeze and a moon after rain” and “the lustre of jade and the resonance of metal,” these do not amount to understanding Master Zhou.

When Master Zhu composed his Commentary on the Poetry, he said that he could leave no regrets. But in his interpretation of Encountering Sorrow (Li sao), he said: “I dare not regard him simply as a literary man.” If we examine Qu Yuan’s underlying intentions, although his aspirations and conduct sometimes exceeded the mean, and his ornate language sometimes departed from the teachings of the classics, nevertheless, should loyal ministers, filial sons, resentful concubines, or repudiated wives unfortunately encounter such adversity, they would be unwilling to slacken in goodness because of what they themselves had suffered. If, fortunately, they should recognize their errors, they would have the means to recover the enduring norms of human relationships and their Heaven-given nature, each coming to rest in the proper place. In this respect, when compared with…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
易之吉凶悔吝詩之勸戒美刺也何以異
焉然則若原者其可以詞人視之乎雖然
易詩無二理性命同一源易之元吉即詩
之無邪也詩之和平即易之時中也誠能
易簡以一其心豈弟以平其志觀於井以
辨吾之義觀於巽以行吾之權本之國風
以達其情正之雅頌以要其極則易詩之
理吾心一以貫之無遺而易不在於四聖
詩不在於三百篇矣惜拘於象者不知剛
===
柔相推之義泥於數者不知進退離合之
神以文害辭者昧抑揚反覆之理以辭害
意者忘監戒懲勸之機此易詩之理所以
不得也故曰神而明之存乎其人又曰以
意逆志是為得之學易詩者固求之吾心
焉耳
第三問
魏裳
同考試官教諭阮 批 論著古人持身處事最為
punctuated:
《易》之吉凶悔吝、《詩》之勸戒美刺也，何以異焉？然則若原者，其可以詞人視之乎？雖然，《易》《詩》無二理，性命同一源。《易》之元吉，即《詩》之無邪也；《詩》之和平，即《易》之時中也。誠能易簡以一其心，豈弟以平其志，觀於井以辨吾之義，觀於巽以行吾之權，本之國風以達其情，正之雅頌以要其極，則《易》《詩》之理，吾心一以貫之無遺，而《易》不在於四聖，《詩》不在於三百篇矣。惜拘於象者，不知剛柔相推之義；泥於數者，不知進退離合之神；以文害辭者，昧抑揚反覆之理；以辭害意者，忘監戒懲勸之機。此《易》《詩》之理所以不得也。故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」又曰：「以意逆志。」是為得之。學《易》《詩》者，固求之吾心焉耳。
第三問
魏裳
同考試官教諭阮批：論著古人持身處事，最為
translation_en:
…how does this differ from the good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation of the Book of Changes, or the encouragement, admonition, praise, and censure of the Book of Odes? If so, can someone like Qu Yuan be regarded merely as a literary writer? Nevertheless, the Changes and the Odes have no separate principles; human nature and destiny share a single source. The “supreme good fortune” of the Changes is precisely the “absence of waywardness” of the Odes; the harmony and balance of the Odes are precisely the timely attainment of the mean in the Changes. If one can truly unify one’s mind through ease and simplicity, bring one’s purposes into balance through joyous gentleness, contemplate the Well hexagram to distinguish what is right for oneself, and contemplate the Gentle hexagram to exercise discretion; if one takes the Airs of the States as the basis for giving expression to one’s feelings and rectifies them through the Elegantiae and Hymns so as to attain their ultimate standard—then a single thread in one’s own mind will unite the principles of the Changes and the Odes, leaving nothing out. The Changes will no longer be confined to the four sages, nor the Odes to their three hundred poems.
Regrettably, those confined by images do not understand the meaning of the hard and soft impelling one another; those mired in numbers do not understand the subtle workings of advance and retreat, separation and union. Those who let individual words obscure the phrasing fail to grasp the principles of modulation and repeated expression; those who let phrasing obscure meaning forget the workings of warning, restraint, and encouragement. This is why they fail to apprehend the principles of the Changes and the Odes. Thus it is said: “Making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it rests with the person.” It is also said: “Use one’s understanding to apprehend the author’s intent.” This is what it means to grasp them. Those who study the Changes and the Odes must indeed seek them within their own minds, and that is all.
Third Question
Wei Shang

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也應世而病於激執其道以求勝固其心
之欲有為於天下而奮焉以必伸其志要
之非成務之學也非君子之所尚也是故
隱居求志行義達道時之謂也道隆身隆
道詘身詘道之謂也愚於執事之問而得
二人焉其漢之諸葛孔明宋之程伯子乎
愚請歷陳之而執事裁焉夫季子以耕野
而堅守延陵之節魯仲連以揮金而倂却
存趙之封高帝不能致采芝之四皓光皇
===
不能屈披裘之子陵執事固疑其隘矣乃
若子房建誅秦蹙項之謀孔明輔三分鼎
峙之業淵明班荆於柴桑康節乘車於河
洛比之四子則又不遠遁以為潔者矣要
之均以明志也蓋嘗論之季子矢子臧之
義懼父子之行私不可訓也况其周旋於
諸樊父子兄弟之閒其亦逆知釁端之必
起者乎才近伯夷美其節也淵明抒荆軻
之詠守君臣之大義不可逃也况其書甲
punctuated:
也。應世而病於激，執其道以求勝，固其心之欲有為於天下，而奮焉以必伸其志，要之非成務之學也，非君子之所尚也。是故隱居求志，行義達道，時之謂也；道隆身隆，道詘身詘，道之謂也。愚於執事之問而得二人焉，其漢之諸葛孔明、宋之程伯子乎？愚請歷陳之，而執事裁焉。
夫季子以耕野而堅守延陵之節，魯仲連以揮金而倂却存趙之封，高帝不能致采芝之四皓，光皇不能屈披裘之子陵，執事固疑其隘矣。乃若子房建誅秦蹙項之謀，孔明輔三分鼎峙之業，淵明班荆於柴桑，康節乘車於河洛，比之四子，則又不遠遁以為潔者矣。要之均以明志也。蓋嘗論之，季子矢子臧之義，懼父子之行私不可訓也。况其周旋於諸樊父子兄弟之閒，其亦逆知釁端之必起者乎？才近伯夷，美其節也。淵明抒荆軻之詠，守君臣之大義不可逃也。况其書甲
translation_en:
… In responding to the world, one may err through excessive vehemence, clinging to one’s Way in pursuit of victory. This certainly springs from a desire to accomplish something in the world and from a determined effort to fulfill one’s aspirations. Ultimately, however, it is not the learning that brings affairs to completion, nor is it what the gentleman esteems. Thus, dwelling in seclusion to pursue one’s aspirations, or practicing righteousness to make the Way prevail, is a matter of timeliness. When the Way flourishes, one advances; when the Way is constrained, one withdraws: this is a matter of the Way. In considering your question, I venture to identify two men: might they be Zhuge Kongming of the Han and Cheng Bozi of the Song? Allow me to set out my account, and leave the judgment to you.
Jizi tilled the countryside and steadfastly maintained his integrity at Yanling. Lu Zhonglian waved away gold and also rejected the enfeoffment offered for saving Zhao. Emperor Gao could not summon the Four Hoary Ones, who gathered mushrooms; Emperor Guangwu could not bend the will of Ziling, who wore a fur coat. You have, indeed, questioned whether their conduct was too narrow. Yet Zifang devised plans to overthrow Qin and crush Xiang; Kongming assisted in establishing the enterprise of three states standing like the legs of a tripod; Yuanming spread thorn branches to sit upon at Chaisang; and Kangjie rode in a carriage through the He–Luo region. Compared with the preceding four, these men did not seek purity by fleeing far from the world. Ultimately, all alike sought to manifest their aspirations. I have considered this: Jizi pledged himself to the righteousness exemplified by Zizang, fearing that private favoritism between father and son could not serve as a model. Moreover, as he moved among Zhufan and the fathers, sons, and brothers of that family, did he perhaps foresee that discord would inevitably arise? To say that his abilities approached those of Bo Yi is to praise his integrity. Yuanming expressed himself in his poem on Jing Ke, upholding the great moral obligation between ruler and subject, which could not be evaded. Moreover, his writing of jia …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
子於永初之後其可得而臣乎處士而繫
之晉褒其志也四皓之逃漢蓋畏高帝以
施其嫚罵之辱者歌唐虞之日遠其志甚
高而卒以遺其名然一出而漢鼎定豈膏
肓之錮哉子房之報韓蓋借漢以泄其博
浪之憤者棧道之燒其志不遂而卒以輔
成漢業然辟穀而不為漢留焉非止足之
志哉以懷仁輔義之子陵而不能得之光
武諫議之拜豈伊呂之志乎故不若桐江
===
之一絲猶足以九鼎於漢也以臥龍之孔
明而能得之於昭烈魚水之投况帝室之
胄乎故不若出而讎跨有荊益之言尚足
以興漢也仲連之輕世肆志非以為傲也
排難解紛得之談笑不謂其有經世之才
乎堯夫之與常秩同召非所以待高賢也
內聖外王之學聞於天下豈安樂先生之
志邪此愚之所謂以時權之者也安可以
為盡隘乎汲黯之嫉惡太甚李膺之持議
punctuated: 子於永初之後，其可得而臣乎？處士而繫之晉，褒其志也。四皓之逃漢，蓋畏高帝以施其嫚罵之辱者。歌唐虞之日遠，其志甚高，而卒以遺其名。然一出而漢鼎定，豈膏肓之錮哉？子房之報韓，蓋借漢以泄其博浪之憤者。棧道之燒，其志不遂，而卒以輔成漢業。然辟穀而不為漢留焉，非止足之志哉？以懷仁輔義之子陵，而不能得之光武諫議之拜，豈伊呂之志乎？故不若桐江之一絲，猶足以九鼎於漢也。以臥龍之孔明，而能得之於昭烈魚水之投，况帝室之胄乎？故不若出而讎跨有荊益之言，尚足以興漢也。仲連之輕世肆志，非以為傲也。排難解紛，得之談笑，不謂其有經世之才乎？堯夫之與常秩同召，非所以待高賢也。內聖外王之學，聞於天下，豈安樂先生之志邪？此愚之所謂以時權之者也，安可以為盡隘乎？汲黯之嫉惡太甚，李膺之持議
translation_en:
…his use of cyclical year designations after the beginning of the Yongchu era—could he possibly have been made a subject of the new dynasty? To identify him, a scholar in retirement, with the Jin was to commend his resolve. The Four Hoary Elders withdrew from the Han, presumably fearing the humiliation of Emperor Gao's insults and abuse. They sang of how distant the days of Tang Yao and Yu Shun had become; their aspirations were lofty indeed, and ultimately they left their names to posterity. Yet once they emerged, the Han's dynastic rule was secured. Could their withdrawal have been an incurable affliction?

Zifang's effort to avenge Han was, presumably, a matter of using the Han dynasty to vent the indignation behind his attempt at Bolang. When the plank road was burned, his original aim remained unfulfilled, and in the end he helped establish the Han dynasty. Yet he abstained from grain and would not remain in Han service: was this not the resolve of one who knew when to stop and be content? Ziling cherished benevolence and upheld righteousness, yet Guangwu could not secure his service by appointing him Grand Master of Remonstrance. Were his aspirations those of Yi Yin and Lü Shang? Thus, for him, nothing was better than a single fishing line on the Tong River: even this sufficed to give him the weight of the Nine Tripods in relation to the Han.

Kongming, the Crouching Dragon, could be won over through his affinity with Zhaolie, like that of fish and water; moreover, Zhaolie was a descendant of the imperial house. Thus, for Kongming, nothing was better than emerging to fulfill his proposal to hold both Jing and Yi, which might yet suffice to restore the Han. Zhonglian's disdain for worldly standing and free pursuit of his aspirations did not spring from arrogance. He resolved crises and settled disputes amid conversation and laughter: should we not say that he possessed the talent to put the world in order? Summoning Yaofu together with Chang Zhi was no way to treat an eminent worthy. His learning in inward sagehood and outward kingliness was renowned throughout the realm; but was this the aspiration of the Master of Peace and Joy [?]?

This is what I, in my humble judgment, mean by weighing conduct according to its times. How could all these men be deemed narrow-minded? Ji An's hatred of evil was excessive; Li Ying's insistence on his views…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
行不得則龍蛇迻何為者哉明道之不非
青苗獵較之意也廓然大公物來順應豈
其所謂尚氣者哉觀非一家私議之言安
石且為之愧屈爾矣佚之善處新法豈弟
之心也上不害法下不傷民豈其所謂泥
方者哉觀憂患太息之疏神宗且有文學
可用之喜矣此愚之所謂以道裁之者也
安可遂以為激乎夫事之所處有可否焉
時之所值有順逆焉勢之所處有難易焉
===
因其事以度其時因其時以察其勢因其
跡以原其心庶乎其得之矣雖然君子寧
病於隘不隘則必自卑以求幸其道而砥
柱之風衰寧病於激不激則必自貶以求
歡於時而殉國之志懈愚以是知諸賢之
未可以易議也然而君子安所取衷焉是
故非澹泊無以明志非寧靜無以致遠吾
得之孔明嗟乎此伊尹之志也純粹如精
金溫潤如良玉吾得之明道嗟乎此顏子
punctuated:
行不得，則龍蛇迻，何為者哉？明道之不非青苗，獵較之意也。廓然大公，物來順應，豈其所謂尚氣者哉？觀非一家私議之言，安石且為之愧屈爾矣。佚之善處新法，豈弟之心也。上不害法，下不傷民，豈其所謂泥方者哉？觀憂患太息之疏，神宗且有文學可用之喜矣。此愚之所謂以道裁之者也，安可遂以為激乎？夫事之所處有可否焉，時之所值有順逆焉，勢之所處有難易焉。因其事以度其時，因其時以察其勢，因其跡以原其心，庶乎其得之矣。
雖然，君子寧病於隘，不隘則必自卑以求幸其道，而砥柱之風衰；寧病於激，不激則必自貶以求歡於時，而殉國之志懈。愚以是知諸賢之未可以易議也。然而君子安所取衷焉？是故非澹泊無以明志，非寧靜無以致遠，吾得之孔明。嗟乎！此伊尹之志也。純粹如精金，溫潤如良玉，吾得之明道。嗟乎！此顏子
translation_en:
…When one cannot put one's principles into practice, one withdraws like a dragon or snake [?]; what purpose does this serve? Mingdao's refraining from condemning the Green Sprouts policy had the same intent as participation in the hunting contest. Openhearted and entirely impartial, responding fittingly to whatever arose—how could he be what they call headstrong? Consider his statement that this was no matter for one family's private deliberation: even Anshi was shamed into yielding by it. Yi's 佚 [?] skillful handling of the New Policies expressed a kindly and amiable heart. Above, he did not impair the laws; below, he did not injure the people. How could he be what they call rigidly attached to fixed rules? Consider his memorial expressing anxiety and deep sighs: even Shenzong rejoiced that his literary learning could be put to use. This is what I mean by judging matters according to the Way. How, then, can one simply deem it excessive? In dealing with affairs, some courses are acceptable and others are not; the times one encounters may be favorable or adverse; the circumstances in which one finds oneself may be difficult or easy. Assess the times in light of the affairs, examine the circumstances in light of the times, and trace the heart's intentions through outward conduct: then one may come close to a proper understanding.
Even so, a gentleman would rather err on the side of narrowness. Without such narrowness, he will inevitably lower himself to seek favor for his Way [?], and his steadfast bearing, like a pillar amid the current, will decline. He would rather err on the side of excessive zeal. Without such zeal, he will inevitably abase himself to win the approval of his age, and his resolve to sacrifice himself for the state will weaken. From this I know that these worthies cannot be judged lightly. Yet where should a gentleman find the proper balance? Thus, without freedom from worldly desires, one cannot clarify one's purpose; without tranquility, one cannot reach far. I find this in Kongming. Ah! This is the resolve of Yi Yin. Pure as refined gold, warm and lustrous as fine jade: I find this in Mingdao. Ah! This is Master Yan's…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而建茂功宣美績而播休聞而形於甘棠
之留滋乆而逾懷蓋曰此嘗以父母生全
我者如在其耳目且山川靈精賢喆間出
抒大雅之華振周行之譽垂道德之光揖
高風而起敬起慕則又曰是其出於兒童
里社之所跂足而希心者也而頡頏之志
油然以興故曰尚友之誼而士之本務也
夫子曰事其大夫之賢者友其士之仁者
況乎其已試之成績而前哲之遺休可睹
===
也以愚之不敏而仰承執事之問直為是
凛凛焉爾矣夫起於思而覈於名則誦說
易歡其志信於目而貴於耳則精神必奮
其衷蓋人情之所嗜而今昔之所同也何
也其投之者必入而其為心易受也執事
之為惠也蓋遠矣請以宦於楚者言之仲
山甫封樊者也抱柔嘉之德炳明哲之幾
不茹不吐以行其志立戲之諫料民之箴
卓卓乎有補袞之思焉其周之名臣與令
punctuated:
而建茂功，宣美績，而播休聞，而形於甘棠之留，滋乆而逾懷。蓋曰：「此嘗以父母生全我者。」如在其耳目。且山川靈精，賢喆間出，抒大雅之華，振周行之譽，垂道德之光。揖高風而起敬起慕，則又曰：「是其出於兒童里社之所跂足而希心者也。」而頡頏之志油然以興。故曰尚友之誼，而士之本務也。夫子曰：「事其大夫之賢者，友其士之仁者。」況乎其已試之成績，而前哲之遺休可睹也！以愚之不敏，而仰承執事之問，直為是凛凛焉爾矣。
夫起於思而覈於名，則誦說易歡其志；信於目而貴於耳，則精神必奮其衷。蓋人情之所嗜，而今昔之所同也。何也？其投之者必入，而其為心易受也。執事之為惠也，蓋遠矣！請以宦於楚者言之。仲山甫封樊者也，抱柔嘉之德，炳明哲之幾，不茹不吐，以行其志。立戲之諫，料民之箴，卓卓乎有補袞之思焉。其周之名臣與？令
translation_en:
…and established great achievements, displayed admirable accomplishments, and spread an excellent reputation. This found expression in the preservation of the sweet pear tree: the longer time passed, the more deeply they cherished his memory. They would say, “This was the man who once sustained and preserved us like a father and mother,” as though he remained before their eyes and within their hearing. Moreover, the spiritual essence of mountains and rivers brings forth worthy and wise men from time to time. They unfold the brilliance of the great odes, win renown in the ranks of service, and bequeath the radiance of moral virtue. Bowing before their lofty example, people feel respect and admiration arise and say, “Here is someone from the very village community of our childhood, toward whom we stretch on tiptoe and direct our aspirations.” The ambition to rival them then springs up spontaneously. Thus, forming friendships with the worthy of antiquity is a fundamental duty of a scholar. The Master said, “Serve the worthy among its grand masters, and befriend the humane among its scholars.” How much more so when their proven accomplishments and the excellent legacy of earlier worthies can still be seen! Unperceptive though I am, upon respectfully receiving your question, I can only feel profound awe at this.
When reflection is tested against reputation, recitation and discussion readily gladden one's aspirations; when something is confirmed by sight and esteemed through what one hears, one's spirit is sure to be stirred within. This is what human feelings delight in, the same in past and present. Why? What is presented to people in this way surely penetrates, and their hearts readily receive it. The benefit you confer is indeed far-reaching! Allow me to speak of those who served as officials in Chu. Zhong Shanfu was enfeoffed at Fan. He possessed gentle and excellent virtue and a luminous discernment of the subtleties of wisdom. Neither swallowing the weak nor spitting out the strong, he carried out his purpose. His remonstrance against installing Xi and his admonition against counting the populace conspicuously showed his concern to mend the royal robe—that is, to remedy his sovereign's failings. Was he not a renowned minister of the Zhou? Ling [the beginning of an incomplete word or title; ?] …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
豈獨以德政著邪韓愈祝融一登而雲爲
開霽正直之所動也百世之師誦美於蘇
軾此豈獨以文章名邪寇準道州之行憫
剛直之弗容也然而澶淵一役談笑却虜
而天下服其忠吾久不見寇準豈人君之
言哉歐陽脩夷陵之謫知政事之可以澤
物也卒而叅議大政以風節自持而天下
稱其賢如歐陽脩何處得來蓋亦見知於
明主矣凡此者皆遺澤之著于楚至于今
===
不衰也以産于楚者言之尹吉甫發物則
之詠廣文武之憲以輔成周宣中興之烈
可謂全才矣周子程子闡六經不傳之秘
接孔孟垂絶之緒使斯道粲然大明於世
可謂聖學矣黃香博學經典有天下無雙
之謠至孝之稱蓋有本之學也歐陽玄屢
典制語有卓然名世之譽廉平之政蓋有
用之才也蔣琬托志忠純負社稷之器休
休樂善人服其量司馬徽風致清雅有氷
punctuated:
豈獨以德政著邪？韓愈祝融一登，而雲爲開霽，正直之所動也。百世之師，誦美於蘇軾，此豈獨以文章名邪？寇準道州之行，憫剛直之弗容也。然而澶淵一役，談笑却虜，而天下服其忠。「吾久不見寇準」，豈人君之言哉？歐陽脩夷陵之謫，知政事之可以澤物也。卒而叅議大政，以風節自持，而天下稱其賢。「如歐陽脩何處得來」，蓋亦見知於明主矣。凡此者，皆遺澤之著于楚，至于今不衰也。
以産于楚者言之，尹吉甫發物則之詠，廣文武之憲，以輔成周宣中興之烈，可謂全才矣。周子、程子闡六經不傳之秘，接孔孟垂絶之緒，使斯道粲然大明於世，可謂聖學矣。黃香博學經典，有天下無雙之謠、至孝之稱，蓋有本之學也。歐陽玄屢典制語，有卓然名世之譽、廉平之政，蓋有用之才也。蔣琬托志忠純，負社稷之器，休休樂善，人服其量。司馬徽風致清雅，有氷
translation_en:
…Was it only for virtuous government that he was renowned? When Han Yu once ascended Zhurong Peak, the clouds parted and the sky cleared for him: such was the moving power of his uprightness. Su Shi praised him as a teacher for a hundred generations. Was he renowned only for his literary compositions? Kou Zhun’s journey to Daozhou evokes pity that his unbending uprightness could not be tolerated. Yet in the campaign at Chanyuan, he repelled the enemy amid easy conversation and laughter, and all under Heaven admired his loyalty. “I have not seen Kou Zhun for a long time”—how could these be the words of a ruler? [?] From Ouyang Xiu’s banishment to Yiling, we see how government can bestow benefits upon others. Ultimately he participated in deliberations on the great affairs of state, upheld his integrity, and was acclaimed throughout the realm for his worthiness. “Where could one find another like Ouyang Xiu?” Evidently he too won recognition from an enlightened sovereign. All these men left enduring benefits manifest in Chu, which remain undiminished to this day.
Turning to those born in Chu: Yin Jifu composed verses on the principles inherent in things and extended the exemplary institutions of Kings Wen and Wu, helping King Xuan of Zhou accomplish the great work of dynastic revival. He may indeed be called a man of comprehensive talents. Master Zhou and Master Cheng elucidated the hidden meanings of the Six Classics that had ceased to be transmitted, continuing the nearly severed tradition of Confucius and Mencius and making this Way shine brilliantly before the world. Their learning may indeed be called the learning of the sages. Huang Xiang was deeply versed in the classics; a popular verse celebrated him as “without equal under Heaven,” and he was renowned for utmost filial devotion. His was learning with firm foundations. Ouyang Xuan repeatedly took charge of drafting imperial pronouncements; he enjoyed an outstanding reputation in his age and governed with integrity and impartiality. His were talents of practical service. Jiang Wan set his purpose on loyalty and purity and possessed the capacity to sustain the state. Generous in spirit and delighting in goodness, he won admiration for his magnanimity. Sima Hui was refined and elegant in bearing, possessing an ice-like…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
起其詩曰赫赫炎炎云我無所君憂於上
以銷去之其詩曰上下奠瘞靡神不舉民
困於下生理無聊其詩曰周餘黎民靡有
孑遺愚竊以此適然之變而云無遺何邪
吾楚連歲大饑腴壤石田居掠其聚行遷
其次轉徙頓踣道殣相望裂地而薇殫涸
川而魚竭曩與吾居也其生也十室而五
曩與吾居也其徙也十室而七曩與吾居
也其鬻也十室而九宜執事之不忍聞也
===
向非
聖明善貸之仁諸司匍匐之惠蠲復不下帑藏
不發愚又不知其幾也乃知孑遺之歌斯
人生之至勤而振古之頌王道之大成也
是故荒政之策載在今昔諸司固已極力
拯援見諸施行況在今日則旣往之事也
聖德格天被于方內上錫順成之惠下起狉野
之懽是吾民更生之辰也民惟邦本本固
邦寧執事可以無慮矣然而曲突徙薪之
punctuated:
起。其詩曰：「赫赫炎炎，云我無所。」君憂於上，以銷去之。其詩曰：「上下奠瘞，靡神不舉。」民困於下，生理無聊。其詩曰：「周餘黎民，靡有孑遺。」愚竊以此適然之變，而云無遺，何邪？吾楚連歲大饑，腴壤石田，居掠其聚，行遷其次，轉徙頓踣，道殣相望。裂地而薇殫，涸川而魚竭。曩與吾居也，其生也十室而五；曩與吾居也，其徙也十室而七；曩與吾居也，其鬻也十室而九。宜執事之不忍聞也。
向非聖明善貸之仁、諸司匍匐之惠，蠲復不下，帑藏不發，愚又不知其幾也。乃知孑遺之歌，斯人生之至勤，而振古之頌，王道之大成也。是故荒政之策，載在今昔，諸司固已極力拯援，見諸施行。況在今日，則旣往之事也。聖德格天，被于方內，上錫順成之惠，下起狉野之懽，是吾民更生之辰也。民惟邦本，本固邦寧，執事可以無慮矣。然而曲突徙薪之
translation_en:
… arose. The poem says: “Blazing and scorching, I have nowhere to turn.” The ruler worried above, seeking to dispel it. The poem says: “Offerings were laid out and buried for those above and below; no spirit went without worship.” The people suffered below, with no means of sustaining their lives. The poem says: “Of Zhou’s remaining common people, not a single one is left.” I humbly wonder: if this was a chance calamity, why say that none remained? Our Chu has suffered great famine for successive years. Fertile soil has become barren ground; those who stay plunder accumulated stores, while those on the move shift their encampments [?]. Wandering and collapsing, they leave bodies of the starved along the roads within sight of one another. The earth is dug open until the edible ferns are exhausted; streams are drained until the fish are gone. Of those who formerly lived among us, only five households in ten survive; of those who formerly lived among us, seven households in ten have migrated; of those who formerly lived among us, nine households in ten have sold themselves. It is understandable that you cannot bear to hear of this.
Had it not been for the sagely sovereign’s benevolence in generously providing relief and the kindness of the various offices in hastening to our aid—had remissions and exemptions not been promulgated and treasury reserves not been released—I cannot know how many more would have suffered. Only then did I understand that the song of “not a single one left” expresses the utmost hardship of human life, while the praise of antiquity [?] expresses the great fulfillment of the Kingly Way. Thus, measures for famine relief are recorded in both ancient and modern times. The various offices have already exerted themselves to the utmost in rescue and relief, putting these measures into practice. Moreover, by now these are matters of the past. The sovereign’s sagely virtue reaches Heaven and extends throughout the realm. Above, Heaven bestows the blessing of a favorable harvest; below, rejoicing arises in the countryside. This is the hour of our people’s rebirth. The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is secure, the state is at peace. You may therefore be free of anxiety. Yet, as for bending the chimney and moving the firewood away to prevent a fire …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
思而執事每惓惓而爲之計斯仁智之用
心也古者三年之耕藏一年之積九年之
耕藏三年之積以三十年之通則雖以凶
旱水溢而不懼何也其備之者具也古者
詔萬民之食豐則人四鬴中則人三鬴儉
則人二鬴人不能二鬴則移以就穀而不
病何也其察之者周也繇此觀之則堯之
九年湯之七年豈有捐瘠之民乎傳曰田
野縣鄙財之本也垣窌倉廩財之末也百
===
姓時和事業得敘財之源也等賦府庫財
之流也故必謹養其和使天下必有餘而
上不患不足嗟乎執事窮原探本之問其
養和之說乎夫積逋淫禁未足爲憂也近
鬻遠竄未足爲憂也輕徭省刑未足爲憂
也貯粟平糴未足爲憂也豪强兼倂貪墨
爲虐未足爲憂也愚之過計竊以爲憂者
獨曰任人而已也不然則古人之成法儒
先之定論具在也任得其人則誚讓自囚
punctuated: 思，而執事每惓惓而爲之計，斯仁智之用心也。古者，三年之耕，藏一年之積；九年之耕，藏三年之積。以三十年之通，則雖以凶旱水溢而不懼。何也？其備之者具也。古者，詔萬民之食，豐則人四鬴，中則人三鬴，儉則人二鬴。人不能二鬴，則移以就穀而不病。何也？其察之者周也。繇此觀之，則堯之九年、湯之七年，豈有捐瘠之民乎？傳曰：「田野縣鄙，財之本也；垣窌倉廩，財之末也；百姓時和，事業得敘，財之源也；等賦府庫，財之流也。」故必謹養其和，使天下必有餘，而上不患不足。嗟乎！執事窮原探本之問，其養和之說乎？夫積逋淫禁，未足爲憂也；近鬻遠竄，未足爲憂也；輕徭省刑，未足爲憂也；貯粟平糴，未足爲憂也；豪强兼倂、貪墨爲虐，未足爲憂也。愚之過計，竊以爲憂者，獨曰任人而已也。不然，則古人之成法、儒先之定論具在也。任得其人，則誚讓自囚
translation_en: …such forethought, and you, honored sir, continually and earnestly devise plans for it: this is the concern of benevolence and wisdom. In antiquity, three years of cultivation provided a stored surplus sufficient for one year; nine years of cultivation provided a stored surplus sufficient for three years. With resources balanced over thirty years, even drought, crop failure, and flooding caused no fear. Why? Because preparations were complete. In antiquity, the people were instructed concerning their food allowances: in abundant years, four fu per person; in middling years, three fu; in lean years, two fu. When two fu per person could not be supplied, they were moved to places where grain was available and thus suffered no distress. Why? Because their circumstances were thoroughly examined. Viewed in this light, could there have been people abandoned to starvation during Yao’s nine years of flooding or Tang’s seven years of drought? A transmitted text says: “Fields and outlying settlements are the foundation of wealth; enclosed storage pits and granaries are its outer branches. When the common people live in seasonal harmony and their occupations proceed in due order, this is the source of wealth; graded taxation and government treasuries are its downstream flow.” Thus one must carefully nurture this harmony, ensuring that all under Heaven have a surplus, so that those above need not fear insufficiency. Ah! Does not your question, which searches out the source and probes the root, concern precisely this nurturing of harmony? Accumulated arrears and excessive prohibitions are not sufficient cause for concern; selling themselves nearby or fleeing afar is not sufficient cause for concern; lightening labor obligations and reducing punishments are not sufficient cause for concern; storing grain and purchasing it at fair prices are not sufficient cause for concern; annexation of holdings by powerful families and oppression by corrupt officials are not sufficient cause for concern. In my perhaps excessive deliberations, what I privately regard as the concern is solely the appointment of men. Otherwise, the established methods of the ancients and the settled judgments of earlier Confucian scholars are all there. If the right men are appointed, then reproach and self-imprisonment [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
上減其歲額而均以則壤成賦之法召民耕佃
比於屯田以補軍儲藩賦之不足則財用
不患于匱乏矣此萬世之利也朱子曰賑
饑無奇策不如講求水利非愚之私言也
剝膚之狂惟執事財擇焉
punctuated: 上減其歲額，而均以則壤成賦之法，召民耕佃，比於屯田，以補軍儲藩賦之不足，則財用不患于匱乏矣。此萬世之利也。朱子曰：「賑饑無奇策，不如講求水利。」非愚之私言也。剝膚之狂，惟執事財擇焉。
translation_en: …His Majesty should reduce its annual quota and apportion the levy equitably according to the method of assessing land and fixing taxes by soil quality, recruiting commoners to cultivate it as tenants, on the model of agricultural colonies, to make up shortfalls in military provisions and provincial revenues. There would then be no fear of inadequate funds and supplies. This would benefit all generations to come. Master Zhu said: “There is no ingenious strategy for famine relief; nothing is better than investigating and developing water management.” This is not merely my own foolish opinion. These rash words arise from distress that cuts to the skin; I ask only that you, sir, weigh them and adopt what you deem suitable.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
仰惟我
睿宗獻皇帝文德之純久洽民心
皇上龍興撫運覃敷文敎衡郢江
漢之區固
聖澤之所源委也是以一時賢士
莫不勇於趨化而奮庸共臣
===
之願率先寰宇旣增解額則
旌淑之途愈闢彙征之良益
繁彬彬乎思皇之譽焉嘉靖
丙午復當大薦監察御史高
節振德維風加愼厥典內外
諸司洎百執事咸與矢心恪
職和衷翼勵之誠視常爲烈
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

仰惟我睿宗獻皇帝，文德之純，久洽民心。皇上龍興撫運，覃敷文敎。衡郢江漢之區，固聖澤之所源委也。是以一時賢士，莫不勇於趨化，而奮庸共臣之願，率先寰宇。旣增解額，則旌淑之途愈闢，彙征之良益繁，彬彬乎思皇之譽焉。嘉靖丙午，復當大薦，監察御史高節振德維風，加愼厥典。內外諸司洎百執事，咸與矢心恪職，和衷翼勵之誠，視常爲烈。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

We reverently reflect that the pure civil virtue of our Emperor Ruizong Xian has long pervaded the hearts of the people. His Majesty rose like a dragon to assume the imperial mandate and spread civil instruction far and wide. The region of Heng and Ying, the Yangzi and the Han, is indeed where the imperial beneficence originates and flows. Thus all the worthy scholars of this age eagerly embrace its transforming influence, and their aspiration to exert their abilities in service as ministers [?] leads the realm. With the quota of provincial graduates increased, the avenue for recognizing the virtuous has opened still wider, and ever more worthy men advance together, winning praise as cultivated and admirable worthies.

In the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], the time again arrived for the great recommendation of scholars. Investigating Censor Gao Jie promoted virtue and upheld proper customs, exercising added care over this examination. The various offices within and outside the capital, together with all the officials concerned, pledged themselves to discharge their duties conscientiously. Their sincerity in working with one heart and diligently assisting one another surpassed the ordinary …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其爭相濯磨而起獻藝者夫
亦盛倍往昔矣精神意氣所
感非機之相為通者哉且聞
之楚歲不登阻饑告痏用以
上廑
帝念是年雨暘時若恒應雲霓之
望江漢底寧不虞濫溢之流
===
來牟受厥明黃茂遂以嘉鬯
康年之錫蓋共云希睹者也
而賓賢之典適維其期識者
知天道為不虛矣周始入境
見甿夫操銍艾羣集于稼濟
濟焉桎桎焉于是乎太和之
蒸得諸在野入鄂則巷謳達
punctuated: 其爭相濯磨而起獻藝者，夫亦盛倍往昔矣。精神意氣所感，非機之相為通者哉？且聞之，楚歲不登，阻饑告痏，用以上廑帝念。是年雨暘時若，恒應雲霓之望，江漢底寧，不虞濫溢之流。來牟受厥明，黃茂遂以嘉鬯，康年之錫，蓋共云希睹者也。而賓賢之典，適維其期，識者知天道為不虛矣。周始入境，見甿夫操銍艾，羣集于稼，濟濟焉，桎桎焉。于是乎太和之蒸，得諸在野。入鄂，則巷謳達
translation_en:
…Those who vied with one another in refining themselves and came forward to display their accomplishments were indeed twice as numerous as in former times. Was this not a mutual responsiveness, stirred by their spirit and resolve? Moreover, I heard that in Chu the harvest had failed: people suffered hunger and reported their distress, thereby troubling the Emperor with concern. This year, rain and sunshine came in due season, repeatedly answering the longing for rain clouds. The Jiang and Han rivers were tranquil, with no fear of overflowing waters. Wheat and barley received their blessing; the yellow, luxuriant grain flourished abundantly. All declared that the gift of such a bountiful year was seldom witnessed. The ceremony for honoring the worthy as guests happened to fall at just this time, and discerning men knew that the Way of Heaven was no empty notion.
When I, Zhou, first entered the territory, I saw farmers holding reaping sickles, gathered among the crops in great numbers and in orderly ranks [?]. Thus, among those in the fields, I perceived the flourishing of supreme harmony. Upon entering E, the songs in the lanes reached…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於觀風民依慊於司牧上下
承秉胥交爲慶于是乎太和
之合得諸在位旣入鎖院裒
諸士子之辭章俯而讀仰而
思雅麗殊則嚴腴因材則無
不冲融豐豫可以觀樂土之
華焉于是乎太和之發得諸
===
人文至其撤棘懸象賓筵醴
洽蓋所謂有飶其香邦家之
光者居然斯明徵也於戲休
哉善彰片言則星舍順軌明
揚介士則雲物垂祥况俊彥
旅升之會而其所以昭天地
闡性命者燦然具陳于前哉
punctuated:
於觀風，民依慊於司牧，上下承秉，胥交爲慶。于是乎太和之合得諸在位。旣入鎖院，裒諸士子之辭章，俯而讀，仰而思，雅麗殊則，嚴腴因材，則無不冲融豐豫，可以觀樂土之華焉。于是乎太和之發得諸人文。
至其撤棘懸象，賓筵醴洽，蓋所謂「有飶其香，邦家之光」者，居然斯明徵也。於戲，休哉！善彰片言，則星舍順軌；明揚介士，則雲物垂祥。况俊彥旅升之會，而其所以昭天地、闡性命者，燦然具陳于前哉！
translation_en:
… to the observer of local customs, while the people’s needs were satisfactorily met by their governors. Those above and below upheld their responsibilities and joined in mutual celebration. Thus, the concord of supreme harmony was to be found among those holding office. Once I had entered the examination compound under confinement, I gathered the candidates’ compositions, lowered my head to read, and raised it to reflect. Their elegance and beauty followed differing standards; their gravity and richness varied with their authors’ talents [?]. Yet all were harmonious, ample, and abundant, revealing the cultural flowering of this happy land. Thus, the expression of supreme harmony was to be found in literary culture.
When the thorn barriers were removed and the exemplars displayed [?], and sweet wine flowed freely at the banquet for the honored guests, here indeed was clear proof of the saying: “Fragrant is its aroma, a glory to the state.” Ah, how splendid! When goodness is made manifest in a single utterance, the stars in their lodges follow their proper courses; when upright scholars are conspicuously promoted, the clouds display auspicious signs. How much more so at this gathering where outstanding men advance together, and their writings, illuminating Heaven and Earth and elucidating human nature and destiny, are brilliantly arrayed before us!

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
譽主司亦與有望焉由是錄
成當
獻周循職事敬次言之以終其
義云
浙江處州府麗水縣儒學教
諭姜周謹序
punctuated:
譽，主司亦與有望焉。由是錄成當獻，周循職事，敬次言之，以終其義云。
浙江處州府麗水縣儒學教諭姜周謹序。
translation_en:
…praise; the presiding examiners, too, may hope to share in it. Thus, as this record is completed and ready for presentation, I, Zhou, in accordance with my official duties, have respectfully set down these remarks to bring its purport to a conclusion.
Preface respectfully written by Jiang Zhou, Instructor of the Confucian School of Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
我
國家以經學造士論其秀者而
顯庸之學古入官誦詩達政
其法蓋古也故奇傑豪儁鴻
博忠鯁清疆之士繇是以出
而元臣碩輔倚毗康濟彬彬
===
然施於
社稷域民楨國此其效焉自我
神祖
列聖以至我
皇上天運地漸文明太和之氣煥
乎流曜宇宙其治極其盛矣
我
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

我國家以經學造士，論其秀者而顯庸之。學古入官，誦詩達政，其法蓋古也。故奇傑豪儁、鴻博忠鯁、清疆之士繇是以出，而元臣碩輔，倚毗康濟，彬彬然施於社稷，域民楨國，此其效焉。自我神祖、列聖以至我皇上，天運地漸，文明太和之氣煥乎流曜宇宙，其治極其盛矣。我
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

Our dynasty cultivates scholars through the study of the Classics, assesses those who excel, and raises them to distinguished service. They study antiquity to enter office and recite the Odes to understand governance: these methods are indeed ancient. Thus emerge men of extraordinary talent and outstanding ability, extensive learning and loyal candor, purity and strength [?]. Great ministers and eminent counsellors, relied upon to secure peace and bring aid, bring their cultivated accomplishments to the service of the altars of soil and grain. They protect the people and serve as pillars of the state: such are the results of this system.

From our divine progenitor and successive sage sovereigns down to our reigning Emperor, Heaven has moved and Earth has been permeated; the vital force of cultural brilliance and supreme harmony shines resplendently throughout the universe. His governance has reached the height of flourishing. Our …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
主上履乾體正仁涵義洽道乆而
化成之靡不丕孚况三楚皆
在翼軫之分野
虹流
龍飛休祥濬發謀詒翼燕比之豐
芑起籲帝之思建共臣之業
罔不烝烝然思效其休譽寧
===
能從兩畿後邪乃今歲嘉靖
丙午四月監察御史高節奉
命來玆土按圖攷法去太去甚風
紀肅然無不改嚮諸司以秋
試期告乃聚謀曰是役也節
實監臨之其敢不慎於是稽
典肅幣官預其程守疆除館
punctuated:
主上履乾體正，仁涵義洽，道乆而化成之，靡不丕孚。况三楚皆在翼軫之分野，虹流龍飛，休祥濬發，謀詒翼燕，比之豐芑。起籲帝之思，建共臣之業，罔不烝烝然思效其休譽，寧能從兩畿後邪？
乃今歲嘉靖丙午四月，監察御史高節奉命來玆土，按圖攷法，去太去甚，風紀肅然，無不改嚮。諸司以秋試期告，乃聚謀曰：「是役也，節實監臨之，其敢不慎？」於是稽典肅幣，官預其程，守疆除館。
translation_en:
…Our sovereign follows Heaven and embodies rectitude; his benevolence embraces all, and his righteousness pervades everything. Through the enduring exercise of the Way, his transforming influence brings all to maturity, and none fails to respond with profound trust. Moreover, all the Three Chu regions lie within the terrestrial domains corresponding to the celestial lodges Yi and Zhen. A rainbow streams forth and a dragon takes flight: auspicious signs emerge in abundance. His plans bequeath protection and peace to his descendants, comparable to the luxuriant millet of the ode. All are moved to aspire to appeal to the emperor and to accomplish the work of reverent ministers [?]; all earnestly seek to emulate that glorious reputation. How could they lag behind the two metropolitan regions?
Now, in the fourth month of this year, the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], Investigating Censor Gao Jie came to this land by imperial command. He consulted maps and examined laws, eliminating excesses and abuses. Discipline became strict, and everyone amended his conduct. When the various offices reported the date of the autumn examination, he assembled them for deliberation and said: “For this undertaking, I, Jie, am indeed the Supervising Official. How could I dare to be anything but careful?” Thereupon, precedents were consulted and ceremonial gifts duly prepared; officials arranged the procedures in advance, secured the precincts, and cleared the examination quarters…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
工綜其役陳軌詰姦吏防其
怠崇雅黜浮士濯其志品式
物采錯綜咸戒而州等胥以
聘至乃以學正何〔梁〕敎諭楊
〔成〕周〔鼎〕劉〔三正〕林〔一清〕阮〔琳〕
包〔澤〕宋〔時〕分試之而屬州與
敎諭姜〔周〕使總其事曰學也
===
者以徵才也文也者以徵用
也匪是則否已於事而竣其
百執事自知府以下皆遴選
以充而以提調屬左布政使
菅〔懷理〕右參政鄒〔守愚〕監試
屬按察使孫〔應奎〕僉事卜〔大〕
〔同〕曰內其毋出乎精白一心
punctuated:
工綜其役；陳軌詰姦，吏防其怠；崇雅黜浮，士濯其志。品式物采，錯綜咸戒，而州等胥以聘至。乃以學正何〔梁〕、敎諭楊〔成〕、周〔鼎〕、劉〔三正〕、林〔一清〕、阮〔琳〕、包〔澤〕、宋〔時〕分試之，而屬州與敎諭姜〔周〕使總其事，曰：「學也者，以徵才也；文也者，以徵用也。匪是則否。」已於事而竣。
其百執事，自知府以下，皆遴選以充，而以提調屬左布政使菅〔懷理〕、右參政鄒〔守愚〕，監試屬按察使孫〔應奎〕、僉事卜〔大〕〔同〕，曰：「內其毋出乎，精白一心
translation_en:
…the workmen coordinated their tasks; regulations were set forth and wrongdoing investigated, so that the clerks guarded against negligence; refinement was promoted and superficiality rejected, so that the candidates purified their intentions. Standards, procedures, and material arrangements were coordinated, and all were duly admonished [?]. Zhou 州 and the others all arrived in response to invitations. School Instructor He Liang and the Instructors Yang Cheng, Zhou Ding, Liu Sanzheng, Lin Yiqing, Ruan Lin, Bao Ze, and Song Shi were then assigned to examine the candidates in separate groups, while Zhou and Instructor Jiang Zhou were charged with overall responsibility. They were told: “Learning serves to demonstrate talent; writing serves to demonstrate fitness for service. Whatever does not meet these aims is to be rejected.” Thus the arrangements were brought to completion [?].
All the functionaries, from prefects downward, were carefully selected for their assignments. The duties of Proctor were entrusted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Jian Huaili and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zou Shouyu; supervision of the examination was entrusted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Sun Yingkui and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Bu Datong. They were told: “Keep within and do not go out [?]; with minds wholly pure and single in purpose …”

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以稱
德意已於事而竣稽其均守辨其
旗物罔不祗愼而相與防範
之以屬右布政使劉寅左叅
政丁汝夔右叅政許琯右叅
議戴邦正張緒鄭有周張拱
文副使楊應奇陳仕賢潘九
===
齡公躋奎僉事米榮侯寧王
喬齡鄭汝舟都指揮劉遠鐵
冠李杲曰外其毋入乎聖厥
蠹萌明神其森已於事而竣
是時都御史巡撫姜儀振文
耀威邇遠服懷士志大興以
彌力於學撫治鄖陽先任維
punctuated:
以稱德意。已於事而竣，稽其均守，辨其旗物，罔不祗愼，而相與防範之，以屬右布政使劉寅、左叅政丁汝夔、右叅政許琯、右叅議戴邦正、張緒、鄭有周、張拱文，副使楊應奇、陳仕賢、潘九齡、公躋奎，僉事米榮、侯寧、王喬齡、鄭汝舟，都指揮劉遠、鐵冠、李杲，曰：「外其毋入乎！聖厥蠹萌，明神其森！」已於事而竣。
是時，都御史巡撫姜儀振文耀威，邇遠服懷，士志大興，以彌力於學。撫治鄖陽，先任維
translation_en:
…to accord with the imperial gracious intent. Once the business had been completed [?], their allotted guard duties were inspected and their banners and insignia distinguished. All acted with reverent care and jointly maintained precautions. These responsibilities were entrusted to Liu Yin, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Ding Rukui, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Xu Guan, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Dai Bangzheng, Zhang Xu, Zheng Youzhou, and Zhang Gongwen, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners; Yang Yingqi, Chen Shixian, Pan Jiuling, and Gong Jikui, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Mi Rong, Hou Ning, Wang Qiaoling, and Zheng Ruzhou, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Liu Yuan, Tie Guan, and Li Gao, Regional Military Commissioners. They were instructed: “Let nothing from outside enter! Discern the first stirrings of corruption [?]; the luminous spirits stand in solemn array!” Once the business had been completed [?].
At this time, Jiang Yi, Censor-in-chief serving as Grand Coordinator, promoted literary culture and displayed his authority. Those near and far submitted and cherished his rule; scholars’ aspirations rose greatly, and they applied themselves still more diligently to learning. As for the Grand Pacification of Yunyang, the former incumbent was Wei…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賢今葉照提督南贛先虞守
愚今顧遂寧宇不聳樹聲克
崇總兵豐城侯李熈爼豆臨
戎室家無恐故視昔加隆焉
比鎖院合提學副使今陞右
叅政辜嘉賓及副使楊勉學
所校士二千六百有奇三試
===
之御史節猶慮其不瀝衷殫
力也乃又合而誓之曰所不
與祓除其心以報
國者有如此哉於是諸事事大
用竦惕不懈彌虔拔其尤異
者九十人拜錄其文以
獻
punctuated:
賢，今葉照；提督南贛，先虞守愚，今顧遂，寧宇不聳，樹聲克崇。總兵豐城侯李熈，爼豆臨戎，室家無恐，故視昔加隆焉。
比鎖院，合提學副使今陞右叅政辜嘉賓及副使楊勉學所校士二千六百有奇，三試之。御史節猶慮其不瀝衷殫力也，乃又合而誓之曰：「所不與祓除其心以報國者，有如此哉！」於是諸事事，大用竦惕，不懈彌虔，拔其尤異者九十人，拜錄其文以獻。
translation_en:
…Xian, and now Ye Zhao; the Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan was formerly Yu Shouyu and is now Gu Sui. They kept their jurisdictions tranquil and undisturbed, establishing an increasingly distinguished reputation. The Regional Commander, Li Xi, Marquis of Fengcheng, brought the spirit of ritual propriety to military command, so that households had nothing to fear. Thus conditions flourished still more than before.
When the examination compound was sealed, more than 2,600 candidates were assembled who had been assessed by Gu Jiabin, Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, now promoted to Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right, and by Vice Commissioner Yang Mianxue. They were examined in three sessions. Censor Jie [?], still concerned that those responsible might not devote their whole hearts and exert their utmost strength, assembled them again and bound them by an oath: “Should anyone fail to join in cleansing his heart in order to repay the state, let this be his fate! [?]” Thereupon all those attending to their duties became deeply vigilant and apprehensive, unflagging and ever more earnest. They selected ninety outstanding candidates and respectfully transcribed their compositions for presentation.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
□也御史乃言曰於乎慎爾多士
夫篤培者天靈傑者地化成
者人夫明明赫赫厥類惟彰
自烈山氏之興也遐乎邈矣
天生
聖人起於南離我
皇上受圖錫紀遠邁前古而士類
===
之興雲蒸風從蓋其氣然也
詩曰天監有周昭假于下保
玆天子生仲山甫言乎天也
夫高而衡嶽環列者以萬數
淵而江漢迴繞者以千數洩
令德之珍鳩靈貢祉以效於
上猶恐其後也士望國紀厥惟在
punctuated:
□也。御史乃言曰：「於乎！慎爾多士！夫篤培者天，靈傑者地，化成者人。夫明明赫赫，厥類惟彰。自烈山氏之興也，遐乎邈矣！天生聖人，起於南離。我皇上受圖錫紀，遠邁前古，而士類之興，雲蒸風從，蓋其氣然也。
詩曰：『天監有周，昭假于下，保玆天子，生仲山甫。』言乎天也。夫高而衡嶽環列者以萬數，淵而江漢迴繞者以千數，洩令德之珍，鳩靈貢祉，以效於上，猶恐其後也。士望國紀，厥惟在
translation_en:
…[illegible] [?]. The Investigating Censor then said: “Ah! Be watchful, you many scholars! Heaven nurtures abundantly; earth supplies spiritual potency and outstanding talent; human beings bring transformation to completion. Bright and resplendent, those of this kind become manifest. How remote is the time when Lieshan first arose! Heaven brought forth a sage who rose in the south, the quarter of Li. Our Emperor received the chart of sovereignty and was granted the succession [?], far surpassing earlier ages. Scholars have risen like gathering clouds and followed like the wind: surely this is the working of that vital force.
The Book of Odes says: ‘Heaven watched over Zhou; its light reached down below. To protect this Son of Heaven, it brought forth Zhongshan Fu.’ This speaks of Heaven. As for the heights, the peaks arrayed around Mount Heng number in the tens of thousands; as for the depths, the waters winding about the Yangzi and Han rivers number in the thousands. They release their treasures of excellent virtue, gather spiritual potency, and offer blessings in service to the sovereign, fearful even then of falling behind. The hopes of scholars and the guiding principles of the state lie precisely in…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
兹詩曰思皇多士生此王國
王國克生維周之楨言乎地
也夫士以明義所以思奮庸
而熈帝載乃今爾多士濟濟
蹌蹌炳蔚相章抒經藝之指
而敷宏博之詞蓋將賛慮於
智廣業於仁要其卓卓可效
===
用者何以加焉可謂吉士也
已詩曰藹藹王多吉士維天
子使媚于天子又曰藹藹王
多吉人維天子命媚于庶人
言乎人也於乎愼爾多士州
不佞從而申言曰州聞之古
者以榮爲懼也是故能以懼
punctuated:
兹。《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。」言乎地也。夫士以明義，所以思奮庸而熈帝載。乃今爾多士濟濟蹌蹌，炳蔚相章，抒經藝之指，而敷宏博之詞，蓋將賛慮於智，廣業於仁。要其卓卓可效用者，何以加焉？可謂吉士也已。《詩》曰：「藹藹王多吉士，維天子使，媚于天子。」又曰：「藹藹王多吉人，維天子命，媚于庶人。」言乎人也。
於乎！愼爾多士！州不佞，從而申言曰：「州聞之，古者以榮爲懼也，是故能以懼
translation_en:
…here. The Book of Odes says: “Those illustrious many officers were born in this royal realm. The royal realm could bring them forth: they were the pillars of Zhou.” This speaks of the land. Scholars illuminate righteousness, thereby aspiring to exert themselves in service and bring lustre to the emperor’s undertakings. Now you many scholars, dignified and bearing yourselves with decorum, display brilliant literary accomplishments that enhance one another. You express the meaning of the classics and expound it in ample, learned language. Surely you will contribute to deliberations through wisdom and extend the work of government through benevolence. Considering your outstanding capacity for useful service, what could surpass it? You may indeed be called worthy officers. The Book of Odes says: “Numerous are the king’s many worthy officers; employed by the Son of Heaven, they are pleasing to the Son of Heaven.” It also says: “Numerous are the king’s many worthy men; commissioned by the Son of Heaven, they are pleasing to the common people.” This speaks of men.
Ah! Be watchful, you many scholars! I, Zhou, though untalented, would add these words of admonition: “I, Zhou, have heard that the ancients regarded honour with apprehension. Thus they were able to turn apprehension into…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
為榮爾多士敬哉無忘爾御
史之言〔州〕寔與有光耀也矧
曰其爾多士言以徵志文以
足言〔州〕睹其志矣如其貳焉
非〔州〕之所願於多士者也詩
曰庶幾夙夜以永終譽爾多
士愼諸是役也左參議戴〔嘉〕
===
〔猷〕副使魏〔尚純〕以入賀
萬壽行守備太監東□員外郎孫
〔續〕主事王〔景象〕劉〔愨〕行人姚
〔一元〕賀〔承光〕以有事玆土至
右參政楊〔本仁〕按察使林〔雲〕
〔同〕副使孫〔世祐〕以遷代去皆
嘗與於先事而樂觀其成者
punctuated:
為榮。爾多士敬哉！無忘爾御史之言，〔州〕寔與有光耀也，矧曰其爾多士！言以徵志，文以足言，〔州〕睹其志矣。如其貳焉，非〔州〕之所願於多士者也。《詩》曰：「庶幾夙夜，以永終譽。」爾多士愼諸！
是役也，左參議戴〔嘉猷〕、副使魏〔尚純〕以入賀萬壽行；守備太監東□、員外郎孫〔續〕、主事王〔景象〕、劉〔愨〕、行人姚〔一元〕、賀〔承光〕以有事玆土至；右參政楊〔本仁〕、按察使林〔雲〕〔同〕、副使孫〔世祐〕以遷代去，皆嘗與於先事而樂觀其成者。
translation_en:
…turn apprehension into honor. You scholars, be reverent! Do not forget the words of your censor. I, Zhou, truly share in the glory—how much more, then, do you scholars [?]! Words attest to one's aspirations, and literary composition gives full expression to one's words. I have seen your aspirations. Should you depart from them, that would not be what I wish for you scholars. The Book of Odes says: “May you strive morning and night, and thus preserve your good reputation to the end.” You scholars, take heed!
During this examination undertaking, Dai Jiayou, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, and Wei Shangchun, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, departed to attend the celebrations of the emperor's birthday. The eunuch defender Dong □, Vice Director Sun Xu, Secretaries Wang Jingxiang and Liu Que, and Messengers Yao Yiyuan and He Chengguang arrived on official business in this region. Yang Benren, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, Lin Yuntong, Surveillance Commissioner, and Sun Shiyou, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, departed upon transfer or replacement. All had participated in the preliminary arrangements and were pleased to see the undertaking brought to completion…

監試官：湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使孫應奎〔文宿，河南河南衛籍，直隸長洲縣人，辛巳進士〕。湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事卜大同〔吉夫，浙江秀水縣人，戊戌進士〕。

translation_en:
Huguang Provincial Examination, the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546).

Gao Jie, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Huguang. His courtesy name was Ruzhan; he was registered in Yongqing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of the Taicang Left Guard. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuxu year.

Zhou Ding, Instructor at the Confucian School of Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Minggong; he was a native of Neijiang County, Sichuan, and was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.
Liu Sanzheng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Shizhun; he was a native of Neijiang County, Sichuan, and was a tribute scholar of the gengzi year.
Lin Yiqing, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jixi County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Zishi; he was a native of Fuqing County, Fujian, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
