得而不興乎故曰帝天之命主於民心此其所
以久安長治而卜過其歷也歟
===
春秋
秋荆伐鄭 公會齊人宋人救鄭莊公二
十有八年
唐時舉
同考試官教諭劉 批 齊桓霸義此其最先且世道
所係也諸作率草草無所發明此作得之意高詞整佳士佳士
考試官教諭姜 批 謹嚴得體可取
考試官教授陸 批 得聖人扶翊世道之意
觀春秋所書深黜外夷之虐小而特美霸主之
punctuated:
以此以觀，則下有隆德，上有隆命，即視聽明威，而其幾可測也。周王其善於事天者矣！抑吾於是而知周之所以興也。觀於周禮，有削地絀爵、加地進律之制，蓋式序之說也；觀於箕子、太公，有洪範之陳、丹書之戒，蓋求懿德之說也。周王當時巡之日，而天敘、天秩、天命、天討之大法，一舉而皆得矣。祈天永命之要道，實在於此，周安得而不興乎？故曰，帝天之命主於民心，此其所以久安長治而卜過其歷也歟？

春秋

「秋，荆伐鄭。公會齊人、宋人救鄭。」莊公二十有八年。

唐時舉

同考試官教諭劉批：「齊桓霸義，此其最先，且世道所係也。諸作率草草，無所發明；此作得之，意高詞整。佳士！佳士！」

考試官教諭姜批：「謹嚴得體，可取。」

考試官教授陸批：「得聖人扶翊世道之意。」

觀春秋所書，深黜外夷之虐小，而特美霸主之
translation_en:
Viewed in this light, when there is abundant virtue below, there is a generous mandate above. Through Heaven’s seeing and hearing, its discernment and awe-inspiring power, the subtle workings of that mandate can be discerned. The king of Zhou was indeed skilled in serving Heaven! From this I also understand why Zhou rose to greatness. In the Rites of Zhou, we find provisions for reducing territories and lowering noble ranks, and for enlarging territories and advancing ranks [?]. These explain the principle of ordering all according to their proper stations. With Jizi and Taigong, we find the exposition of the Great Plan and the admonitions of the Cinnabar Writing: these explain the seeking of excellent virtue. When the king of Zhou undertook his periodic tours of inspection, the great principles of Heaven’s ordering of human relationships, its regulation of ceremonial distinctions, its conferral of mandates, and its punishment of wrongdoing were all realized in a single undertaking. Here truly lay the essential way to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate. How could Zhou fail to flourish? Thus it is said that the mandate of the Sovereign Heaven rests upon the people’s hearts. Was this not why Zhou enjoyed lasting peace and enduring good government, its duration exceeding the years foretold by divination?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, Jing attacked Zheng. The duke joined men of Qi and Song in coming to Zheng’s aid.” Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.

Tang Shiju

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Among Duke Huan of Qi’s righteous deeds as hegemon, this ranks foremost; moreover, the moral order of the world depended upon it. The other essays are generally perfunctory and shed no light on the matter. This essay grasps it: its conception is elevated and its language well ordered. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Careful, rigorous, and appropriate in form; worthy of selection.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Education official: “It grasps the sage’s intention of supporting and sustaining the moral order of the world.”

Looking at what the Spring and Autumn Annals records, we see that it sternly condemns the outside barbarians’ oppression of small states, while especially praising the hegemon’s …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
恤患也蓋虐小者犯義恤患者志仁春秋一奪
而一予之其為世道計也豈淺淺哉且荆為春
秋强國日以爭鄭為事蓋將握天下之樞闚周
室以兼制諸夏也至是荆成初立子元用事無
故以重兵伐鄭齊桓主霸會宋魯之師救之荆
遂遁焉夫内夏外夷天下之大限也以夷事夏
古今之大誼也荆恃其强不能周旋禮文以從
諸姬固已非矣又况於肆暴以猾夏邪以車六
百入鄭純門分布諸帥旆之殿之轘逵市刈人
===
民而溱洧之邦騷如也是不徒求從先君之志
且將以悅夫人之心不徒陵我懿親之邦實已
震及王畿之内是時中國有霸而敢横行如此
視之初敗蔡繼入蔡屬時之無霸與霸而未成
者其惡為益烈矣聖人以其犯義不祥不可長
也故特舉號以黜之焉然安夏攘夷霸者之大
業也以大字小天下之大經也桓主乎霸方將
攘斥兇醜以寧中國不但已也能忍於縱夷以
生患邪遂連宋魯申救鄭人遠播先聲以警以
punctuated: 恤患也。蓋虐小者犯義，恤患者志仁，春秋一奪而一予之，其為世道計也，豈淺淺哉？且荆為春秋强國，日以爭鄭為事，蓋將握天下之樞，闚周室，以兼制諸夏也。至是荆成初立，子元用事，無故以重兵伐鄭。齊桓主霸，會宋魯之師救之，荆遂遁焉。夫内夏外夷，天下之大限也；以夷事夏，古今之大誼也。荆恃其强，不能周旋禮文以從諸姬，固已非矣，又况於肆暴以猾夏邪？以車六百入鄭純門，分布諸帥，旆之、殿之，轘逵市，刈人民，而溱洧之邦騷如也。是不徒求從先君之志，且將以悅夫人之心；不徒陵我懿親之邦，實已震及王畿之内。是時中國有霸，而敢横行如此，視之初敗蔡、繼入蔡，屬時之無霸與霸而未成者，其惡為益烈矣。聖人以其犯義不祥，不可長也，故特舉號以黜之焉。然安夏攘夷，霸者之大業也；以大字小，天下之大經也。桓主乎霸，方將攘斥兇醜以寧中國，不但已也，能忍於縱夷以生患邪？遂連宋魯，申救鄭人，遠播先聲，以警以
translation_en:
…his relief of those in distress. For those who brutalize small states violate righteousness, while those who relieve distress set their minds on benevolence. The Spring and Autumn Annals censures the one and commends the other: could its concern for the moral order of the world be shallow? Jing was a powerful state during the Spring and Autumn period, constantly striving for control of Zheng. Its purpose was to grasp the pivot of the realm, eye the Zhou royal house, and thereby bring all the Xia states under its control. At this point, King Cheng of Jing had just ascended the throne, and Ziyuan held power. Without cause, he attacked Zheng with a large army. Duke Huan of Qi, acting as hegemon, joined the armies of Song and Lu to rescue it, whereupon Jing withdrew.

To treat the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders is the great boundary governing the realm; for the Yi to serve the Xia is the great principle of righteousness, past and present. Jing relied on its strength and failed to observe the forms of ritual in following the states of the Ji lineage. This was already wrong; how much worse to unleash violence and disrupt the Xia? With six hundred chariots it entered Zheng’s Chun Gate and deployed its commanders, setting up banners and stationing rear guards; it inflicted dismemberment in the thoroughfares and markets [?] and slaughtered the people, throwing the land of the Zhen and Wei rivers into turmoil. This was not merely an attempt to fulfill the former ruler’s ambition, but also to please his lady. It not only violated a state closely related to our royal house, but sent tremors into the royal domain itself. At a time when the central states had a hegemon, it dared act with such lawlessness. Compared with its earlier defeat of Cai and subsequent invasion of Cai, when there was either no hegemon or the hegemony was not yet established, its wickedness was all the more flagrant. The Sage judged that its violation of righteousness was inauspicious and must not be allowed to grow; he therefore singled it out by its designation to express condemnation.

Yet securing the Xia and repelling the Yi is the great undertaking of a hegemon; for the great to nurture the small is the cardinal principle of the realm. Duke Huan presided over the hegemony and was preparing to repel these vicious foes and bring peace to the central states, without stopping there [?]. Could he bear to let the Yi loose to cause calamity? He therefore allied with Song and Lu and extended aid to the people of Zheng, spreading word of his coming far ahead, to warn and to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
驅息虐燄起陷溺而蠻荆之氛廓如也是雖則
師不動乎大衆而已克遏桐丘之奔雖則澤僅
及乎一方而已發舒華夏之氣是時鄭急朝夕
而適相及如此較之狄伐邢楚伐黄坐視而不
救與救而無及者其業爲益勤矣聖人以其志
仁能愛終有賴也故特書救以美之焉觀於此
者可以明義可以體仁可以遏兵爭可以定分
守世道其永康矣抑此實齊桓所以匡天下之
首一舉義也自是而衣裳會兵車同九合諸侯
===
一匡天下王室視之以爲輕重者逾三十年皆
由先得乎鄭以執其樞而運衡南北也然則斯
舉也豈徒制伏一荆而已哉
晋侯伐鄭宣公十有四年
萬一貫
同考試官敎諭劉批鄭人所以背晋以其德之不
足且勢去也乃復恃力以逞非義矣此作發揮透徹宜錄以式
考試官敎諭姜批氣象嚴毅語意渾成佳作也
考試官敎授陸批聖人所以厚望晋伯意正如此
punctuated:
驅，息虐燄，起陷溺，而蠻荆之氛廓如也。是雖則師不動乎大衆，而已克遏桐丘之奔；雖則澤僅及乎一方，而已發舒華夏之氣。是時鄭急朝夕，而適相及如此，較之狄伐邢、楚伐黄，坐視而不救與救而無及者，其業爲益勤矣。聖人以其志仁能愛，終有賴也，故特書救以美之焉。觀於此者，可以明義，可以體仁，可以遏兵爭，可以定分守，世道其永康矣。抑此實齊桓所以匡天下之首一舉義也。自是而衣裳會，兵車同，九合諸侯，一匡天下，王室視之以爲輕重者逾三十年，皆由先得乎鄭，以執其樞而運衡南北也。然則斯舉也，豈徒制伏一荆而已哉？
晋侯伐鄭。宣公十有四年。
萬一貫
同考試官敎諭劉批：鄭人所以背晋，以其德之不足，且勢去也。乃復恃力以逞，非義矣。此作發揮透徹，宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭姜批：氣象嚴毅，語意渾成，佳作也。
考試官敎授陸批：聖人所以厚望晋伯，意正如此。
translation_en:
…to drive them away, extinguishing the flames of cruelty and raising up those engulfed in distress, until the threatening miasma of barbarian Jing was wholly cleared away. Although his army did not mobilize a great host, he had already checked the onrush at Tongqiu; although his beneficence reached only one region, he had already revived the spirit of Huaxia. At that time Zheng’s peril was imminent, and his intervention arrived just in time. Compared with occasions when the Di attacked Xing or Chu attacked Huang, and aid was withheld as others stood watching, or came too late, his undertaking showed all the greater diligence. The Sage considered that his purpose was humane and that he could care for others, so that he could ultimately be relied upon; he therefore specifically wrote “came to the rescue” to commend him. Those who contemplate this can understand righteousness, embody benevolence, restrain armed contention, and establish proper duties and responsibilities. The world might thereby enjoy lasting peace.
Indeed, this was Duke Huan of Qi’s first righteous undertaking in setting the world in order. Thereafter came assemblies in ceremonial robes and gatherings of war chariots: nine times he brought the feudal lords together, and he set the world in order. For more than thirty years, the royal house regarded his support as decisive for its standing. All this arose from first securing Zheng, thereby grasping the pivotal position and balancing north against south. Was this undertaking, then, merely a matter of subduing Jing alone?
“The Lord of Jin attacked Zheng.” Fourteenth year of Duke Xuan.
Wan Yiguan
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The people of Zheng turned their backs on Jin because its virtue was insufficient and its ascendancy was also slipping away. Yet it again relied on force to gratify its will: this was unrighteous. This composition expounds the matter thoroughly and should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Its bearing is stern and resolute, and its language and meaning form a seamless whole. An excellent composition.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: “This precisely expresses the Sage’s intention in holding such high expectations of Jin as hegemon.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
霸者虐小以復怨春秋所以譏之也蓋兵革之
於以服人末也晉侯不勝私忿而以兵加鄭焉
其未聞綏懷之大道矣乎且晉景伐鄭爲邲故
也景蓋忿鄭人背己而不念德附楚而甘即異
也故玆執言耳若然則鄭襄者罪之在也春秋
何以獨譏晉邪誠以霸者之於天下非離叛之
患而惟一德招徠之難非面從之求而必心悅
誠服之貴鄭非吾人邪其所以南附於楚亦啗
於小惠而逼於淫威耳景而思所以致之誠能
修德飭躬任賢立政使誼足以相懷而勢又足
以相庇鄭將棄楚如遺不俟加兵而自來矣何
乃知不出此德則不競而惟力是恃己實有闕
而惟人之求伐焉毒以兵也姑以紓報復之忿
蒐焉示以整也欲以爲脅服之資曾不思遺義
于楚莊使得討陳者何人邪顧可以責鄭之慕
義而甘心南向邪又不思失將於林父以致喪
師者何人邪寧可以責鄭之畏威而不敢北還
邪噫捍王于艱而榮膺錫命文侯所以服天下
punctuated: 霸者虐小以復怨，春秋所以譏之也。蓋兵革之於以服人，末也。晉侯不勝私忿，而以兵加鄭焉，其未聞綏懷之大道矣乎！且晉景伐鄭，爲邲故也。景蓋忿鄭人背己而不念德，附楚而甘即異也，故玆執言耳。若然，則鄭襄者罪之在也，春秋何以獨譏晉邪？誠以霸者之於天下，非離叛之患，而惟一德招徠之難；非面從之求，而必心悅誠服之貴。鄭非吾人邪？其所以南附於楚，亦啗於小惠而逼於淫威耳。景而思所以致之，誠能修德飭躬，任賢立政，使誼足以相懷，而勢又足以相庇，鄭將棄楚如遺，不俟加兵而自來矣。何乃知不出此，德則不競，而惟力是恃；己實有闕，而惟人之求？伐焉，毒以兵也，姑以紓報復之忿；蒐焉，示以整也，欲以爲脅服之資。曾不思遺義于楚莊，使得討陳者何人邪？顧可以責鄭之慕義而甘心南向邪？又不思失將於林父，以致喪師者何人邪？寧可以責鄭之畏威而不敢北還邪？噫！捍王于艱而榮膺錫命，文侯所以服天下
translation_en:
That a hegemon should oppress a small state to avenge a grievance is what the Spring and Autumn Annals censures. For armed force is the lowest means of securing others’ submission. The Marquis of Jin could not master his private anger and attacked Zheng with his troops. Had he never heard of the great Way of pacifying others and winning their allegiance?

Moreover, Duke Jing of Jin attacked Zheng because of Bi. Jing resented the people of Zheng for turning their backs on him without remembering his beneficence, attaching themselves to Chu, and willingly joining another allegiance. Hence he seized upon this as his justification. If so, then Duke Xiang of Zheng was at fault. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals censure Jin alone? In truth, for a hegemon dealing with the realm, the concern is not desertion and rebellion: the difficulty lies in attracting others through undivided virtue. Nor should he seek outward compliance: what he must prize is willing and sincere submission from the heart.

Were the people of Zheng not our own people? That they attached themselves southward to Chu was merely because they were enticed by petty favors and compelled by excessive force. Had Jing considered how to bring them back, sincerely cultivated his virtue and disciplined his conduct, employed worthy men and established sound government, making his righteousness sufficient to win their affection and his power sufficient to shelter them, Zheng would have cast Chu aside like something discarded. Without waiting for an armed attack, they would have come of their own accord.

Why, then, did his understanding fail to reach this? Unable to rival Chu in virtue, he relied solely on force; though the shortcomings were his own, he demanded everything of others. He attacked them, afflicting them with arms, merely to vent his vengeful anger. He held a military review, displaying his troops’ discipline, hoping to use it to intimidate them into submission. Did he never consider who had left the cause of righteousness to King Zhuang of Chu, allowing him to undertake the punitive expedition against Chen? Could he then blame Zheng for admiring righteousness and willingly turning southward? Nor did he consider who had erred in appointing Linfu as commander, thereby bringing about the army’s defeat. Could he blame Zheng for fearing that might and not daring to return to allegiance in the north?

Alas! Defending the king in adversity and receiving the honor of a royal investiture—this was how Marquis Wen secured the submission of the realm …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也釋宋之圍而光啓霸圖文公所以懷友邦也
景何爲者襲二祖之成業而墜二祖之休風不
競於楚莫致乎鄭祗見其疎焉已矣故春秋直
書晉侯伐鄭以譏之焉自是楚日益横陵逼駸
駸直至于蜀一盟同之者凡十有一國蓋俛而
南向者盡乎諸侯不特失一鄭人而已也厲公
之世鄭且依違以其失德猶夫景耳向非清明
如悼公者出以服鄭而駕楚晉之業亦云殆哉
噫此固賢君之足以光大人國家而藩屏乎天
===
下也
禮記
詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫肅肅敬也雝
雝和也夫敬以和何事不行
唐萬幾
同考試官教諭宋批就敬和處渾融詳悉體貼明
白千古作樂大旨無過於是者
考試官教諭姜批理明詞暢可錄
考試官教授陸批典實
punctuated:
也。釋宋之圍而光啓霸圖，文公所以懷友邦也。景何爲者？襲二祖之成業，而墜二祖之休風；不競於楚，莫致乎鄭，祗見其疎焉已矣。故《春秋》直書「晉侯伐鄭」以譏之焉。自是楚日益横，陵逼駸駸，直至于蜀一盟，同之者凡十有一國。蓋俛而南向者盡乎諸侯，不特失一鄭人而已也。厲公之世，鄭且依違，以其失德猶夫景耳。向非清明如悼公者出，以服鄭而駕楚，晉之業亦云殆哉！噫！此固賢君之足以光大人國家而藩屏乎天下也。
《禮記》
《詩》云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
唐萬幾
同考試官教諭宋批：就敬和處，渾融詳悉，體貼明白。千古作樂大旨，無過於是者。
考試官教諭姜批：理明詞暢，可錄。
考試官教授陸批：典實。
translation_en:
…such was his achievement. By lifting the siege of Song and gloriously inaugurating his hegemony, Duke Wen won the affection of friendly states. What sort of ruler was Duke Jing? He inherited the accomplishments of his two forebears but let their admirable example fall away. Unable to compete with Chu or win over Zheng, he merely revealed his ineptitude. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals directly records, “The Marquis of Jin attacked Zheng,” to censure him. Thereafter Chu grew more overbearing by the day, its encroachments and coercion advancing rapidly, until at the covenant at Shu fully eleven states joined it. Indeed, virtually all the feudal lords bowed their heads and turned south in submission: it was not merely the people of Zheng whom Jin had lost. In Duke Li’s time, Zheng still vacillated, for his failure in virtue was just like Duke Jing’s. Had a ruler as clear-sighted as Duke Dao not then arisen to bring Zheng into submission and gain ascendancy over Chu, Jin’s enterprise would surely have been in peril! Ah! This indeed shows how a worthy ruler can bring greatness and glory to a state and serve as a bulwark for all under Heaven.
Record of Rites
The Book of Odes says: “Solemn and harmonious, they sound together; the ancestors listen.” Solemnity means reverence; harmony means concord. With reverence and concord, what undertaking will not succeed?
Tang Wanji
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: In treating reverence and concord, the discussion is thoroughly integrated and detailed, its interpretation perceptive and clear. The enduring essential purpose of making music goes no further than this.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Clear reasoning and fluent expression; worthy of inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: Authoritative and substantial.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賢者引詩而釋之以見古樂之裕於用也夫敬
與和古樂備之矣其用之惡有不宜者乎子夏
旣言溺音之不善而祭祀不之用矣此則引周
頌之詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫所謂肅肅者
蓋言聲音節奏而極禮義度數之詳倫之不相
奪也統之不相淆也肅然以辨是故可以知敬
矣所謂雝雝者蓋言鏗鏘翕合而有優柔平中
之美廣大而不姦也會守而各叙也雝然克諧
是故可以知和矣夫敬不徒敬而有和以爲之
===
濟和不徒和而有敬以爲之節用之祭祀而先
祖且聽之矣况於事有不行乎哉吾知中聲發
越之下自啓乎衆妙之門德音流溢之餘默神
乎感通之用以之脩身則動正履和可以樂其
志而舉其道恊至善於克一也其行之何有於
悖邪以之爲家國天下則合敬同愛可以通其
情而定其分舉遠邇於大同也其施之何有于
拂邪夫古樂爲用之妙如此若夫溺音則其害
大矣豈但祭祀之不可用而已乎抑古樂之作
punctuated: 賢者引詩而釋之，以見古樂之裕於用也。夫敬與和，古樂備之矣，其用之惡有不宜者乎？子夏旣言溺音之不善，而祭祀不之用矣。此則引周頌之詩云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫所謂肅肅者，蓋言聲音節奏，而極禮義度數之詳，倫之不相奪也，統之不相淆也，肅然以辨，是故可以知敬矣。所謂雝雝者，蓋言鏗鏘翕合，而有優柔平中之美，廣大而不姦也，會守而各叙也，雝然克諧，是故可以知和矣。夫敬不徒敬，而有和以爲之濟；和不徒和，而有敬以爲之節。用之祭祀，而先祖且聽之矣，况於事有不行乎哉？吾知中聲發越之下，自啓乎衆妙之門；德音流溢之餘，默神乎感通之用。以之脩身，則動正履和，可以樂其志而舉其道，恊至善於克一也，其行之何有於悖邪？以之爲家國天下，則合敬同愛，可以通其情而定其分，舉遠邇於大同也，其施之何有于拂邪？夫古樂爲用之妙如此，若夫溺音，則其害大矣，豈但祭祀之不可用而已乎？抑古樂之作
translation_en:
The worthy quotes the Odes and explains them to show the ample efficacy of ancient music. Ancient music possesses both reverence and harmony: in what application could it be unsuitable? Zixia has already spoken of the harmful character of licentious music and of its exclusion from sacrifices. Here he quotes a poem from the Hymns of Zhou: “Solemn and harmonious, the sounds blend; the ancestors listen.” What is called solemnity refers to sounds and rhythms that fully embody the intricacies of ritual principles and prescribed measures. Their ordered relationships do not encroach upon one another, and their governing patterns do not become confused. They remain solemnly distinct: from this one can recognize reverence. What is called harmony refers to ringing tones blending together, possessing the beauty of gentle ease, balance, and moderation. They are expansive without becoming wayward; they converge and hold their places, each in due order [?]. They achieve harmonious concord: from this one can recognize harmony.

Reverence does not stand alone: harmony assists it. Harmony does not stand alone: reverence regulates it. When this music is used in sacrifices, even the ancestors listen. How, then, could any undertaking fail to succeed? I know that when balanced tones ring forth, they naturally open the gate to manifold wonders; as virtuous sounds flow abundantly, they silently bring a spiritual efficacy to the workings of sympathetic response and communion. Applied to cultivating oneself, this enables one to act uprightly and tread in harmony, to delight in one’s aspirations and carry out one’s Way, attaining accord with the highest good through singleness of purpose. How could practicing it involve any perversity? Applied to governing the family, the state, and all under Heaven, it unites people in reverence and shared affection, allowing their feelings to communicate and their proper stations to be established, bringing those far and near alike into great concord. How could its application encounter any obstruction? Such is the wondrous efficacy of ancient music. Licentious music, by contrast, causes great harm. Is its unsuitability for sacrifices the only objection to it? Furthermore, the creation of ancient music…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
本於聖人至德之光而協天地自然之和其始
也以吾身而推之家國天下其終也以天下而
樂之吾心焉蓋樂作於吾心而感於人心無二
理也君子於是而道古其所得者深矣魏文侯
聽之則惟恐臥何哉孔子曰樂則韶舞又曰放
鄭聲夫樂非外作者也必其得之也深則樂之
也篤惜夫文侯不足以語此
仁之為器重其為道遠舉者莫能勝也行
者莫能致也取數多者仁也夫勉於仁
===
者不亦難乎
胡伯涵
同考試官教諭宋批仁道至重至遠非全體不息
者不足以當之此篇說理明淨發揮無遺亦善作者
考試官教諭姜批讀其文字蓋究心於仁者
考試官教授陸批莊重不浮
聖人狀仁之道大而慨求仁者之難也夫仁非
全體不息者不足以當之也求之可以易言乎
哉此君子所以議道自己而置法以民也今夫
punctuated:
本於聖人至德之光，而協天地自然之和。其始也，以吾身而推之家國天下；其終也，以天下而樂之吾心焉。蓋樂作於吾心而感於人心，無二理也。君子於是而道古，其所得者深矣。魏文侯聽之，則惟恐臥，何哉？孔子曰：「樂則韶舞。」又曰：「放鄭聲。」夫樂非外作者也，必其得之也深，則樂之也篤。惜夫文侯不足以語此！

仁之為器重，其為道遠，舉者莫能勝也，行者莫能致也。取數多者，仁也。夫勉於仁者，不亦難乎？
胡伯涵

同考試官教諭宋批：仁道至重至遠，非全體不息者不足以當之。此篇說理明淨，發揮無遺，亦善作者。
考試官教諭姜批：讀其文字，蓋究心於仁者。
考試官教授陸批：莊重不浮。

聖人狀仁之道大，而慨求仁者之難也。夫仁，非全體不息者不足以當之也。求之可以易言乎哉？此君子所以議道自己而置法以民也。今夫
translation_en:
…is rooted in the radiance of the sage’s consummate virtue and accords with the spontaneous harmony of Heaven and Earth. At its beginning, one extends it from oneself to the family, state, and all under Heaven; at its culmination, one takes joy in one’s own heart through all under Heaven. Music arises in my heart and moves the hearts of others: there are not two different principles at work. Thus, when the gentleman speaks of antiquity, his understanding is profound. Why, then, did Marquis Wen of Wei, on hearing it, fear only that he would fall asleep? Confucius said, “For music, use the Shao dance,” and also, “Banish the sounds of Zheng.” Music is not something produced externally. Only when one’s understanding of it is deep will one’s delight in it be wholehearted. Alas, Marquis Wen was not capable of discussing this!

“As a burden, benevolence is heavy; as a way, it is long. Those who lift it cannot bear its weight; those who travel it cannot reach its end. What embraces the greatest number is benevolence. Is it not difficult, then, to exert oneself in benevolence?”
Hu Bohan

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “The way of benevolence is supremely weighty and far-reaching. Only someone who embodies it fully and practices it without cease can meet its demands. This essay expounds the principles clearly and lucidly, developing them without omission. Its author, too, is an accomplished writer.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Reading his writing, one sees that he has surely devoted his mind to benevolence.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: “Grave and dignified, without superficiality.”

The sage describes the greatness of the way of benevolence and laments the difficulty faced by those who seek it. Only someone who embodies benevolence fully and practices it without cease can meet its demands. Can seeking it be spoken of as easy? This is why the gentleman, in discussing the Way, begins with himself, but in establishing standards takes the people as his basis. Now, as for…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
立人之道有所謂仁焉妙天德之渾全而兼統
無外自夫人之所任言之其爲器莫重也配乾
行之至健而流通不禦自夫人之所行言之其
爲道至遠也惟其重也非莫舉之而鮮克勝焉
惟其遠也非莫行之而鮮克致焉是以隨所舉
之多寡而皆可以分量稱隨所至之遠近而皆
可以造就名仁之數如此勉仁者亦難乎其人
矣吾知渾然以具者由我而兼體之也一理未
純則於仁爲有虧充然自足者由我而操存之
===
也一息少懈則與仁不相似其必孜孜黽勉而
貞固足以爲負荷之基庶乎德性我用而無欲
好仁者爲可幾矣否則舉其偏而無以體其全
欲仁之克勝難矣哉拳拳服膺而强毅足以爲
致遠之地庶乎成性是存而中心安仁者可馴
至矣否則因其就而無以詣其極欲仁之我致
難矣哉仁之難成如此君子之以人望人也亦
有見於此歟雖然夫子論仁又曰仁遠乎哉我
欲仁斯仁至矣是皆人之所固有其機在我而
punctuated: 立人之道，有所謂仁焉，妙天德之渾全而兼統無外。自夫人之所任言之，其爲器莫重也；配乾行之至健而流通不禦。自夫人之所行言之，其爲道至遠也。惟其重也，非莫舉之，而鮮克勝焉；惟其遠也，非莫行之，而鮮克致焉。是以隨所舉之多寡，而皆可以分量稱；隨所至之遠近，而皆可以造就名。仁之數如此，勉仁者亦難乎其人矣。吾知渾然以具者，由我而兼體之也，一理未純，則於仁爲有虧；充然自足者，由我而操存之也，一息少懈，則與仁不相似。其必孜孜黽勉，而貞固足以爲負荷之基，庶乎德性我用，而無欲好仁者爲可幾矣。否則舉其偏而無以體其全，欲仁之克勝，難矣哉！拳拳服膺，而强毅足以爲致遠之地，庶乎成性是存，而中心安仁者可馴至矣。否則因其就而無以詣其極，欲仁之我致，難矣哉！仁之難成如此，君子之以人望人也，亦有見於此歟？雖然，夫子論仁又曰：「仁遠乎哉？我欲仁，斯仁至矣。」是皆人之所固有，其機在我而
translation_en:
…in the Way that establishes human beings, there is what is called benevolence. It embodies the wondrous wholeness of Heaven’s virtue and encompasses everything without exception. Viewed as a responsibility borne by human beings, nothing is weightier as a burden. It matches the supreme vigor of Heaven’s movement and flows unobstructed. Viewed as a path traveled by human beings, no Way reaches farther. Because it is weighty, it is not that no one lifts it, but that few can bear it fully; because it reaches far, it is not that no one travels it, but that few can reach its end. Thus, according to how much or how little people bear, each may be credited with a measure of attainment; according to how far they advance, each may be accorded a name for their achievement. Such are the dimensions of benevolence: a person who strives fully for it is indeed difficult to find.

I know that what is endowed in undivided completeness depends upon me to embody in its entirety. If even one principle remains impure, benevolence is impaired. What is abundantly sufficient in itself depends upon me to hold fast and preserve it. If I slacken for even a single breath, I cease to accord with benevolence. One must surely strive diligently and untiringly, with steadfastness firm enough to provide a foundation for bearing this burden. Then perhaps one’s moral nature may be brought into use, and the state of one who is free of selfish desires and loves benevolence may be approached. Otherwise, if one takes up only a part and cannot embody the whole, how difficult it is to bear benevolence fully! One must cherish it earnestly in one’s heart, with strength and resolution sufficient to provide a basis for reaching far. Then perhaps one’s fully realized nature may be preserved, and the state of one whose heart rests at ease in benevolence may gradually be attained. Otherwise, if one remains content with an existing achievement and cannot reach the utmost limit, how difficult it is to attain benevolence oneself! Such is the difficulty of fully achieving benevolence. When the gentleman expects others to fulfill their humanity, does he not also perceive this?

Yet, when discussing benevolence, the Master also said: “Is benevolence far away? If I desire benevolence, benevolence is here.” All this is inherent in human beings; the impulse that brings it into effect lies within me, and…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
無難也求仁之道奈何克已其要也强恕其近
也取譬其方也偏曲者純全之致近似者同歸
之途而强勉不已者下學之功學者觀夫子之
論仁合而求之吾心則於求仁之事思過半矣
第貳塲
論
君子有絜矩之道
蔡制
同考試官教諭楊批絜矩之道推之可以平治而
本之則在格致誠正此大學一書始終本旨士子作者類襲緒言而
多不顧傳義此論初讀似覺不甚過人反覆潛玩乃知順理說去而
大學一書包括殆盡平淡中自有餘味真程式之文也
考試官教諭姜批氣昌體正有根據有照應
考試官教授陸批文不務竒而理自足
===
君子所以致天下之治者無他焉亦惟其心之
公而已矣公則誠誠則天天無私也君子亦無
私也天無私公以體天下之物而已矣君子無
私公以感天下之心而已矣其始也知吾之心
punctuated:
無難也。求仁之道奈何？克已其要也，强恕其近也，取譬其方也，偏曲者純全之致，近似者同歸之途，而强勉不已者下學之功。學者觀夫子之論仁，合而求之吾心，則於求仁之事思過半矣。
第貳塲
論
君子有絜矩之道
蔡制
同考試官教諭楊批：絜矩之道，推之可以平治，而本之則在格致誠正，此《大學》一書始終本旨。士子作者類襲緒言，而多不顧傳義。此論初讀似覺不甚過人，反覆潛玩，乃知順理說去，而《大學》一書包括殆盡。平淡中自有餘味，真程式之文也。
考試官教諭姜批：氣昌體正，有根據，有照應。
考試官教授陸批：文不務竒，而理自足。
君子所以致天下之治者，無他焉，亦惟其心之公而已矣。公則誠，誠則天。天無私也，君子亦無私也。天無私，公以體天下之物而已矣；君子無私，公以感天下之心而已矣。其始也，知吾之心
translation_en:
…there is no difficulty. What, then, is the way to seek benevolence? Overcoming oneself is its essential requirement; striving to practice reciprocity is the nearest approach; drawing analogies from oneself is its method. For those who are partial and constrained, it leads to purity and completeness; for those who merely approximate it, it provides a path to the same destination. Unremitting effort constitutes the work of learning through everyday affairs. If students consider the Master's discussions of benevolence together and seek their meaning within their own hearts, they will have understood more than half of what seeking benevolence entails.
Second Session
Discourse
“The Gentleman Has the Way of the Measuring Square”
Cai Zhi 蔡制
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Extended outward, the way of the measuring square can bring peace and order; traced to its roots, it lies in investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the heart. This is the fundamental purport of the Great Learning from beginning to end. Candidates who compose essays generally repeat inherited sayings and often disregard the meaning of the commentary. On first reading, this discourse seems scarcely above the ordinary. Only after repeated, attentive consideration does one recognize that its exposition follows the principles naturally and encompasses almost the whole of the Great Learning. Its plainness holds a lingering savor: this is truly a model composition.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Its spirit is vigorous and its form correct; it has firm grounding and its parts correspond well with one another.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: The writing does not strive for novelty, yet its reasoning is fully adequate.
There is nothing else by which the gentleman brings order to all under Heaven: it is simply the impartiality of his heart. Impartiality brings sincerity; sincerity brings accord with Heaven. Heaven has no selfish partiality, and neither does the gentleman. Heaven is without selfish partiality: through its impartiality it simply embodies all things under Heaven. The gentleman is without selfish partiality: through his impartiality he simply moves the hearts of all under Heaven. At the outset, he knows that his own heart…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
即天下之心其既也以吾之心爲天下之心其
久也以天下之心而合于吾之一心天下各得
其所而治道成矣于此見心之爲大而君子之
不可及也然豈能有所加哉蓋心體本如是其
大而君子能不以私蔽之有以全其大耳是故
君子絜矩之道夫豈外于心乎蓋嘗觀之萬物
之生也造化以主之也造化所以主之者理也
造化以理生萬物而物固無有不齊者惟形氣
分而物感交而天下始於是紛擾膠雜而不得
===
其所矣豈不猶器物之在天下長短廣狹各殊
其體而所以賴匠者裁之制之以成其方也哉
方之理盡於矩故矩一設而物不能欺矣治之
理盡於心故心一公而天下之治無有不成者
則夫絜矩也者所以盡吾之心而成天下之治
固非智術之所能與也何也今夫自身而家有
内外不一自家而國有親疎不一自國而天下
有遠近不一君子以一人而統理之家欲我齊
國欲我治天下欲我平使用智則有時而窮任
punctuated: 即天下之心，其既也，以吾之心爲天下之心；其久也，以天下之心而合于吾之一心。天下各得其所，而治道成矣。于此見心之爲大，而君子之不可及也。然豈能有所加哉？蓋心體本如是其大，而君子能不以私蔽之，有以全其大耳。是故君子絜矩之道，夫豈外于心乎？蓋嘗觀之：萬物之生也，造化以主之也；造化所以主之者，理也。造化以理生萬物，而物固無有不齊者。惟形氣分，而物感交，而天下始於是紛擾膠雜，而不得其所矣。豈不猶器物之在天下，長短廣狹各殊其體，而所以賴匠者裁之制之，以成其方也哉？方之理盡於矩，故矩一設而物不能欺矣。治之理盡於心，故心一公而天下之治無有不成者。則夫絜矩也者，所以盡吾之心而成天下之治，固非智術之所能與也。何也？今夫自身而家，有内外不一；自家而國，有親疎不一；自國而天下，有遠近不一。君子以一人而統理之，家欲我齊，國欲我治，天下欲我平。使用智，則有時而窮；任
translation_en:
…is precisely the heart-mind of all under Heaven. Subsequently, he makes his own heart-mind the heart-mind of all under Heaven; with time, he brings the heart-minds of all under Heaven into accord with his own single heart-mind. Everyone under Heaven obtains their proper place, and the way of good government is accomplished. Here we see the greatness of the heart-mind and the gentleman’s unsurpassed attainment. Yet how could he add anything to it? The heart-mind in its fundamental constitution is inherently this great; the gentleman merely keeps selfishness from obscuring it and thereby preserves its greatness intact. Thus, could the gentleman’s way of “measuring with the square”—applying to others the measure one applies to oneself—lie outside the heart-mind?

Consider this: when the myriad things come into being, the creative transformations of Heaven and Earth govern them. What enables these transformations to govern them is principle. These transformations produce the myriad things according to principle, and inherently none is out of order. Only when physical forms and vital energies become differentiated, and the influences of things intermingle, does all under Heaven begin to become confused and entangled, so that things fail to find their proper places. Is this not like the implements of the world, whose forms differ in length and breadth, and which depend on craftsmen to cut and fashion them into the proper shape? The principle of squareness is fully embodied in the carpenter’s square; thus, once the square is applied, an object cannot conceal its irregularities. The principle of government is fully embodied in the heart-mind; thus, once the heart-mind is impartial, good government throughout all under Heaven cannot fail to be accomplished. “Measuring with the square,” then, is the means of fully realizing one’s heart-mind and accomplishing good government throughout all under Heaven. It is certainly beyond what cleverness and expedients can achieve.

Why is this? Extending from oneself to the family, there are distinctions between inner and outer; from the family to the state, distinctions between close and distant kin; from the state to all under Heaven, distinctions between far and near. The gentleman, as a single person, directs and orders them all. The family requires that I set it in order; the state requires that I govern it; all under Heaven requires that I bring it peace. If one employs cleverness, there will come a time when it is exhausted; if one relies on…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
法則有時而敝窮與敝吾未見其能治也是故
家國天下之不一者勢也而未始不一者心也
不一者分也而未始不一者理也君子心以會
理理以聯分分以維勢而天下之内外親疎遠
近固無有不合於一者大哉心乎冒天下之道
如斯而已乎何也人之一心體用具焉蘊之爲
孝弟慈性不同也而所以統之者心發之爲好
惡情不同也而所以統之者心推之爲理財爲
用人政不同也而所以統之者心心之在人本
===
公而無私也本誠而無僞也本天而非人也本
大而無外也自夫欲動情勝而公者私矣誠者
僞矣天者人矣大者有外矣性不能盡也情不
能正也政不能立也而智術以强之是本之則
無如之何言治邪君子知心統天下之大而天
下不異于吾心也于是乎求諸天焉非求諸天
也求諸心也非徒求諸心也求諸學也積學存
乎明德明德存乎修身格物也致知也所以啓
修之之端誠意也正心也所以踐修之之實是
punctuated: 法則有時而敝。窮與敝，吾未見其能治也。是故家國天下之不一者，勢也，而未始不一者，心也；不一者，分也，而未始不一者，理也。君子心以會理，理以聯分，分以維勢，而天下之内外親疎遠近，固無有不合於一者。大哉，心乎！冒天下之道，如斯而已乎！何也？人之一心，體用具焉。蘊之爲孝弟慈，性不同也，而所以統之者，心；發之爲好惡，情不同也，而所以統之者，心；推之爲理財、爲用人，政不同也，而所以統之者，心。心之在人，本公而無私也，本誠而無僞也，本天而非人也，本大而無外也。自夫欲動情勝，而公者私矣，誠者僞矣，天者人矣，大者有外矣。性不能盡也，情不能正也，政不能立也，而智術以强之，是本之則無如之何，言治邪？君子知心統天下之大，而天下不異于吾心也，于是乎求諸天焉。非求諸天也，求諸心也；非徒求諸心也，求諸學也。積學存乎明德，明德存乎修身。格物也，致知也，所以啓修之之端；誠意也，正心也，所以踐修之之實。是
translation_en: …methods, too, eventually become worn out. When resources are exhausted and methods worn out, I have never seen them bring about good government. Thus, what makes the family, state, and world diverse is their circumstances, while what has never ceased to unite them is the heart-mind. What makes them diverse is their distinct roles, while what has never ceased to unite them is principle. The gentleman uses the heart-mind to comprehend principle, principle to connect distinct roles, and those roles to hold circumstances together. Thus, within the world, inner and outer, close and distant kin, near and far are all united as one. Great indeed is the heart-mind! Is this not all that is required of the Way that encompasses the world? Why is this so? In a person's single heart-mind, both substance and function are complete. As it is held within, it constitutes filial devotion, respect for elder brothers, and parental kindness: these dispositions differ, but what unifies them is the heart-mind. As it issues forth, it constitutes likes and dislikes: these feelings differ, but what unifies them is the heart-mind. As it is extended into practice, it constitutes the management of wealth and the employment of people: these matters of government differ, but what unifies them is the heart-mind. In human beings, the heart-mind is originally impartial and without selfishness, sincere and without falsity, of Heaven rather than human contrivance, and so great that nothing lies outside it. Once desires stir and feelings prevail, however, impartiality becomes selfishness, sincerity becomes falsity, what is of Heaven becomes human contrivance, and what was all-embracing comes to exclude things. One can no longer fully realize one's nature, rectify one's feelings, or establish government. Yet one tries to force matters through clever techniques. If one can do nothing about this root, how can one speak of good government? The gentleman knows that the heart-mind unifies the vastness of the world and that the world is not separate from his own heart-mind. He therefore seeks the answer in Heaven. Yet he seeks it not in Heaven but in the heart-mind; and not merely in the heart-mind, but in learning. Accumulating learning rests upon making one's luminous virtue manifest; making luminous virtue manifest rests upon cultivating oneself. Investigating things and extending knowledge initiate this cultivation; making the intentions sincere and rectifying the heart-mind put it into actual practice. Thus …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
故察天地之變也通古今之宜也而物無不格
精義以入神也窮神以知化也而知無不致戒
自欺也求自慊也而意無不誠忿懥也恐懼也
好樂也憂患也而心無不正由是孝之于其親
焉弟之于其長焉慈之于其衆焉彞倫攸敘而
德無不明矣德無不明而心有不公乎公則誠
誠則天天之道所以體萬物而不遺也誠之道
所以感萬民而無外也君子體誠而至於是囿
囿天下於吾心也不難矣是故以此心而推之
===
家也則宜家人也宜兄弟也而孝弟慈行于家
矣以此心而推之國也則興仁也興讓也而孝
弟慈行于國矣以此心而推之天下也天下之
人此心同也此理同也天下有一不孝焉吾之
心弗盡也有一不弟焉吾之心弗盡也有一不
慈焉吾之心弗盡也是故因天下之不一者而
齊之以至一以吾心之至一者而感天下之所
同上下不同也其心同也所惡于上下者吾弗
施也前後不同也其心同也所惡于前後者吾
punctuated: 故察天地之變也，通古今之宜也，而物無不格；精義以入神也，窮神以知化也，而知無不致；戒自欺也，求自慊也，而意無不誠；忿懥也，恐懼也，好樂也，憂患也，而心無不正。由是孝之于其親焉，弟之于其長焉，慈之于其衆焉，彞倫攸敘，而德無不明矣。德無不明，而心有不公乎？公則誠，誠則天。天之道，所以體萬物而不遺也；誠之道，所以感萬民而無外也。君子體誠而至於是，囿囿天下於吾心也不難矣。是故以此心而推之家也，則宜家人也，宜兄弟也，而孝弟慈行于家矣；以此心而推之國也，則興仁也，興讓也，而孝弟慈行于國矣；以此心而推之天下也，天下之人，此心同也，此理同也。天下有一不孝焉，吾之心弗盡也；有一不弟焉，吾之心弗盡也；有一不慈焉，吾之心弗盡也。是故因天下之不一者而齊之以至一，以吾心之至一者而感天下之所同。上下不同也，其心同也，所惡于上下者，吾弗施也；前後不同也，其心同也，所惡于前後者，吾
translation_en:
…Thus, by examining the changes of Heaven and Earth and comprehending what is appropriate in ancient and modern times, one leaves no thing uninvestigated. By refining one’s understanding of principle to enter into the spiritual, and fathoming the spiritual to understand transformation, one brings knowledge to its fullest extent. By guarding against self-deception and seeking satisfaction within oneself, one makes one’s intentions wholly sincere. Amid anger, fear, delight, and anxiety, one keeps the mind wholly rectified. From this follow filial devotion toward one’s parents, deference toward one’s elders, and kindness toward the people. The enduring human relationships are duly ordered, and virtue is fully illuminated. When virtue is fully illuminated, can the mind be anything but impartial? Impartiality leads to sincerity, and sincerity to accord with Heaven. The Way of Heaven embodies all things without omitting any; the Way of sincerity moves all people without excluding any. When the gentleman embodies sincerity and reaches this point, encompassing [?] all under Heaven within his own mind is no difficult matter.

Thus, when this mind is extended to the family, it brings harmony among family members and among brothers, and filial devotion, deference, and kindness prevail within the family. When this mind is extended to the state, it inspires benevolence and yielding, and filial devotion, deference, and kindness prevail within the state. When this mind is extended to all under Heaven, all people share this same mind and this same principle. If there is a single person under Heaven who lacks filial devotion, my mind has not been fully realized; if a single person lacks deference to elders, my mind has not been fully realized; if a single person lacks kindness, my mind has not been fully realized. Thus, taking what is disparate under Heaven, one brings it into accord through perfect unity; through the perfect unity of one’s own mind, one moves what all under Heaven share. Those above and below differ in position, but their minds are the same: what I dislike in those above or below, I do not inflict upon others. Those before and behind differ in position, but their minds are the same: what I dislike in those before or behind, I…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
弗施也左右不同也其心同也所惡于左右者
吾弗施也猶未也財者人之所資以養也吾與
之聚焉生之衆也食之寡也爲之疾也用之舒
也而拂民以從欲者吾弗爲也賢才者人之所
賴以治也吾與之集焉休休有容者人之彦聖
者保我子孫黎民者見之必舉也舉之必先也
而娼嫉以妨賢者所必遠矣至是而君子之所
以感天下之心者無不至矣其卽矩以度物而
長短廣狹無不成于方矣是亦天之所以體物
===
而不遺也是故天下之人得于所感者莫不應
之以同觀于其心者莫不率其理之所有人人
親其親而天下莫不孝也長其長而天下莫不
弟也幼其幼而天下莫不慈也何有爭奪悖逆
者乎何有不好義終事者乎此之謂天下之治
而君子之所以不可及也然非君子有求于天
下也理本至順各順焉而已矣亦非天下有私
于君子也理本至足各足焉而已矣各順則君
子感天下而通所以感之者天也各足則天下
punctuated:
弗施也。左右不同也，其心同也，所惡于左右者，吾弗施也。猶未也。財者，人之所資以養也，吾與之聚焉。生之衆也，食之寡也，爲之疾也，用之舒也，而拂民以從欲者，吾弗爲也。賢才者，人之所賴以治也，吾與之集焉。休休有容者，人之彦聖者，保我子孫黎民者，見之必舉也，舉之必先也，而娼嫉以妨賢者，所必遠矣。至是而君子之所以感天下之心者，無不至矣。其卽矩以度物，而長短廣狹無不成于方矣。是亦天之所以體物而不遺也。
是故天下之人，得于所感者，莫不應之以同；觀于其心者，莫不率其理之所有。人人親其親，而天下莫不孝也；長其長，而天下莫不弟也；幼其幼，而天下莫不慈也。何有爭奪悖逆者乎？何有不好義終事者乎？此之謂天下之治，而君子之所以不可及也。然非君子有求于天下也，理本至順，各順焉而已矣；亦非天下有私于君子也，理本至足，各足焉而已矣。各順則君子感天下而通，所以感之者，天也；各足則天下
translation_en:
…I do not inflict it upon others. Those to the left and right occupy different positions, but their hearts are alike. What I dislike in those to my left or right, I do not inflict upon others. Yet this is not all. Wealth is what people depend upon for their sustenance; I gather it for them. Those who produce it are numerous, those who consume it few; production is swift, and expenditure restrained. I will not act against the people to indulge my desires. Worthy and talented men are those upon whom people depend for good government; I assemble them. Those who are generous and accommodating, those who possess outstanding talent and sagacity, and those who can safeguard my descendants and the common people—whenever I see them, I invariably promote them, and do so without delay. Those whose jealousy obstructs the worthy [?] must assuredly be kept at a distance. At this point, the gentleman has left nothing undone in moving the hearts of all under Heaven. It is as though he applies a carpenter’s square to measure things: whatever their length or breadth, all are brought into conformity with the square. This, too, is how Heaven gives substance to all things without omitting any.
Thus, among all under Heaven, none who receive his influence fail to respond in harmony; none who look into his heart fail to follow the principles inherent in it. Everyone cherishes their own parents, and none under Heaven fail to be filial; everyone honors their own elders, and none fail in fraternal deference; everyone cares for their own young, and none fail to be loving. How could there be contention, plunder, insubordination, or rebellion? How could anyone fail to love righteousness yet bring affairs to completion [?]? This is what is meant by order throughout all under Heaven, and it is what makes the gentleman beyond compare. Yet the gentleman seeks nothing from all under Heaven: principle is inherently supremely harmonious, and each simply accords with it. Nor does the world show partiality toward the gentleman: principle is inherently wholly sufficient, and each simply finds sufficiency in it. When each accords with it, the gentleman moves all under Heaven and reaches their hearts; that through which he moves them is Heaven. When each finds sufficiency in it, all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
應君子而興所以應之者亦天也至微而至彰
至遠而至近神化存焉耳君子不得而知也天
下不得而知也大哉心乎冒天下之道如斯而
已乎而智術以圖治者藐乎卑矣故曰君子所
以致天下之治者無他焉亦惟其心之公而已
矣是道也求之堯舜書曰惟精惟一允執厥中
曰克明峻德曰克諧以孝言乎其心之公也德
之明也身之脩也天之合也是故推之國家天
下自九族之既睦而至于萬邦協和自烝烝乂
===
而至于四方風動絜矩之道堯舜盡之矣故曰
堯舜帥天下以仁而民從之堯舜而後禹之祗
台湯之制心文武之緝熈建極皆所以善事乎
心也故其治化之成為不距為彰信為修和為
丕冒孰非絜矩之所致哉反是則私私則偽偽
則與天不相似矣豈可以言治邪故求治于天
下者不必求于天下而求之吾心斯得之矣治
心之要何居曰主靜而已矣天地之道不專一
則不能直遂不翕聚則不能發散天地且然而
punctuated:
應君子而興，所以應之者亦天也。至微而至彰，至遠而至近，神化存焉耳。君子不得而知也，天下不得而知也。大哉，心乎！冒天下之道，如斯而已乎！而智術以圖治者，藐乎卑矣。故曰：君子所以致天下之治者，無他焉，亦惟其心之公而已矣。
是道也，求之堯舜。《書》曰：「惟精惟一，允執厥中。」曰：「克明峻德。」曰：「克諧以孝。」言乎其心之公也，德之明也，身之脩也，天之合也。是故推之國家天下，自九族之既睦而至于萬邦協和，自烝烝乂而至于四方風動。絜矩之道，堯舜盡之矣。故曰：「堯舜帥天下以仁，而民從之。」堯舜而後，禹之祗台，湯之制心，文武之緝熈建極，皆所以善事乎心也。故其治化之成，為不距，為彰信，為修和，為丕冒，孰非絜矩之所致哉？反是則私，私則偽，偽則與天不相似矣，豈可以言治邪？故求治于天下者，不必求于天下，而求之吾心，斯得之矣。
治心之要何居？曰：主靜而已矣。天地之道，不專一則不能直遂，不翕聚則不能發散。天地且然而
translation_en:
…respond to the gentleman and are stirred to action; that through which they respond is likewise Heaven. Utterly subtle yet utterly manifest, utterly distant yet utterly near: spiritual transformation resides therein. The gentleman cannot comprehend it, nor can the people of the world. Great indeed is the heart! Its way of embracing all under Heaven amounts to just this! How paltry and lowly, then, are those who seek good government through clever schemes. Thus I say: there is nothing else by which the gentleman brings order to all under Heaven; it is simply the impartiality of his heart.
To seek this Way, turn to Yao and Shun. The Book of Documents says: “Be discerning and single-minded; truly hold fast to the Mean.” It also says: “He was able to make manifest his lofty virtue,” and “He was able to bring harmony through filial piety.” These speak of the impartiality of their hearts, the illumination of their virtue, the cultivation of their persons, and their accord with Heaven. Thus, when extended to the state and all under Heaven, this proceeded from harmony among the nine degrees of kinship to concord among the myriad states, and from steady progress in good order to the four quarters being moved as by the wind. Yao and Shun fully realized the Way of the measuring square—the principle of judging others’ needs by one’s own. Hence the saying: “Yao and Shun led all under Heaven with benevolence, and the people followed them.” After Yao and Shun, Yu’s reverent attention to himself, Tang’s regulation of his heart, and Kings Wen and Wu’s continuing illumination and establishment of the supreme standard were all means of properly tending the heart. Thus their achievements in government and moral transformation met with no resistance, made trustworthiness manifest, fostered harmony, and extended protection far and wide. Which of these was not brought about by the principle of the measuring square? To turn against this is to be selfish; selfishness leads to falsity, and falsity leaves one unlike Heaven. How could one then speak of good government? Thus those who seek order in all under Heaven need not seek it in the world: by seeking it in their own hearts, they will attain it.
Wherein lies the essential means of governing the heart? I answer: simply in making stillness the governing principle. In the Way of Heaven and Earth, without single-minded concentration there can be no direct advance; without gathering together there can be no spreading forth. Even Heaven and Earth are thus, and…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
况于人乎是故無欲其本也主敬其功也無欲
則靜虛動直主敬則欲寡理明積而久之神乎
天德而絜矩之道自我出矣尚何天下有不平
哉謹論
同前
唐時舉
同考試官教諭劉批題本冠冕作者難於精當此
篇議論不離本傳而委曲抑揚有法度有精采論場中之健筆也故
復錄之以式學者
===
考試官教諭姜批開闔無窮自是作筆
考試官教授陸批格高詞爽
君子能以其心一天下而後可以運天下夫天
下之求於君子也至衆也勢也君子之運於天
下也至簡也心也勢之所極而心行焉則天下
莫不各以其分而取足於君子心之所運而勢
通焉則君子亦莫不各以其情而均其欲於天
下是故勢也者天下之所異也心也者天下之
所同也所貴於君子者不過推天下之所同者
punctuated:
况于人乎？是故，無欲其本也，主敬其功也。無欲則靜虛動直，主敬則欲寡理明。積而久之，神乎天德，而絜矩之道自我出矣，尚何天下有不平哉？謹論。

同前。
唐時舉。

同考試官教諭劉批：題本冠冕，作者難於精當。此篇議論不離本傳，而委曲抑揚，有法度，有精采，論場中之健筆也，故復錄之以式學者。

考試官教諭姜批：開闔無窮，自是作筆。

考試官教授陸批：格高詞爽。

君子能以其心一天下，而後可以運天下。夫天下之求於君子也，至衆也，勢也；君子之運於天下也，至簡也，心也。勢之所極而心行焉，則天下莫不各以其分而取足於君子；心之所運而勢通焉，則君子亦莫不各以其情而均其欲於天下。是故，勢也者，天下之所異也；心也者，天下之所同也。所貴於君子者，不過推天下之所同者
translation_en:
…how much more so with human beings? Thus, freedom from desire is the foundation, and maintaining reverent attentiveness is the work required. With no desires, one is empty in stillness and upright in action; by maintaining reverent attentiveness, desires diminish and principle becomes clear. Through sustained accumulation over time, one becomes wondrously attuned to Heaven’s virtue, and the Way of the measuring square proceeds from oneself. How, then, could anything under Heaven remain unequally treated? Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Same topic as above.
By Tang Shiju.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The topic itself is grand and dignified, making precision and aptness difficult for the writer. This essay’s argument never departs from the original commentary, yet its intricate development and its modulations have both discipline and brilliance. It is a vigorous piece of writing among the discourses submitted in this examination; accordingly, we have also recorded it to provide a model for students.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Its unfolding and drawing together are inexhaustible: this is indeed the work of an accomplished writer.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: Its style is lofty and its language crisp.

Only when the gentleman can unite all under Heaven through his heart can he direct all under Heaven. What the people under Heaven seek from the gentleman is exceedingly manifold: this arises from their circumstances. What the gentleman employs to direct all under Heaven is exceedingly simple: his heart. Wherever circumstances extend, his heart acts; thus everyone under Heaven obtains from the gentleman what suffices for their respective station. Wherever his heart operates, circumstances are brought into accord; thus the gentleman, taking account of each person’s feelings, equitably satisfies the desires of all under Heaven. Hence circumstances are what differ among the people under Heaven, while the heart is what they share. What is valued in the gentleman is nothing more than his extending what all under Heaven share…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以一天下而已矣是故其操也非有煩也其動
也非有阻也其邇不距也而其遠不禦也至易
至簡而天下之化成夫是之謂絜矩之道也故
曰君子能以其心一天下而後可以運天下今
夫矩也物之所由以方也矩設則天下之物無
不方者矣心也者天下之所由以平也心之矩
設則天下之民無不平者矣蓋嘗觀之天下至
大矣而遠者近者智者愚者衆者寡者紛紛焉
擾擾焉以求競於其私遂至於相凌相軋相勝
===
而莫之捄止此皆不明於因心之故者也夫心
也者至寂而感也至微而著也至近而遠也至
無而有也至無而有故用可神也至近而遠故
化可博也至微而著故端可求也至寂而感故
應可順也而彼以其起於競也皆自廢其心者
也天下而至於自廢其心其又可得而平乎故
君子於此直因其心之所同者而驗之自夫我
之有老老也而興孝之心同矣自夫我之有長
長也而興弟之心同矣自夫我之有恤孤也而
punctuated: 以一天下而已矣。是故其操也非有煩也，其動也非有阻也，其邇不距也，而其遠不禦也。至易至簡，而天下之化成，夫是之謂絜矩之道也。故曰：「君子能以其心一天下，而後可以運天下。」今夫矩也，物之所由以方也；矩設，則天下之物無不方者矣。心也者，天下之所由以平也；心之矩設，則天下之民無不平者矣。蓋嘗觀之，天下至大矣，而遠者、近者、智者、愚者、衆者、寡者，紛紛焉，擾擾焉，以求競於其私，遂至於相凌、相軋、相勝，而莫之捄止。此皆不明於因心之故者也。夫心也者，至寂而感也，至微而著也，至近而遠也，至無而有也。至無而有，故用可神也；至近而遠，故化可博也；至微而著，故端可求也；至寂而感，故應可順也。而彼以其起於競也，皆自廢其心者也。天下而至於自廢其心，其又可得而平乎？故君子於此，直因其心之所同者而驗之。自夫我之有老老也，而興孝之心同矣；自夫我之有長長也，而興弟之心同矣；自夫我之有恤孤也，而
translation_en: …thereby to unite all under Heaven, and nothing more. Thus, there is nothing complicated in his practice and nothing obstructed in his action. Those nearby do not resist him, and those far away do not oppose him. Through the utmost ease and simplicity, the moral transformation of all under Heaven is accomplished. This is what is called the Way of applying the measuring square. Hence it is said: “Only after the gentleman can unite all under Heaven through his own heart can he guide all under Heaven.” Now, the square is that by which things are made square. Once the square is established, nothing under Heaven fails to be square. The heart is that by which all under Heaven is brought into equitable order. Once the heart’s square is established, none of the people under Heaven fails to receive equitable treatment. I have considered this: vast indeed is the world, yet those far away and those nearby, the wise and the foolish, the many and the few, in their confusion and turmoil, seek to compete for their private interests. They consequently come to oppress, crush, and overcome one another, with no one to rescue them or put a stop to it. All this arises from failure to understand what it means to follow the heart. The heart is utterly still yet responsive, utterly subtle yet manifest, utterly near yet far-reaching, utterly without form yet possessed of reality. Because it is utterly without form yet possessed of reality, its functioning can be wondrous; because it is utterly near yet far-reaching, its transforming influence can be extensive; because it is utterly subtle yet manifest, its beginnings can be sought out; because it is utterly still yet responsive, its responses can accord with circumstances. Yet those whose actions arise from rivalry have all cast aside their own hearts. If all under Heaven reach the point of casting aside their own hearts, how can equitable order be attained? Thus, in this matter, the gentleman simply follows what hearts share and puts it to the test. When I treat my elders as elders, others share the impulse to filial devotion thereby awakened; when I treat my seniors as seniors, others share the impulse to fraternal deference thereby awakened; when I show compassion for orphans, then…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
不倍之心同矣君子之心不約而行於天下非
其有强而合之者也天下之心不言而同於君
子非其有分而畀之者也於是君子因而推之
度吾之矩於好惡也我之所欲也天下之所同
也與民同欲之而已矣我之所惡也天下之所
同也與民同惡之而已矣夫與民同惡也則恫
瘝之心生恫瘝之心生則法天之震曜因之以
同去乎其病與民同好也則保合之心生保合
之心生則法天之生殖因之以同滿乎其分於
===
是天下咸服吾之公然其爲好惡之大端者有
二曰用人而已矣理財而已矣度吾之矩以用
人也則賢者必舉而休休之臣進矣不肖者必
退而娼疾之人屏矣寅亮熈載則公卿大夫得
其職康惠屏垣則州牧侯伯得其職修攘懷服
則尹帥師長得其職於是天下咸服吾之義度
吾之矩以理財也則其悖入有禁而聚斂之人
逐矣其生之有道而損益之政行矣因天分地
則阜生得其紀經賦式用則斂節得其紀生富
punctuated:
不倍之心同矣。君子之心不約而行於天下，非其有强而合之者也；天下之心不言而同於君子，非其有分而畀之者也。於是君子因而推之，度吾之矩於好惡也：我之所欲也，天下之所同也，與民同欲之而已矣；我之所惡也，天下之所同也，與民同惡之而已矣。夫與民同惡也，則恫瘝之心生；恫瘝之心生，則法天之震曜，因之以同去乎其病。與民同好也，則保合之心生；保合之心生，則法天之生殖，因之以同滿乎其分。於是天下咸服吾之公。
然其爲好惡之大端者有二，曰用人而已矣，理財而已矣。度吾之矩以用人也，則賢者必舉，而休休之臣進矣；不肖者必退，而娼疾之人屏矣。寅亮熈載，則公卿大夫得其職；康惠屏垣，則州牧侯伯得其職；修攘懷服，則尹帥師長得其職。於是天下咸服吾之義。度吾之矩以理財也，則其悖入有禁，而聚斂之人逐矣；其生之有道，而損益之政行矣。因天分地，則阜生得其紀；經賦式用，則斂節得其紀；生富
translation_en:
…the disposition not to turn one’s back on others is shared by all. The gentleman’s intentions prevail throughout the realm without prior agreement; this is not because he forces people into conformity. The hearts of all under Heaven accord with the gentleman’s without a word being spoken; this is not because he has apportioned something and bestowed it upon them. The gentleman therefore extends this shared disposition, applying his measuring square to likes and dislikes: what I desire is what all under Heaven share, so I simply desire it together with the people; what I abhor is what all under Heaven share, so I simply abhor it together with the people. Sharing the people’s aversions gives rise to heartfelt concern for their suffering. From this concern, one models oneself on Heaven’s thunderous might and thereby joins with them to remove their afflictions. Sharing the people’s preferences gives rise to a wish to preserve them in harmony. From this wish, one models oneself on Heaven’s generation and nurture and thereby joins with them to ensure that each receives their full due. Thus all under Heaven acknowledge my impartiality.
There are, however, two principal spheres in which these likes and dislikes operate: employing men and managing wealth. When I apply my measuring square to employing men, the worthy are invariably promoted, and magnanimous ministers advance; the unworthy are invariably dismissed, and jealous people [?] are excluded. Through reverent assistance and the splendid accomplishment of affairs, the dukes, ministers, and grandees fulfill their offices. Through bringing peace and beneficence and serving as protective walls, regional governors and lords fulfill their offices. Through cultivating internal order, repelling threats, cherishing the distant, and securing their submission, administrators and military commanders fulfill their offices. Thus all under Heaven acknowledge my righteousness. When I apply my measuring square to managing wealth, wrongful acquisition is prohibited, and those who exact excessive levies are expelled; wealth is produced in accordance with the Way, and policies of reduction and increase are implemented. By following Heaven’s seasons and distinguishing the uses of the land, the increase of production is properly regulated; by regulating taxation and setting standards for expenditure, revenue collection and economy are properly regulated; by giving life and enriching…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
壽逸則生人得其紀於是天下咸服吾之仁是
故綱紀法度非以飾治也禮樂名物非以飾文
也慶賞刑威非以飾喜怒也其以通民之故順
民之性起民之志而行之者凡以天下之所同
也夫然後吾矩絜於此而上下四方無不均一
於是天下之遠者近者智者愚者强者弱者莫
不翕然而惟吾之聽而就於條理天下之老者
長者少者各得其所非獨興孝也而不得不孝
非獨興弟也而不得不弟非獨不倍也而不得
===
有倍使一夫無不獲之歎而天下可平也是故
君子惟知其絜矩之在我也是以不出戶牖而
可以知天下如日月之照臨於上雖以幽隱而
不能遁也不下階序而可以理天下如天地之
長養萬物各正其性命而不亂也以此而總攝
羣生以此而宰制萬務以此而周流六極絜矩
之道斯其至乎故吾聞之史之稱堯也存心於
天下一夫饑曰我饑之也一夫寒曰我寒之也
一人有罪曰我陷之也堯德其至矣而必曰我
punctuated: 壽逸，則生人得其紀，於是天下咸服吾之仁。是故綱紀法度非以飾治也，禮樂名物非以飾文也，慶賞刑威非以飾喜怒也。其以通民之故，順民之性，起民之志而行之者，凡以天下之所同也。夫然後吾矩絜於此，而上下四方無不均一。於是天下之遠者、近者、智者、愚者、强者、弱者，莫不翕然而惟吾之聽，而就於條理。天下之老者、長者、少者，各得其所。非獨興孝也，而不得不孝；非獨興弟也，而不得不弟；非獨不倍也，而不得有倍。使一夫無不獲之歎，而天下可平也。是故君子惟知其絜矩之在我也，是以不出戶牖而可以知天下，如日月之照臨於上，雖以幽隱而不能遁也；不下階序而可以理天下，如天地之長養萬物，各正其性命而不亂也。以此而總攝羣生，以此而宰制萬務，以此而周流六極，絜矩之道斯其至乎！故吾聞之，史之稱堯也，存心於天下，一夫饑，曰：「我饑之也。」一夫寒，曰：「我寒之也。」一人有罪，曰：「我陷之也。」堯德其至矣，而必曰我
translation_en:
…longevity and ease, then the people's lives attain their proper order, and all under Heaven acknowledge my benevolence. Thus, governing principles, laws, and institutions do not merely embellish government; rites, music, and named ceremonial objects do not merely embellish its cultural forms; celebrations, rewards, punishments, and coercive authority do not merely embellish joy and anger. These are put into practice to understand the people's circumstances, accord with their nature, and awaken their aspirations, all on the basis of what everyone under Heaven shares. Only then is my measuring square applied here, so that above and below and in all four directions everything is made equitable. Then, throughout the world, those far away and nearby, the wise and the foolish, the strong and the weak, all unite in heeding me and come into an orderly condition. The elderly, the mature, and the young throughout the world each obtain their proper place. It is not merely that filial devotion is inspired: they cannot but be filial. It is not merely that respect for elder brothers is inspired: they cannot but show that respect. It is not merely that they refrain from disloyalty: there can be no disloyalty. Let not even one man have cause to lament that he has not received his due, and all under Heaven can be brought to peace.

Thus the gentleman knows that the responsibility for applying the measuring square rests with himself. Hence, without going beyond his doors and windows, he can know all under Heaven, like the sun and moon shining down from above, whose light even the hidden and obscure cannot escape. Without descending his steps, he can bring order to all under Heaven, like Heaven and Earth nurturing the myriad things, each duly fulfilling its nature and allotted destiny without disorder. By this he brings all living beings under his care; by this he directs the myriad affairs; by this his influence reaches throughout the six extremities of the universe. Does not the Way of the measuring square reach its utmost here?

Thus I have heard that, in the histories' praise of Yao, he set his heart upon all under Heaven. If one man went hungry, he said, “I have caused him to go hungry.” If one man suffered cold, he said, “I have caused him to suffer cold.” If one person committed an offense, he said, “I have led him into it.” Yao's virtue had reached its utmost, yet he invariably said “I”…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
者堯以矩在我者也又曰以親九族九族旣睦
平章百姓百姓昭明協和萬邦黎民於變時雍
是則堯之絜矩也此其效也雖然君子豈强爲
之哉亦曰先養之以吾心之矩而已矣夫所謂
心之矩何也格致誠正而已矣吾之格致誠正
無一而不合於矩焉則由一身以至於家國天
下可得而論矣蓋格致則天下之志可通故能
以天下之心爲一心而吾絜矩之仁所以殊也
誠正則天下之私可勝故能以一心爲天下之
===
心而吾絜矩之量所以博也博則不隘殊則不
混而後可以其心一天下使其不然焉則私已
而已耳有私視也故有不見也有私聽也故有
不聞也有私慮也故有不知也安有運之天下
而可以私已參哉是故君子以心爲矩此一天
下之本原也吾故曰君子能以其心一天下而
後可以運天下
表
擬宋宴貢士賜綠袍鞾笏詩章謝表〔太平〕
punctuated:
者，堯以矩在我者也。又曰：「以親九族，九族旣睦，平章百姓；百姓昭明，協和萬邦，黎民於變時雍。」是則堯之絜矩也，此其效也。雖然，君子豈强爲之哉？亦曰先養之以吾心之矩而已矣。夫所謂心之矩何也？格致誠正而已矣。吾之格致誠正，無一而不合於矩焉，則由一身以至於家國天下，可得而論矣。蓋格致則天下之志可通，故能以天下之心爲一心，而吾絜矩之仁所以殊也；誠正則天下之私可勝，故能以一心爲天下之心，而吾絜矩之量所以博也。博則不隘，殊則不混，而後可以其心一天下。使其不然焉，則私已而已耳。有私視也，故有不見也；有私聽也，故有不聞也；有私慮也，故有不知也。安有運之天下，而可以私已參哉？是故君子以心爲矩，此一天下之本原也。吾故曰：君子能以其心一天下，而後可以運天下。

表

擬宋宴貢士賜綠袍鞾笏詩章謝表〔太平〕
translation_en:
…because Yao held that the measuring square lay within himself. It is further said: “He brought affection to the nine degrees of kinship. Once these were harmonious, he distinguished and ordered the hundred clans. Once the hundred clans were enlightened, he harmonized the myriad states, and the common people were thereby transformed and brought into concord.” This was Yao’s practice of applying the measuring square—the principle of judging others’ needs by one’s own—and these were its effects. Yet does the gentleman force himself to do this? He simply first nurtures it through the measuring square within his own heart. What is this measuring square of the heart? Nothing more than investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the heart. If none of these practices in me fails to accord with the measuring square, then we may discuss extending them from the individual to the family, the state, and all under Heaven.

Through investigating things and extending knowledge, one can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven. Thus one can take the hearts of all under Heaven as a single heart; this is how the benevolence with which I apply the measuring square makes distinctions. Through sincerity of intention and rectification of the heart, one can overcome the selfishness of all under Heaven. Thus one can make one heart the heart of all under Heaven; this is how my capacity to apply the measuring square becomes broad. Being broad, it is not confined; making distinctions, it does not confuse. Only then can one unite all under Heaven through one’s heart. Otherwise, one merely favors oneself. Selfishness in looking leaves things unseen; selfishness in listening leaves things unheard; selfishness in thinking leaves things unknown. How could one govern all under Heaven while allowing selfishness to intrude? Thus the gentleman takes his heart as the measuring square: this is the foundation for uniting all under Heaven. Therefore I say: only when the gentleman can unite all under Heaven through his heart can he govern all under Heaven.

Memorial

A memorial of thanks, composed as if under the Song dynasty, for a banquet for tribute scholars and gifts of green robes, boots, audience tablets, and verses. 〔Taiping …〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
興國二年
許宏用
同考試官教諭阮批用事切實措詞典雅非特
工於四六而已不亦文之表表者乎
同考試官教諭林批佳句愈出愈竒讀此作猶
聆韶濩之音不覺令人豁然也可錄可錄
同考試官學正何批表中感激之情溢於言外
考試官教諭姜批駢儷典則可取
考試官教授陸批得體
===
太平興國二年正月某日臣某等伏蒙
聖恩錫宴及綠袍鞾笏詩二章者伏以
羲畫堯言麗珠璣於北斗
周笱商鼎出珍綺於上方氣協雲龍
惠均苹鹿際
龍飛之景運煥奎聚之人文臣某等誠懽誠忭
稽首頓首上言虞帝闢門明山彝以作服
殷宗審象賴麴糵以交修惟上下之志通
故地天之道泰賡歌不聞於喜起幽側安
punctuated:
興國二年。
許宏用。
同考試官教諭阮批：用事切實，措詞典雅，非特工於四六而已，不亦文之表表者乎！
同考試官教諭林批：佳句愈出愈竒，讀此作猶聆韶濩之音，不覺令人豁然也。可錄，可錄！
同考試官學正何批：表中感激之情溢於言外。
考試官教諭姜批：駢儷典則，可取。
考試官教授陸批：得體。
太平興國二年正月某日，臣某等伏蒙聖恩錫宴及綠袍鞾笏、詩二章者，伏以：羲畫堯言，麗珠璣於北斗；周笱商鼎，出珍綺於上方。氣協雲龍，惠均苹鹿。際龍飛之景運，煥奎聚之人文。臣某等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言：虞帝闢門，明山彝以作服；殷宗審象，賴麴糵以交修。惟上下之志通，故地天之道泰。賡歌不聞於喜起，幽側安
translation_en:
…the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977).

Xu Hongyong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ruan, Instructor: “The allusions are apt and substantial, and the diction classical and elegant. This is more than mere skill in four-and-six prose. Is it not an outstanding piece of writing!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Each fine phrase is more remarkable than the last. Reading this composition is like hearing the music of Shao and Huo: one cannot help feeling one's mind open and clear. Worth selecting, worth selecting!”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, School Instructor: “The gratitude expressed in this memorial overflows beyond its words.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The parallel prose conforms to classical standards and merits selection.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: “Appropriate to the form.”

On a certain day of the first month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo, we, your servants So-and-so and others, humbly received Your Majesty's gracious gift of a banquet, green robes, boots, audience tablets, and two poems. We respectfully reflect:

Like Fuxi's diagrams and Yao's words, your compositions array pearls and gems beside the Northern Dipper; like Zhou fish baskets [?] and Shang tripods, precious and splendid gifts issue from the imperial stores. Our vital forces accord, as clouds follow the dragon; your favor extends equally to us, as deer share the duckweed. We encounter the glorious age of the dragon's ascent, when literary culture shines like stars gathered in the constellation Kui. We, your servants So-and-so and others, truly joyful and truly delighted, bow our heads to the ground and knock our foreheads upon it, submitting these words:

The Emperor of Yu opened his gates, displaying mountain and ritual-vessel emblems to fashion ceremonial robes. The revered ruler of Yin examined an image to find his minister, relying upon him as yeast and malt for their mutual cultivation. Only when the intentions of ruler and subjects communicate does the intercourse of Earth and Heaven bring peace. If responsive songs of joy and rising to service are not heard, how can those in humble obscurity …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
望於明揚雖拊髀以興思豈借才於異代
顧茲
希典實出
昌朝伏念臣某等菲葑下體糟粕斷經技空
拙於雕蟲才僅施於襪線詎意網羅之盛
選濫塵麟鳳之兼收需雲著象於六爻章
天抒歌於四始屨傳飾足卑讚牧身懽授
粲於緇衣記對命於玉藻嬰心入寐顧影
生慚被褐敢負於懷珠囊螢自分於食藿
===
同岱畎之絲枲獲貢
王廷比野人之藻芹豈甘田畝文非韓愈詎
懷龍虎之榮策愧仲舒孰抱天人之業不
謂縉紳之盛事聿振
醇世之希聲心敢侈于五榮
恩獨殊於九宴歌擊筑於漢祖惜霸心其猶存
忘設醴于穆生歎明時之不值弊衣空泣
於寶應折俎粗寵於宣徽開聞喜於曲江
徒炫醵金之會兆先幾於神栁但符尚象
punctuated:
望於明揚？雖拊髀以興思，豈借才於異代？顧茲希典，實出昌朝。

伏念臣某等，菲葑下體，糟粕斷經，技空拙於雕蟲，才僅施於襪線。詎意網羅之盛選，濫塵麟鳳之兼收！需雲著象於六爻，章天抒歌於四始。屨傳飾足，卑讚牧身，懽授粲於緇衣，記對命於玉藻。嬰心入寐，顧影生慚。被褐敢負於懷珠？囊螢自分於食藿。同岱畎之絲枲，獲貢王廷；比野人之藻芹，豈甘田畝？文非韓愈，詎懷龍虎之榮？策愧仲舒，孰抱天人之業？

不謂縉紳之盛事，聿振醇世之希聲！心敢侈于五榮，恩獨殊於九宴。歌擊筑於漢祖，惜霸心其猶存；忘設醴于穆生，歎明時之不值。弊衣空泣於寶應，折俎粗寵於宣徽。開聞喜於曲江，徒炫醵金之會；兆先幾於神栁，但符尚象
translation_en:
…hope to be brought to light and advanced? Though one pats one’s thigh in longing for worthy men, why borrow talent from another age? This rare ceremony truly issues from a flourishing court.

We, your servants So-and-so and the others, humbly reflect that we are but the lowly roots of radish and turnip, the dregs of fragmentary classical learning. Our skill amounts only to clumsy literary ornament; our talent stretches no farther than thread for stockings. How could we have imagined that, in this grand selection casting its net for talent, we would undeservedly be gathered among unicorns and phoenixes? The clouds of the hexagram Waiting display their image among its six lines; songs celebrating Heaven are voiced in the Four Beginnings of the Book of Odes. Footwear is said to adorn the feet, and lowliness is praised as a means of tending oneself [?]. We rejoice in the gift of fine grain evoked by “Black Robes,” and recall the response to a command prescribed in “Jade Pendants.” These thoughts possess our hearts even in sleep; looking upon our own shadows, we feel ashamed. Clad in coarse cloth, dare we betray the pearl held within? Studying by bagged fireflies, we accept our lot of eating bean leaves. Like the silk and hemp of the valleys of Mount Dai, we have been offered as tribute at the royal court; like the rustic offering water plants and celery, how could we remain content among the fields? Our writing is no match for Han Yu’s: how could we aspire to the glory of dragons and tigers? Our policy essays fall shamefully short of Dong Zhongshu’s: who among us possesses his mastery of Heaven and humanity?

We never expected that this splendid occasion for the gentry would sound anew the rare strains of an age of pure virtue! Dare our hearts aspire extravagantly to the five glories? Yet this favor surpasses even that of the nine banquets. When Gaozu of Han sang to the accompaniment of the zhu, it was regrettable that the ambition of a hegemon still remained. When sweet wine was no longer provided for Mu Sheng, one lamented that he had not encountered an enlightened age. In the Baoying era, tears over worn clothing were shed in vain; at the Court of Palace Ceremonial, portions of sacrificial meat afforded only modest favor. The Banquet of Rejoicing at the News, held at Qujiang, merely flaunted a gathering funded by pooled contributions; the early portent disclosed by the divine willow merely fulfilled a divination that prized images …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之占豈若
離裁侁隆
晉錫玆蓋伏遇
○○○○
敷皇作極
大智用中
法黃帝之垂裳
躬文王之昃食
天經地緯志混一於中原
===
虎步龍行兼創垂於
藝帝謂太平匪繇一士曜黼黻於
皇猷謂大烹所以養賢佇燮調於
聖代
總五服五章之寵柄
降三握三吐之虛衷
黻座臨軒灑絲綸之清問
彤庭賜第寵閶闔之芳名
渥惠下而樽俎星陳
punctuated: 之占。豈若離裁侁隆，晉錫！玆蓋伏遇○○○○，敷皇作極，大智用中，法黃帝之垂裳，躬文王之昃食。天經地緯，志混一於中原；虎步龍行，兼創垂於藝帝。謂太平匪繇一士，曜黼黻於皇猷；謂大烹所以養賢，佇燮調於聖代。總五服五章之寵柄，降三握三吐之虛衷。黻座臨軒，灑絲綸之清問；彤庭賜第，寵閶闔之芳名。渥惠下而樽俎星陳，
translation_en:
…the divination. How could that compare with the exalted imperial dispensation [?] and the bestowal of advancement! This is because we have humbly encountered ○○○○, who sets forth the august standard and establishes the supreme norm, and whose great wisdom applies the Mean. He follows the Yellow Emperor in governing with robes hanging down, and personally emulates King Wen in delaying his meal until the sun declines. Taking Heaven as warp and Earth as weft, he aspires to unite the Central Plain; striding like a tiger and moving like a dragon, he combines founding achievement with a legacy for posterity—“藝帝” [?].

He holds that peace throughout the realm does not depend upon a single scholar, and brings the embroidered splendor of cultivated talent to illuminate the imperial enterprise. He holds that lavish feasts serve to nourish the worthy, and awaits those who will harmonize affairs in this sagely age. He commands the authority to confer favor through the five robes and their five insignia, and graciously reveals the humility of one who thrice grasps his unbound hair and thrice spits out his food to receive worthy men. From his embroidered throne he presides at the palace balcony, issuing searching questions in imperial pronouncements; in the vermilion court he grants examination ranks, honoring distinguished names at the palace gates. Abundant favor descends, and wine vessels and sacrificial stands are arrayed like stars…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
□恩暢而冠蓋雲集金釀玉削俾襲鴈塔以
新題
鳳翥龍蟠忽燭雲霄而下濟魚躍式逢於雷
化鷺序幸竊於玉聯學豈儒宗叨荷韋彪
之珍襲賦非德諷竝受司馬之金莖覆信
美馬周之飾羶耀握嘉孫樵之起鯁飽大
官之清馥恍新睹於膏梁釋韋布之卑微
懽初陪于履舄臣某等敢不曳婁拜賜煥
衣被於
===
日華什襲寶藏思對揚於
天藻飾先簠簋補效
袞衣操節肯變於伐檀勛名懼慙於濡鵜釀
經酣史敢廢淵源緯治經邦誓懷糜殞伏
願煥爛時歌於
舜旦璣衡長運於
堯尊
配地配天彌綸
至誠之功化
punctuated:
□恩暢而冠蓋雲集，金釀玉削，俾襲鴈塔以新題。鳳翥龍蟠，忽燭雲霄而下濟；魚躍式逢於雷化，鷺序幸竊於玉聯。學豈儒宗，叨荷韋彪之珍襲；賦非德諷，竝受司馬之金莖。覆信美馬周之飾羶，耀握嘉孫樵之起鯁。飽大官之清馥，恍新睹於膏梁；釋韋布之卑微，懽初陪于履舄。臣某等敢不曳婁拜賜，煥衣被於日華；什襲寶藏，思對揚於天藻。飾先簠簋，補效袞衣；操節肯變於伐檀，勛名懼慙於濡鵜。釀經酣史，敢廢淵源；緯治經邦，誓懷糜殞。
伏願煥爛時歌於舜旦，璣衡長運於堯尊，配地配天，彌綸至誠之功化。
translation_en:
…Your □ favor spreads abroad, and capped officials and their carriages gather like clouds. With golden brew and jade carving [?], you enable us to add fresh inscriptions to the Wild Goose Pagoda. Phoenixes soar and dragons coil: your writing suddenly illuminates the cloudy heavens and descends to aid us. Like leaping fish, we have encountered the thunder that transforms us into dragons; we have fortunately gained places in the egret ranks of court, joined with jade-like worthies. How could our learning qualify us as masters of the Confucian tradition? Yet we undeservedly receive precious gifts like those bestowed upon Wei Biao [?]. Our rhapsodies offer no admonition concerning virtue, yet we too receive Sima’s “golden stem” [?]. Your sheltering favor indeed commends Ma Zhou’s “adornment of rank-smelling meat” [?]; the radiance held in our hands honors Sun Qiao’s “rousing the forthright” [?]. Sated with the pure fragrance of food from the imperial provisioners, we seem to behold fine grain and meat for the first time. Leaving behind the lowly condition of leather belts and plain cloth, we rejoice to take our first places among the ranks of court. How could we, your servants So-and-so and the others, fail to trail our robes [?] and bow in thanks for these gifts, our clothing radiant in the imperial sunlight? Wrapping them in many layers and treasuring them, we intend to acknowledge and proclaim your heavenly compositions. We shall first adorn the sacrificial vessels through proper conduct and strive to mend the imperial dragon robe by assisting your rule. Would we compromise our integrity and incur the reproach of “Cutting Sandalwood”? We fear that our achievements and reputation may bring us the shame described in “The Pelican Wetting Its Wings.” Brewing the Classics and drinking deeply of the Histories, how dare we neglect the sources of learning? Weaving good government and ordering the realm, we pledge ourselves to service even unto death.
We humbly pray that songs of splendor may continually resound at Shun’s dawn, and that the celestial mechanism may revolve forever under Yao’s majesty; that, matching Earth and matching Heaven, the transforming achievements of your utmost sincerity may encompass all…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
得名得壽詠歌
大聖之休祥臣某等無任瞻
天仰
聖恇躍感激之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
===
===

第一問
蔡制

translation_en:
…attaining renown and longevity, we sing in praise of the auspicious blessings of the Great Sage. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sageliness, overwhelmed with trembling elation [?] and gratitude. We respectfully submit this memorial of thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays

First Question
Cai Zhi 蔡制

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: The workings of our Emperor’s supreme virtue and the splendor of his rites and music extend throughout the realm. They truly far surpass preceding ages and accord with the magnificent achievements and virtue of the Sagely Progenitor, following the same standard across the generations. You have described each in detail and have further traced their source to the essential principle of reverent single-mindedness in the imperial heart. Your exposition and praise are almost exhaustive. This answer is selected for more than its literary merits alone.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: The profound mysteries of our Emperor’s learning of the mind manifest themselves in the magnificence of his achievements and virtue. Your praise is detailed and apt: you have evidently been steeped in this teaching and gained an understanding of it.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The exposition is clear and thorough and can serve as a model.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授陸批得稱頌體
對有帝王之盛德大業者以創垂之于上
則其時必有立德立言之臣以揄揚之于
下是故其精神足以窺天運而摹神功其
言辭足以鋪閎休而耀偉績布之天下而
天下信其猷流之萬世而萬世侈其盛鏗
鉤炳燿赫奕偉燁此固帝王之所隆也由
今觀之如在其當時而上古之懿鑠神聖
之休靈迄久而逾章而樹之乎無窮凡以
===
此也是故堯舜帝之隆也禹湯文武王之
盛也其可以上繼而遠承者其惟我
太祖高皇帝逮我
皇上乎昔者益之賛堯也曰帝德廣運乃聖乃
神乃文乃武臯陶之賛舜也曰帝德罔愆
臨下以簡御衆以寬夫其仁之如天也其
德之好生也巍巍蕩蕩同於天地至今爲
烈以有益與臯陶也曰有典有則以詒子
孫則五子所以歌禹也曰聖敬日躋式于
punctuated:
考試官教授陸批：得稱頌體。

對：有帝王之盛德大業者，以創垂之于上，則其時必有立德立言之臣，以揄揚之于下。是故其精神足以窺天運而摹神功，其言辭足以鋪閎休而耀偉績，布之天下而天下信其猷，流之萬世而萬世侈其盛。鏗鉤炳燿，赫奕偉燁，此固帝王之所隆也。由今觀之，如在其當時，而上古之懿鑠、神聖之休靈，迄久而逾章，而樹之乎無窮，凡以此也。是故堯舜，帝之隆也；禹湯文武，王之盛也。其可以上繼而遠承者，其惟我太祖高皇帝逮我皇上乎！昔者益之賛堯也，曰：「帝德廣運，乃聖乃神，乃文乃武。」臯陶之賛舜也，曰：「帝德罔愆，臨下以簡，御衆以寬。」夫其仁之如天也，其德之好生也，巍巍蕩蕩，同於天地，至今爲烈，以有益與臯陶也。曰：「有典有則，以詒子孫。」則五子所以歌禹也。曰：「聖敬日躋，式于
translation_en:
Examiner, Professor Lu, comments: It achieves the proper form for an encomium.

In reply: When a sovereign possesses the flourishing virtue and great accomplishments of the ancient emperors and kings, establishing them on high and transmitting them to posterity, there must in his time be ministers below who establish lasting virtue and lasting words to extol him. Thus their spiritual insight suffices to discern Heaven’s workings and portray his wondrous achievements; their language suffices to expound his vast beneficence and illuminate his mighty deeds. Disseminated throughout the realm, their words lead all under Heaven to trust his plans; transmitted through ten thousand generations, they lead those generations to celebrate his greatness. Resonant [?] and brilliant, resplendent and magnificent: these are indeed what exalt emperors and kings. Viewed from the present, their deeds seem to unfold before us in their own time. The splendid excellence of high antiquity and the blessed potency of its divine sages grow ever more manifest with the passage of time and endure without limit—all because of this.

Thus Yao and Shun represent the height of imperial achievement; Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, the fullness of kingly greatness. Those capable of succeeding them and carrying forward their distant legacy—surely these are our Emperor Taizu Gao and, after him, our present Emperor!

In former times, Yi praised Yao, saying: “The emperor’s virtue is far-reaching in its operation: sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and martial affairs.” Gao Yao praised Shun, saying: “The emperor’s virtue is without fault; he oversees those below with simplicity and governs the multitude with generosity.” Their benevolence was like Heaven, and their virtue cherished life; towering and boundless, they equaled Heaven and Earth. That their achievements remain illustrious to this day is because there were Yi and Gao Yao.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
九圍則殷人所以頌湯也曰宣哲惟人文
武惟后曰執競武王無競維烈則周公所
以美文武也夫其靈承帝事肇修人紀地
平天成萬世允賴俾三代盛隆昭揭日月
獨以詩書之載粲焉可睹也使萬世之下
歷選哲辟攷德論世煥在方冊猗乎盛矣
繇是以降神母夜號漢高崛起而史有寬
仁大度規模宏遠之稱信乎其爲天授也
霍精晝謁唐宗肇業而史有比跡湯武庶
===
幾成康之稱蓋卓乎其不可及也神木兆
符日光啟運而藝祖聿興至其曰神武不
殺君道偉然其亦近於知言矣然漢之雜
霸唐之雜夷宋之卒於仁厚而不競也蓋
其侈詞則有之矣其可與二帝三王同日
語邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝體
神聖之上資握
天人之合贊奮起淮甸仗一劍以盪定羣雄掃
punctuated:
九圍，則殷人所以頌湯也。曰「宣哲惟人，文武惟后」，曰「執競武王，無競維烈」，則周公所以美文武也。夫其靈承帝事，肇修人紀，地平天成，萬世允賴，俾三代盛隆昭揭日月，獨以詩書之載，粲焉可睹也。使萬世之下，歷選哲辟，攷德論世，煥在方冊，猗乎盛矣！繇是以降，神母夜號，漢高崛起，而史有「寬仁大度，規模宏遠」之稱，信乎其爲天授也。霍精晝謁，唐宗肇業，而史有「比跡湯武，庶幾成康」之稱，蓋卓乎其不可及也。神木兆符，日光啟運，而藝祖聿興，至其曰「神武不殺，君道偉然」，其亦近於知言矣。然漢之雜霸，唐之雜夷，宋之卒於仁厚而不競也，蓋其侈詞則有之矣，其可與二帝三王同日語邪？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，體神聖之上資，握天人之合贊，奮起淮甸，仗一劍以盪定羣雄，掃
translation_en:
…the nine regions”: this was how the people of Yin praised Tang. The words “Discerning and wise was the man; cultured and martial was the sovereign,” and “Mighty was King Wu; matchless were his achievements,” were how the Duke of Zhou praised Kings Wen and Wu. They wondrously carried on the work of the Lord on High and first established order in human relations; the earth was brought to order and Heaven’s work completed, and all subsequent ages have indeed depended upon them. That the flourishing greatness of the Three Dynasties shines as clearly as the sun and moon, plainly visible to us, is due solely to its recording in the Odes and the Documents. Thus, even ten thousand generations later, one may survey the wise sovereigns in succession, examine their virtue, and assess their ages, all brilliantly preserved in written records. Ah, how splendid!
Thereafter, a divine mother cried out in the night, and Gaozu of Han rose to power. The histories praise his “generosity, benevolence, and magnanimity, and the grandeur and far-reaching scope of his designs.” Truly, his authority was bestowed by Heaven. Huo Jing [?] paid a visit in broad daylight, and the Tang sovereign laid the foundations of his dynasty. The histories praise him as one who “matched the deeds of Tang and Wu and approached Cheng and Kang.” Indeed, he stood so far above others that they could not attain his stature. A divine tree furnished an auspicious sign, sunlight inaugurated a new dynastic destiny, and the founding ancestor of Song arose. When the histories say, “Divinely martial without killing, he displayed the majestic Way of the ruler,” they too come close to discerning appraisal. Yet Han mingled its rule with the methods of hegemons; Tang mingled its rule with the ways of non-Chinese peoples; and Song ultimately proved benevolent and generous but lacking in strength. Extravagant praise there certainly was, but could these rulers be spoken of in the same breath as the Two Emperors and Three Kings?
We reverently consider our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor: endowed with the highest qualities of divine sagacity and supported jointly by Heaven and humanity, he rose in the Huai region and, wielding a single sword, subdued the contending warlords and swept…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
濯函區歷一紀而隆成
帝業拯生人之塗炭還狄虜於漠荒星珠月璧
功格乾樞滄海崑崙仁漸坤軸自古功德
之隆未有臻於玆理者故其當時若
大誥三篇
祖訓一錄傳於父老家喻戶曉而超黃邁唐越
商踰夏見於劉基
方丘之頌
文武神聖功高千古見於王景平雲南之頌其
===
它諸臣蓋未易以更縷數也而惟宋濂
日曆之序六者執事以爲得其精要誠是矣
一曰功高萬古二曰得國之正三曰獨禀
全智四曰敬天勤民五曰家法之嚴六曰
兵政有統此其與堯舜禹湯文武之盛德
大業曠世而同經眞足以凌耀古初而燕
休統緒矣然愚甞莊誦而伏思之竊以兵
政有統懲藩鎭之不掉家法之嚴戒戚寺
之預政敬天勤民窺
punctuated:
濯函區，歷一紀而隆成帝業，拯生人之塗炭，還狄虜於漠荒。星珠月璧，功格乾樞；滄海崑崙，仁漸坤軸。自古功德之隆，未有臻於玆理者。故其當時，若《大誥》三篇、《祖訓》一錄，傳於父老，家喻戶曉。而「超黃邁唐，越商踰夏」，見於劉基《方丘》之頌；「文武神聖，功高千古」，見於王景平雲南之頌。其它諸臣，蓋未易以更縷數也。
而惟宋濂《日曆》之序，六者執事以爲得其精要，誠是矣。一曰功高萬古，二曰得國之正，三曰獨禀全智，四曰敬天勤民，五曰家法之嚴，六曰兵政有統。此其與堯舜禹湯文武之盛德大業，曠世而同經，眞足以凌耀古初而燕休統緒矣。然愚甞莊誦而伏思之，竊以兵政有統，懲藩鎭之不掉；家法之嚴，戒戚寺之預政；敬天勤民，窺
translation_en:
…cleansed the realm, and over a twelve-year cycle brought the imperial enterprise to magnificent completion. He rescued the people from utter misery and drove the northern foes back into the desert wastes. Like pearl-like stars and the jade-disc moon, his achievements reached the pivot of Heaven; like the vast sea and Mount Kunlun, his benevolence suffused the axis of Earth. Since antiquity, no one’s achievements and virtue had attained such greatness. Thus, in his own time, works such as the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) and the single collection of Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) circulated among the elders and became known in every household. The words “surpassing the Yellow Emperor and outstripping Tang Yao, exceeding Shang and transcending Xia” appear in Liu Ji’s hymn to the Square Mound altar; “accomplished in civil and military affairs, divine and sagely, with achievements surpassing a thousand ages” appears in Wang Jing’s hymn celebrating the pacification of Yunnan. The other ministers’ compositions cannot readily be enumerated one by one.
As for the six points in Song Lian’s preface to the Daily Record (Rili), you judge that they capture the essential qualities, and this is indeed correct. The first is achievement surpassing all antiquity; the second, the rectitude of his acquisition of the realm; the third, his unique endowment with comprehensive wisdom; the fourth, reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people; the fifth, the strictness of his household regulations; and the sixth, unified command of military administration. In these respects, his flourishing virtue and great undertaking followed the same constant principles as those of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, despite the ages separating them. They were truly sufficient to outshine remote antiquity and bring peace and blessings to the dynastic succession. Yet I, in my ignorance, have solemnly recited this text and humbly reflected upon it. I venture to consider that “unified command of military administration” takes warning from the insubordination of regional military governors; “the strictness of his household regulations” guards against interference in government by imperial relatives and eunuchs; and “reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people” affords a glimpse of…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
仁敬之廣運獨稟全智仰
勇智之天錫則信然矣至於比漢高以爲得國
之正也統華夷以爲功高萬古也蓋亦宋
濂一時之言君子猶以爲有遺論焉蓋自
古創業之君唐因隋資宋襲周業獨漢起
自布衣此所謂爲高於川洿爲深於丘陵
者也蓋亦難矣我
太祖不階尺土起自徒步雖似於漢而義旗四
指志在弔伐
===
命將勿殺之戒昭昭乎天地臨之也斯亦以暴
天吏於天下矣愚竊以應天順人跡比湯
武而功則過之也自古創業之君止以驅
除禍亂雖其戡定之猷混一之業施鴻名
而騰茂烈然其敵皆以吾中國也我
太祖訊掃腥羶再造區夏驅禽獸而秩之彛典
剗左衽而還之冠裳使晦冥日月穢濁天
地得以復其開闢照臨之常愚竊以誠生
民之未有雖擬之盤古立極不過也
punctuated:
仁敬之廣運，獨稟全智，仰勇智之天錫，則信然矣。至於比漢高以爲得國之正也，統華夷以爲功高萬古也，蓋亦宋濂一時之言，君子猶以爲有遺論焉。蓋自古創業之君，唐因隋資，宋襲周業，獨漢起自布衣。此所謂爲高於川洿，爲深於丘陵者也，蓋亦難矣。我太祖不階尺土，起自徒步，雖似於漢，而義旗四指，志在弔伐。命將勿殺之戒，昭昭乎天地臨之也。斯亦以暴天吏於天下矣。愚竊以應天順人，跡比湯武，而功則過之也。

自古創業之君，止以驅除禍亂，雖其戡定之猷、混一之業，施鴻名而騰茂烈，然其敵皆以吾中國也。我太祖訊掃腥羶，再造區夏，驅禽獸而秩之彛典，剗左衽而還之冠裳，使晦冥日月、穢濁天地得以復其開闢照臨之常。愚竊以誠生民之未有，雖擬之盤古立極不過也。
translation_en:
…the far-reaching workings of benevolence and reverence; and, in his uniquely possessing perfect wisdom, we look up to his Heaven-bestowed courage and wisdom: these claims are indeed true. As for comparing him with Gaozu of Han to establish the legitimacy of his acquisition of the realm, and citing his unification of Chinese and non-Chinese peoples to declare his achievements unsurpassed through all antiquity, these were, after all, words Song Lian wrote on a particular occasion. The gentleman still considers that more remains to be said. Among dynastic founders since antiquity, the Tang inherited the resources of the Sui, and the Song succeeded to the enterprise of the Zhou.
