Only the Han founder arose from the common people. This is what is meant by making a height in a low-lying river basin and making a depth upon a hill: difficult indeed! Our Taizu, without so much as a foot of territory to serve as his stepping-stone, arose from the ranks of ordinary men. In this he resembled the Han founder, but wherever his righteous banners advanced, his purpose was to comfort the afflicted and punish the guilty. His injunction to his commanders not to kill was manifestly witnessed by Heaven and Earth. Thus he made himself known throughout the world as Heaven’s agent. In my humble view, in responding to Heaven and following the wishes of the people, his deeds matched those of Tang and King Wu, while his achievements surpassed theirs.

Since antiquity, dynastic founders have merely driven out calamity and disorder. Although their plans for pacification and their accomplishments in unification spread their great names and exalted their glorious deeds, their adversaries were all within our Central Realm [?]. Our Taizu swept away [?] the rank and mutton-smelling aliens and created the Chinese realm anew. He drove out the birds and beasts and ordered the people through enduring institutions; he eradicated left-lapped dress and restored caps and robes. He thereby enabled the sun and moon, which had been darkened, and Heaven and Earth, which had been defiled, to recover their constant order of illumination established at the beginning of the world. In my humble view, such an achievement had truly never occurred since humankind came into being. Even to compare him with Pangu establishing the cosmic order would be no exaggeration.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
列聖繼統推符配休炳
皇謨而賛
帝力代有其人永垂無極以逮我
皇上應天縱之
上聖承無疆之
大統
首正父子之倫
大孝達於今古
親裁
===
郊廟之典
至誠格于神明
澤洽南征則交人繫組
威暢北伐則虜酋褫魄括九圍而旅七緯濡
萬物而協庶徵
參天兩地
體信達順
道至于天慶雲見而膏露凝
道至于地靈兔儀而瑞鹿出執事所謂
punctuated: 列聖繼統，推符配休，炳皇謨而賛帝力，代有其人，永垂無極。以逮我皇上，應天縱之上聖，承無疆之大統，首正父子之倫，大孝達於今古；親裁郊廟之典，至誠格于神明；澤洽南征，則交人繫組；威暢北伐，則虜酋褫魄。括九圍而旅七緯，濡萬物而協庶徵，參天兩地，體信達順。道至于天，慶雲見而膏露凝；道至于地，靈兔儀而瑞鹿出。執事所謂：
translation_en: Successive sage emperors inherited the imperial succession, manifesting auspicious tokens and matching the blessings bestowed upon them. In every generation there were men who illuminated imperial plans and assisted imperial power, leaving an enduring legacy without limit. And so we come to our present Emperor, a supreme sage endowed by Heaven, who has inherited the boundless imperial succession. He first rectified the relationship between father and son, his great filial piety reaching across past and present. He personally determined the rites of the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, his utmost sincerity reaching the spirits. His beneficence spread through the southern campaign, and the people of Jiao bound themselves with cords in submission; his might extended through the northern expedition, and the barbarian chieftains lost their courage. He encompasses the nine regions and orders the seven celestial luminaries, nourishes all things and brings the manifold signs into harmony. He accords with Heaven’s number of three and Earth’s number of two, embodies trustworthiness and gives full expression to compliance with the cosmic order. When his Way reaches Heaven, auspicious clouds appear and rich dew condenses; when his Way reaches Earth, numinous rabbits present themselves and auspicious deer emerge. This is what you, honored examiners, call …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
至德之廣運禮樂之重光際天所覆極地所載
咸蒙
厚澤與
聖祖之功德先後一揆者真足以對揚
駿惠而熈播
休靈矣况於珥筆執經之彦
帷幄論思之老必有以默窺
彌綸天地之機緘宏鋪
幽賛神明之猷績以震天下以幸萬世有非
===
愚草茅之所能窺其萬一也雖然愚聞之
帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心自古
及今未有外心而可以爲盛德大業者也
觀我
太祖造觀心亭
召學士宋濂曰人心虛靈乗氣機出入操而
存之爲難朕罔敢自暇自逸我
皇上御製敬一箴曰敬怠純駁應驗頓殊徴諸
天人如鼓發桴大哉
punctuated:
至德之廣運，禮樂之重光，際天所覆，極地所載，咸蒙厚澤，與聖祖之功德先後一揆者，真足以對揚駿惠而熈播休靈矣。况於珥筆執經之彦，帷幄論思之老，必有以默窺彌綸天地之機緘，宏鋪幽賛神明之猷績，以震天下，以幸萬世，有非愚草茅之所能窺其萬一也。
雖然，愚聞之：帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。自古及今，未有外心而可以爲盛德大業者也。觀我太祖造觀心亭，召學士宋濂曰：「人心虛靈，乗氣機出入，操而存之爲難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」我皇上御製《敬一箴》曰：「敬怠純駁，應驗頓殊。徴諸天人，如鼓發桴。」大哉！
translation_en:
…the far-reaching operation of supreme virtue and the renewed brilliance of rites and music: throughout all that Heaven covers and Earth bears, all receive abundant favor. These achievements accord in every respect with the sagely ancestor’s merit and virtue, though accomplished in different times. They truly suffice to acknowledge and extol the great beneficence and gloriously spread its auspicious power. Moreover, the distinguished men who tuck writing brushes into their caps and hold the classics, and the elder counselors who deliberate in the imperial presence, must have means of silently discerning the hidden workings that encompass Heaven and Earth, and of amply setting forth the plans and accomplishments that mysteriously assist the spirits. Thereby they may stir all under Heaven and bring blessings to ten thousand generations. Such things lie beyond even the slightest glimpse that an ignorant rustic such as I can attain.
Nevertheless, I have heard that the government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and their Way is rooted in the mind. From antiquity to the present, no one has ever attained flourishing virtue and great achievements apart from the mind. Consider how our Taizu built the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind and summoned Academician Song Lian, saying: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. To grasp and preserve it is difficult. I dare not allow myself leisure or ease.” Our Emperor’s own Admonition on Reverence and Unity states: “Reverence and negligence, purity and admixture—their effects differ utterly. Test this in Heaven and humanity: it is like a drum responding to a drumstick [?].” How great …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
皇言與天爲一此與堯舜之精一執中禹湯文
武之祗台德先制事制心緝熈敬止不泄
不忘者無以異也愚聞之受命不于其天
于其人休符不于其祥于其仁然則
盛德大業之本原實出於此而愚也譬之天地
之不能摹其高深日月之不能摹其光耀
也傳曰君子之道本諸身徵諸庶民考諸
三王而不謬建諸天地而不悖質諸鬼神
而無疑百世以俟聖人而不惑此之謂大
===
信又曰唯天下至誠爲能盡其性能盡其
性則能盡人之性能盡人之性則能盡物
之性能盡物之性則可以賛天地之化育
可以賛天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
此之謂大順其惟
今日乎愚謹誦其盛以
獻焉
第二問
孫鳴世
punctuated:
皇言與天爲一，此與堯舜之精一執中，禹湯文武之祗台德先、制事制心、緝熈敬止、不泄不忘者，無以異也。愚聞之：受命不于其天，于其人；休符不于其祥，于其仁。然則盛德大業之本原，實出於此，而愚也，譬之天地之不能摹其高深，日月之不能摹其光耀也。傳曰：「君子之道，本諸身，徵諸庶民，考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑。」此之謂大信。又曰：「唯天下至誠，爲能盡其性；能盡其性，則能盡人之性；能盡人之性，則能盡物之性；能盡物之性，則可以賛天地之化育；可以賛天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。」此之謂大順。其惟今日乎！愚謹誦其盛以獻焉。

第二問
孫鳴世
translation_en:
…the imperial words are one with Heaven. This is no different from Yao and Shun’s refinement and single-mindedness in holding fast to the Mean, or from Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu’s reverently putting virtue first, regulating affairs and the mind, continuing in luminous reverence, and neither growing lax nor forgetting. I have heard that receiving the Mandate depends not on Heaven but on the people, and that auspicious signs lie not in portents but in benevolence. Thus the source of abundant virtue and great achievements truly lies here. Yet for me to describe it would be like attempting to portray the height and depth of Heaven and Earth, or the radiance of the sun and moon.

The transmitted text says: “The gentleman’s Way is rooted in his own person and verified among the common people. Tested against the Three Kings, it is without error; established before Heaven and Earth, it does not conflict with them; submitted to ghosts and spirits, it leaves no doubt; and even after waiting a hundred generations for a sage, it remains free from perplexity.” This is what is called great trustworthiness. It also says: “Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize his own nature. Able to realize his own nature fully, he can fully realize the nature of others. Able to realize the nature of others fully, he can fully realize the nature of things. Able to realize the nature of things fully, he can assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth. Able to assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, he can form a triad with Heaven and Earth.” This is what is called great accord. Surely this describes the present day! I respectfully praise this flourishing achievement and offer these words.

Second Policy Question
Sun Mingshi

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭劉批周子契易道之源固有以接
孔孟不傳之緖而屈子以忠愛之情契詩人之旨是亦未可以詞人視之
子能考究經旨深發二子之奥而末又以易詩之理求之吾心非見
道明而造詣深者不能道此繼屈周而下者子非楚之豪傑也邪
考試官敎諭姜批是深悟易詩之旨者
考試官敎授陸批究對詳悉
悟於易者深於易者也深於易者道與器
而已矣悟於詩者深於詩者也深於詩者
性與情而已矣昔者易之未作也非無易
===
也而易具於天地此道器之所繇形也詩
之未作也非無詩也而詩藏於天地此性
情之所繇出也是故易也者其天地有形
之畫乎聖人因而作之以通聖明之德以
類萬物之情先天下以開物後天下以成
務合四聖而歷三古闡造化而行鬼神而
易之道始章故曰易之爲書廣大悉備此
之謂也夫詩也者其天地自然之音乎聖
人因而刪之庶民歌之則以貢其俗君子
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭劉批：「周子契易道之源，固有以接孔孟不傳之緖；而屈子以忠愛之情契詩人之旨，是亦未可以詞人視之。子能考究經旨，深發二子之奥，而末又以易詩之理求之吾心，非見道明而造詣深者不能道此。繼屈周而下者，子非楚之豪傑也邪？」
考試官敎諭姜批：「是深悟易詩之旨者。」
考試官敎授陸批：「究對詳悉。」
悟於易者，深於易者也。深於易者，道與器而已矣。悟於詩者，深於詩者也。深於詩者，性與情而已矣。昔者易之未作也，非無易也，而易具於天地，此道器之所繇形也。詩之未作也，非無詩也，而詩藏於天地，此性情之所繇出也。是故易也者，其天地有形之畫乎？聖人因而作之，以通聖明之德，以類萬物之情，先天下以開物，後天下以成務，合四聖而歷三古，闡造化而行鬼神，而易之道始章。故曰：「易之爲書，廣大悉備。」此之謂也。夫詩也者，其天地自然之音乎？聖人因而刪之，庶民歌之則以貢其俗，君子
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Master Zhou grasped the source of the Way of the Changes, and thereby continued the thread of transmission from Confucius and Mencius that had been broken. Master Qu, through his feelings of loyalty and loving concern, grasped the intent of the poets of the Odes; he too cannot be regarded merely as a literary man. You have investigated the meaning of the classics and brought out the profound insights of these two masters. At the end, moreover, you seek the principles of the Changes and the Odes within our own minds. Only someone who sees the Way clearly and has attained profound understanding could say this. As a successor to Qu and Zhou, are you not an outstanding man of Chu?”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who deeply comprehends the meaning of the Changes and the Odes.”
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: “The investigation and response are thorough and detailed.”
Those who comprehend the Changes are those who have penetrated it deeply. What is profound in the Changes is simply the Way and concrete things. Those who comprehend the Odes are those who have penetrated it deeply. What is profound in the Odes is simply human nature and feelings. In antiquity, before the Changes was composed, it was not that there were no Changes: the Changes was already fully present in Heaven and Earth. This is how the Way and concrete things took form. Before the Odes was composed, it was not that there were no Odes: the Odes lay hidden within Heaven and Earth. This is whence human nature and feelings emerged. Thus, is not the Changes the visible delineation of Heaven and Earth? The sages composed it on this basis, to communicate the virtue of sagely illumination and classify the actual conditions of the myriad things; to go before all under Heaven in opening up understanding of things, and to follow all under Heaven in bringing affairs to completion. Combining the work of four sages across the three ages of antiquity, it elucidated the transformations of creation and gave effect to the workings of spirits. Only then did the Way of the Changes become manifest. Hence the saying: “As a book, the Changes is vast and great, encompassing everything.” This is what it means. As for the Odes, is it not the spontaneous voice of Heaven and Earth? The sage edited it on this basis. When the common people sing its poems, they thereby present their customs; when gentlemen …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賦之則以見其志邪正之所感也美刺之
所生也扶三綱而明五常動萬物而察庶
彙而詩之用始大故曰興於詩又曰不學
詩無以言此之謂也是故易之爲道也天
道也故夫不悟於易者則其學不足以知
天詩之爲道人道也故夫不悟於詩者則
其學不足以知人嗟乎學不足以知人不
足以知天如是而有作焉者皆妄也執事
有感於吾楚之有屈原周子而以易詩焉
===
問愚也抱遺經而究終始或者有一得焉
何可不就正之執事之前也夫周子之崛
起南服也學匪繇於師傳心不假於智索
其爲太極也建圖著書根極道要窺陰陽
五行之本推四時萬物之變使學者知主
靜之可以立極探性命鬼神之奧闡仁誠
義利之辨使學者知聖學之可以上達要
其淵源精粹以上繼孔孟之絶緒自今觀
之其曰無極太極無方無體之旨也動靜
punctuated:
賦之則以見其志，邪正之所感也，美刺之所生也。扶三綱而明五常，動萬物而察庶彙，而詩之用始大。故曰：「興於詩。」又曰：「不學詩，無以言。」此之謂也。是故易之爲道也，天道也，故夫不悟於易者，則其學不足以知天；詩之爲道，人道也，故夫不悟於詩者，則其學不足以知人。嗟乎！學不足以知人，不足以知天，如是而有作焉者，皆妄也。執事有感於吾楚之有屈原、周子，而以易、詩焉問。愚也抱遺經而究終始，或者有一得焉，何可不就正之執事之前也？
夫周子之崛起南服也，學匪繇於師傳，心不假於智索。其爲太極也，建圖著書，根極道要，窺陰陽五行之本，推四時萬物之變，使學者知主靜之可以立極；探性命鬼神之奧，闡仁誠義利之辨，使學者知聖學之可以上達。要其淵源精粹，以上繼孔孟之絶緒。自今觀之，其曰「無極太極」，無方無體之旨也；動靜
translation_en:
…when gentlemen recite the poems, they thereby reveal their aspirations. These poems are responses to what is deviant or upright, and from them arise praise and criticism. They uphold the Three Bonds and illuminate the Five Constant Virtues, move the myriad things and discern their many kinds; thus the utility of the Book of Odes becomes great. Hence the sayings, “Be stirred by the Odes,” and “Unless you study the Odes, you will have no means of speaking.” This is what they mean. Thus the Way embodied in the Book of Changes is the Way of Heaven: those who fail to comprehend the Changes lack the learning needed to understand Heaven. The Way embodied in the Book of Odes is the human Way: those who fail to comprehend the Odes lack the learning needed to understand humanity. Alas! If one’s learning is insufficient to understand either humanity or Heaven, anything one writes under such circumstances is misguided. Reflecting on the fact that our land of Chu produced Qu Yuan and Master Zhou, you have questioned me about the Changes and the Odes. In my humble study, I hold fast to the surviving classics and investigate their beginnings and ends. If perchance I have gained some insight, how could I fail to submit it to you for correction?
When Master Zhou rose to prominence in the southern regions, his learning did not derive from a teacher’s transmission, nor did his mind depend upon intellectual probing. In his treatment of the Supreme Ultimate, he constructed a diagram and composed a text, tracing the essentials of the Way to their roots. He discerned the foundations of yin, yang, and the Five Phases and investigated the transformations of the four seasons and the myriad things, enabling students to understand how giving primacy to stillness can establish the ultimate standard. He explored the mysteries of human nature, destiny, ghosts, and spirits, and elucidated humaneness and sincerity and the distinction between righteousness and profit, enabling students to understand how the learning of the sages can lead to higher understanding. In sum, the depth and purity of his learning enabled him to take up the severed line of transmission from Confucius and Mengzi. Viewed from the present, his words “Without Ultimate and yet Supreme Ultimate” express the meaning of having neither spatial bounds nor bodily form. Movement and stillness…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
互根一陰一陽之道也誠通誠復繼善成
性之義也五氣順布元亨利貞之體也綱
領宏濶而渾成條理整嚴而縝密雖不規
規於易也而易之道由是以粲然于世此
非易之遺乎胡五峯以為其功蓋在孔孟
之間者此也若文中子之賛易楊雄之太
玄祗見其妄矣而陸子靜猶詆非吾儒宗
㫖何邪蓋太極非有也自其至中至正者
而強名之也無極非無也自其無聲無臭
===
者而推本之也是故不言無極則太極之
體近於有物不言太極則無極之貞淪於
空寂其安能以為萬化之根柢乎子靜之
學不免於禪矣善乎北溪陳氏之言曰手
為圖筆為書而孔氏之傳復續然則易之
在楚也非以此邪屈原之為楚宗臣也嫉
上官之猜構遭聰聽之瞶亂其為離騷也
抒衷以寤主洗志於放言攄其忠君愛國
之誠心以寫其繾綣惻怛之情使人知吾
punctuated:
互根，一陰一陽之道也；誠通誠復，繼善成性之義也；五氣順布，元亨利貞之體也。綱領宏濶而渾成，條理整嚴而縝密。雖不規規於易也，而易之道由是以粲然于世，此非易之遺乎？胡五峯以為其功蓋在孔孟之間者，此也。若文中子之賛易、楊雄之太玄，祗見其妄矣。而陸子靜猶詆非吾儒宗㫖，何邪？蓋太極非有也，自其至中至正者而強名之也；無極非無也，自其無聲無臭者而推本之也。是故不言無極，則太極之體近於有物；不言太極，則無極之貞淪於空寂。其安能以為萬化之根柢乎？子靜之學不免於禪矣。善乎北溪陳氏之言曰：「手為圖，筆為書，而孔氏之傳復續。」然則易之在楚也，非以此邪？
屈原之為楚宗臣也，嫉上官之猜構，遭聰聽之瞶亂。其為離騷也，抒衷以寤主，洗志於放言，攄其忠君愛國之誠心，以寫其繾綣惻怛之情，使人知吾
translation_en:
…are rooted in one another: this is the Way of alternating yin and yang. Sincerity’s outgoing activity and return express the meaning of goodness continuing and nature becoming complete. The orderly diffusion of the five vital energies embodies origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy. The main principles are expansive and form an integrated whole; their articulation is orderly, rigorous, and meticulous. Although he did not confine himself narrowly to the Book of Changes, through this the Way of the Changes shone forth in the world. Is this not the legacy of the Changes? This is why Hu Wufeng judged that his achievement ranked between those of Confucius and Mencius. As for Wenzhongzi’s Praise of the Changes and Yang Xiong’s Supreme Mystery, one sees only their presumption. Yet Lu Zijing still denounced his teaching as contrary to the essential principles of our Confucian tradition. Why?
The Supreme Ultimate is not an existent thing: the name is provisionally imposed on that which is perfectly central and perfectly correct. The Ultimateless is not nothingness: its source is traced back through that which has neither sound nor smell. Thus, without speaking of the Ultimateless, the substance of the Supreme Ultimate comes close to being a tangible thing; without speaking of the Supreme Ultimate, the constancy of the Ultimateless sinks into empty quiescence. How then could it serve as the root of all transformations? Zijing’s learning cannot escape the influence of Chan Buddhism. Well said are the words of Chen Beixi: “With his hands he made the diagram, and with his brush he wrote the book, and the transmission of Confucius was renewed.” Is this not, then, how the Changes came to be present in Chu?
Qu Yuan, an eminent minister of Chu, detested Shangguan’s jealous plotting and suffered when his ruler’s hearing was deafened and confused. In composing Encountering Sorrow (Li sao), he poured out his innermost feelings to awaken his lord and purified his resolve through unrestrained expression. He unfolded his sincere devotion to his ruler and love for his state, giving voice to his feelings of attachment and anguish, so that people might understand that my…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
身之無所逃而不流於怨出其篤古博物
之偉詞以極其跌宕激發之氣使知吾情
之有以自遏而不涉於怒文約而詞微志
潔而行廉要其清惠狷潔雖與日月爭光
可也自今觀之其曰耿介祗敬之旨則雅
頌之奧也猖狂顛隕之詞則規誦之音也
虬鳯芷艾之譬則比興之義也彭咸伯夷
之思則廉狷之行也稱文小而指極大取
類邇而見義遠命意託物取諸其心雖以
===
迫切忍死而終不忘乎君臣之大義此非
詩之遺者乎淮南謂其國風好色而不淫
小雅怨誹而不亂而以離騷可謂兼之者
此也文中子之續詩束晳之補亡祗見其
不知量矣而楊雄乃撫其文作反離騷自
崏山投諸江流以弔之何邪蓋屈原之過
過於忠者也屈原之忠忠之過者也故有
原之地而無其才則不可以語騷有原之
才而無其心則不能以知騷雄乃自取於
punctuated: 身之無所逃而不流於怨，出其篤古博物之偉詞，以極其跌宕激發之氣，使知吾情之有以自遏而不涉於怒。文約而詞微，志潔而行廉，要其清惠狷潔，雖與日月爭光可也。自今觀之，其曰耿介祗敬之旨，則雅頌之奧也；猖狂顛隕之詞，則規誦之音也；虬鳯芷艾之譬，則比興之義也；彭咸伯夷之思，則廉狷之行也。稱文小而指極大，取類邇而見義遠，命意託物，取諸其心，雖以迫切忍死，而終不忘乎君臣之大義，此非詩之遺者乎？淮南謂其國風好色而不淫，小雅怨誹而不亂，而以離騷可謂兼之者，此也。文中子之續詩，束晳之補亡，祗見其不知量矣。而楊雄乃撫其文，作反離騷，自崏山投諸江流以弔之，何邪？蓋屈原之過，過於忠者也；屈原之忠，忠之過者也。故有原之地而無其才，則不可以語騷；有原之才而無其心，則不能以知騷。雄乃自取於
translation_en: …that I have nowhere to escape, yet without lapsing into resentment. He brought forth magnificent expressions of his devotion to antiquity and his broad knowledge of things, giving full scope to his exuberant, impassioned spirit, so that others would understand how his feelings could restrain themselves without crossing into anger. His writing is concise and his diction subtle; his aspirations are pure and his conduct incorruptible. In sum, such are his purity, benevolence, principled restraint, and integrity that he may indeed vie in brilliance with the sun and moon. Viewed from the present, his expressions of uprightness and reverence embody the profound meaning of the Elegantiae and Hymns; his words of wild abandon and downfall carry the sound of admonitory recitation; his comparisons involving dragons and phoenixes, angelica and mugwort embody the principles of comparison and evocative imagery; and his thoughts of Peng Xian and Bo Yi embody incorruptible and principled conduct. The things his writing names are small, but its import is exceedingly great; his analogies draw on things close at hand, but the meaning they reveal reaches far. He framed his meanings and lodged them in things, drawing everything from his own heart. Although driven to extremity and enduring death, he never forgot the great moral obligation between ruler and minister. Is this not a surviving legacy of the Book of Odes? This is what the Prince of Huainan meant when he said that the Airs of the States delight in beauty without becoming licentious, and the Lesser Elegantiae voice resentment and criticism without becoming disorderly, and that Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) could be said to unite both qualities. Master Wenzhong’s Continuation of the Odes and Shu Xi’s Supplementing the Lost Odes merely reveal their failure to recognize their own limitations. Yet Yang Xiong, taking up Qu Yuan’s text, composed Refuting Encountering Sorrow and cast it into the river from Mount Min to lament him. Why? Qu Yuan’s fault was an excess of loyalty; Qu Yuan’s loyalty was loyalty carried to excess. Thus, someone who occupies Qu Yuan’s position but lacks his talent cannot discuss Encountering Sorrow; someone who possesses his talent but lacks his heart cannot understand it. Yet Yang Xiong brought upon himself…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
投閣之辱豈龍蛇之謂乎善乎臨川吳氏
之言曰詩亡而後楚騷作然則謂詩之在
楚也非以此邪厥後程子因之有易傳之
作朱子因之有本義之作有太極通書之
註其所以發天人之奥洞性命之原究事
物之賾統倫理之全粹乎亡以復加也使
學者知吾心之爲至靈可以窮神知化知
吾性之爲至善可以爲堯舜周公孔子知
吾道之爲至大可以位育天地起往聖於
===
一綫覺來學於無窮故當時有再開渾淪
之語至於光風霽月玉色金聲之稱未爲
知周子者也朱子之作詩傳自謂可以無
遺憾至其離騷之解則曰不敢直以詞人
視之也夫推原之爲心雖其志行或過於
中庸辭藻或離於經訓然使忠臣孝子怨
妾逐婦不幸而處其變則不肯以其身之
所遭而自懈於善幸而或悟其非則有以
復其民彝天性之常而各止其所此其與
punctuated: 投閣之辱，豈龍蛇之謂乎？善乎臨川吳氏之言曰：「詩亡而後楚騷作。」然則謂詩之在楚也，非以此邪？厥後程子因之有《易傳》之作，朱子因之有《本義》之作，有《太極》《通書》之註。其所以發天人之奥，洞性命之原，究事物之賾，統倫理之全，粹乎亡以復加也。使學者知吾心之爲至靈，可以窮神知化；知吾性之爲至善，可以爲堯舜周公孔子；知吾道之爲至大，可以位育天地，起往聖於一綫，覺來學於無窮。故當時有再開渾淪之語。至於光風霽月、玉色金聲之稱，未爲知周子者也。朱子之作《詩傳》，自謂可以無遺憾；至其《離騷》之解，則曰：「不敢直以詞人視之也。」夫推原之爲心，雖其志行或過於中庸，辭藻或離於經訓，然使忠臣孝子、怨妾逐婦，不幸而處其變，則不肯以其身之所遭而自懈於善；幸而或悟其非，則有以復其民彝天性之常，而各止其所。此其與
translation_en:
…the disgrace of leaping from the pavilion: could this be what is meant by the dragon and snake [?]? Well said are the words of Master Wu of Linchuan: “Only after the Poetry had vanished did the Songs of Chu arise.” Is this not why one speaks of the Poetry as surviving in Chu?

Thereafter, Master Cheng, following this, composed his Commentary on the Changes; Master Zhu, following this, composed the Original Meaning and commentaries on the Supreme Ultimate and the Comprehensive Writings. These works disclose the mysteries of Heaven and humanity, penetrate the source of human nature and destiny, investigate the intricacies of things and affairs, and encompass the entirety of ethical relationships and principles. Their purity could not be surpassed. They enable learners to recognize that our minds possess the utmost spiritual intelligence and can fathom the numinous and understand transformation; that our nature is supremely good and that we can become Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, or Confucius; and that our Way is supremely great and can establish Heaven and Earth in their proper places and foster their unfolding. They revive the former sages’ legacy where it hangs by a single thread and awaken future learners without end. Thus people at the time spoke of “opening primordial unity anew.” As for praising Master Zhou as “a clear breeze and a moon after rain” or as having “the lustre of jade and the resonance of metal,” such words do not yet amount to knowing him.

When Master Zhu composed his Commentary on the Poetry, he said that he could leave no regrets. Yet in his explanation of Encountering Sorrow (Li Sao), he said: “I dare not regard him merely as a literary writer.” Now, if we trace Qu Yuan’s intentions to their source, although his aspirations and conduct may at times have exceeded the mean, and his ornate language may at times have departed from the teachings of the Classics, loyal ministers and filial sons, resentful concubines and repudiated wives who unhappily find themselves in such adverse circumstances will not, because of what has befallen them, allow their commitment to goodness to slacken. If, fortunately, they come to recognize their errors, they will have the means to restore the enduring norms of human relationships and their Heaven-given nature, each coming to rest in the proper place. In this, compared with …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
易之吉凶悔吝詩之勸戒美刺也何以異
焉然則若原者其可以詞人視之乎雖然
易詩無二理性命同一源易之元吉卽詩
之無邪也詩之和平卽易之時中也誠能
易簡以一其心豈弟以平其志觀於井以
辨吾之義觀於巽以行吾之權本之國風
以達其情正之雅頌以要其極則易詩之
理吾心一以貫之無遺而易不在於四聖
詩不在於三百篇矣惜拘於象者不知剛
===
柔相推之義泥於數者不知進退離合之
神以文害辭者昧抑揚反覆之理以辭害
意者忘監戒懲勸之機此易詩之理所以
不得也故曰神而明之存乎其人又曰以
意逆志是爲得之學易詩者固求之吾心
焉耳
第三問
魏裳
同考試官教諭阮 批 論著古人持身處事最爲
punctuated:
易之吉凶悔吝，詩之勸戒美刺也，何以異焉？然則若原者，其可以詞人視之乎？雖然，易詩無二理，性命同一源。易之元吉，卽詩之無邪也；詩之和平，卽易之時中也。誠能易簡以一其心，豈弟以平其志，觀於井以辨吾之義，觀於巽以行吾之權，本之國風以達其情，正之雅頌以要其極，則易詩之理，吾心一以貫之無遺，而易不在於四聖，詩不在於三百篇矣。惜拘於象者，不知剛柔相推之義；泥於數者，不知進退離合之神；以文害辭者，昧抑揚反覆之理；以辭害意者，忘監戒懲勸之機。此易詩之理所以不得也。故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」又曰：「以意逆志。」是爲得之。學易詩者，固求之吾心焉耳。

第三問
魏裳
同考試官教諭阮批：論著古人持身處事，最爲
translation_en:
…how does this differ from the good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation in the Book of Changes, or the encouragement, admonition, praise, and criticism in the Book of Odes? Can someone such as Qu Yuan, then, be regarded merely as a literary writer? Nevertheless, the Changes and the Odes do not have two different principles; human nature and Heaven’s mandate share one source. The “supreme good fortune” of the Changes is precisely the “absence of waywardness” of the Odes; the harmony and balance of the Odes are precisely the timely attainment of the mean in the Changes. If one can truly unify one’s mind through ease and simplicity, calm one’s intentions through gentleness and good cheer, contemplate the Well hexagram to discern what is right for oneself, and contemplate the Gentle hexagram to exercise discretion; if one takes the Airs of the States as the basis for expressing one’s feelings and rectifies them through the Court Hymns and Sacrificial Songs so as to attain their ultimate standard, then one’s mind will comprehend the principles of the Changes and the Odes through a single unifying thread, leaving nothing out. The Changes will no longer reside solely in the four sages, nor the Odes solely in their three hundred poems.

Regrettably, those constrained by images do not understand the meaning of the hard and the yielding impelling one another; those mired in numbers do not understand the wondrous workings of advance and retreat, separation and union. Those who let individual words obscure phrases fail to understand the principles of modulation and repeated expression; those who let phrases obscure meaning forget the workings of warning, admonition, correction, and encouragement. This is why they fail to grasp the principles of the Changes and the Odes. Thus it is said, “Making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it depends upon the person.” It is also said, “Use one’s understanding to meet the author’s intent.” This is what it means to grasp them. Those who study the Changes and the Odes must simply seek within their own minds.

Third Question
Wei Shang
Associate Examiner Ruan, Instructor, comments: “In discussing how the ancients conducted themselves and dealt with affairs, this is most…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
精詳如身歷其間可以占子它日之風節和平矣佳士佳士
同考試官教諭林批學知古人用心到處敬服
同考試官學正何批不激不隘蓋有用之士
考試官教諭姜批議論明當誦之朗然
考試官教授陸批詞旨古雅
居以明志其失也病於隘君子則以時權
之而已矣行以應世其失也病於激君子
則以道裁之而已矣夫居以明志也則澹
心以遺榮閟影以全真非獨任其身之所
===
至以娛悅其性而或托焉以明其不事之
節視世之慕不槩于其懷是亦高矣然有
時焉否則適以為隘也夫行以應世也則
忘身以瘁國秉道以嫉邪蓋其蹇蹇匪躬
之義即有齟齬而不合反以起其狷介憤
鬱之氣而動乎其心雖若不可犯矣然有
道焉否則適以為激也是故明志而病於
隘伏其身而不見雖其風誼之足以廉頑
立懦而樹聲稱於天下要之非適用之體
punctuated:
精詳，如身歷其間，可以占子它日之風節和平矣。佳士！佳士！
同考試官教諭林批：學知古人用心到處，敬服。
同考試官學正何批：不激不隘，蓋有用之士。
考試官教諭姜批：議論明當，誦之朗然。
考試官教授陸批：詞旨古雅。

居以明志，其失也病於隘，君子則以時權之而已矣；行以應世，其失也病於激，君子則以道裁之而已矣。夫居以明志也，則澹心以遺榮，閟影以全真，非獨任其身之所至以娛悅其性，而或托焉以明其不事之節，視世之慕不槩于其懷，是亦高矣。然有時焉，否則適以為隘也。夫行以應世也，則忘身以瘁國，秉道以嫉邪，蓋其蹇蹇匪躬之義，即有齟齬而不合，反以起其狷介憤鬱之氣，而動乎其心，雖若不可犯矣。然有道焉，否則適以為激也。是故明志而病於隘，伏其身而不見，雖其風誼之足以廉頑立懦，而樹聲稱於天下，要之非適用之體
translation_en:
…precise and detailed, as though you had personally lived through those circumstances. From this one can anticipate the integrity and even temper you will display in years to come. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: Through your learning you understand the full extent of the ancients’ intentions [?]. I admire this respectfully.
Associate Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: Neither extreme nor narrow-minded: surely a man capable of useful service.
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: The arguments are clear and sound; read aloud, they ring out lucidly.
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: The language and purport possess an antique elegance.

In retirement one makes one’s aspirations clear; its failing lies in narrowness. The gentleman merely weighs it according to the times. In public action one responds to the world; its failing lies in excess. The gentleman merely regulates it according to the Way. In retirement, making one’s aspirations clear means quieting the heart to leave worldly honors behind and concealing oneself to preserve one’s true nature. It is not merely letting oneself go where one will to delight one’s disposition; one may also use retirement to manifest one’s principled refusal to serve. What the world covets finds no place in one’s heart: this, too, is lofty. Yet there is a proper time for it; otherwise it serves only to produce narrowness. In public action, responding to the world means forgetting oneself in exhausting service to the state and holding fast to the Way in abhorrence of evil. Such is the principle of steadfast service without thought of oneself. Even when one encounters discord and incompatibility, these instead stir one’s uncompromising rectitude and pent-up indignation, agitating the heart until one seems to brook no affront. Yet there is a Way to govern this; otherwise it serves only to produce excess. Thus, when making one’s aspirations clear becomes afflicted with narrowness, one hides oneself and does not appear in public. Although the moral influence of one’s conduct may make the obstinate scrupulous and the weak resolute, establishing one’s reputation throughout the realm, in the final reckoning this is no foundation for practical service…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也應世而病於激執其道以求勝固其心
之欲有為於天下而奮焉以必伸其志要
之非成務之學也非君子之所尚也是故
隱居求志行義達道時之謂也道隆身隆
道詘身詘道之謂也愚於執事之問而得
二人焉其漢之諸葛孔明宋之程伯子乎
愚請歷陳之而執事裁焉夫季子以耕野
而堅守延陵之節魯仲連以揮金而併却
存趙之封高帝不能致采芝之四皓光皇
===
不能屈披裘之子陵執事固疑其隘矣乃
若子房建誅秦蹙項之謀孔明輔三分鼎
峙之業淵明班荆於柴桑康節乘車於河
洛比之四子則又不遠遁以為潔者矣要
之均以明志也蓋嘗論之季子矢子臧之
義懼父子之行私不可訓也况其周旋於
諸樊父子兄弟之間其亦逆知釁端之必
起者乎才近伯夷美其節也淵明抒荆軻
之詠守君臣之大義不可逃也况其書甲
punctuated:
也。應世而病於激，執其道以求勝，固其心之欲有為於天下，而奮焉以必伸其志，要之非成務之學也，非君子之所尚也。是故「隱居求志，行義達道」，時之謂也；「道隆身隆，道詘身詘」，道之謂也。愚於執事之問而得二人焉，其漢之諸葛孔明、宋之程伯子乎？愚請歷陳之，而執事裁焉。
夫季子以耕野而堅守延陵之節，魯仲連以揮金而併却存趙之封，高帝不能致采芝之四皓，光皇不能屈披裘之子陵，執事固疑其隘矣。乃若子房建誅秦蹙項之謀，孔明輔三分鼎峙之業，淵明班荆於柴桑，康節乘車於河洛，比之四子，則又不遠遁以為潔者矣。要之，均以明志也。蓋嘗論之：季子矢子臧之義，懼父子之行私不可訓也。况其周旋於諸樊父子兄弟之間，其亦逆知釁端之必起者乎？才近伯夷，美其節也。淵明抒荆軻之詠，守君臣之大義不可逃也。况其書甲
translation_en:
… To engage with the world yet fall into excessive vehemence, clinging to one’s principles in pursuit of victory, certainly expresses a desire to accomplish something in the realm and a determination to realize one’s aspirations. Ultimately, however, this is not learning that brings affairs to completion, nor is it what the gentleman esteems. Thus, “dwelling in seclusion to pursue one’s aspirations, and practicing righteousness to give effect to the Way” concerns the proper timing; “when the Way flourishes, one advances; when the Way is suppressed, one withdraws” concerns the Way. In considering your question, I humbly find two men who exemplify this: might they be Zhuge Kongming of the Han and Cheng Bozi of the Song? Allow me to set out my account, and leave the judgment to you.
Jizi, tilling in the countryside, steadfastly maintained his integrity as lord of Yanling. Lu Zhonglian, waving aside gold, also refused the enfeoffment offered for saving Zhao. Emperor Gao could not summon the Four Hoary Elders, who gathered fungi; Emperor Guangwu could not bend the will of Ziling, clad in a fur robe. You certainly suspect these men of being too narrow. Yet Zifang devised plans to destroy Qin and crush Xiang; Kongming assisted in establishing a realm that stood as one of three, like the legs of a tripod; Yuanming spread thorn branches to sit upon at Chaisang; and Kangjie rode in a carriage through the He–Luo region. Compared with the preceding four, these men did not seek purity by withdrawing far from the world. Ultimately, all sought to make their aspirations clear.
I have considered the matter as follows. Jizi pledged himself to Zizang’s standard of righteousness, fearing that private favoritism between father and son could not serve as a model. Moreover, moving as he did among Zhufan and his family’s fathers, sons, and brothers, did he not also foresee that grounds for conflict would inevitably arise? To say that his worth approached Boyi’s is to praise his integrity. Yuanming expressed himself in his poem on Jing Ke, holding that the great moral obligation between ruler and subject could not be evaded. Moreover, his writing of the cyclical character jia …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
子於永初之後其可得而臣乎處士而繫
之晉褒其志也四皓之逃漢蓋畏高帝以
施其嫚罵之辱者歌唐虞之日遠其志甚
高而卒以遺其名然一出而漢鼎定豈膏
肓之錮哉子房之報韓蓋借漢以泄其博
浪之憤者棧道之燒其志不遂而卒以輔
成漢業然辟穀而不爲漢留焉非止足之
志哉以懷仁輔義之子陵而不能得之光
武諫議之拜豈伊尹呂之志乎故不若桐江
===
之一絲猶足以九鼎於漢也以臥龍之孔
明而能得之於昭烈魚水之投况帝室之
胄乎故不若出而讎跨有荊益之言尚足
以興漢也仲連之輕世肆志非以爲傲也
排難解紛得之談笑不謂其有經世之才
乎堯夫之與常秩同召非所以待高賢也
内聖外王之學聞於天下豈安樂先生之
志邪此愚之所謂以時權之者也安可以
爲盡隘乎汲黯之嫉惡太甚李膺之持議
punctuated: 子於永初之後，其可得而臣乎？處士而繫之晉，褒其志也。四皓之逃漢，蓋畏高帝以施其嫚罵之辱者。歌唐虞之日遠，其志甚高，而卒以遺其名。然一出而漢鼎定，豈膏肓之錮哉？子房之報韓，蓋借漢以泄其博浪之憤者。棧道之燒，其志不遂，而卒以輔成漢業。然辟穀而不爲漢留焉，非止足之志哉？以懷仁輔義之子陵，而不能得之光武諫議之拜，豈伊尹呂之志乎？故不若桐江之一絲，猶足以九鼎於漢也。以臥龍之孔明，而能得之於昭烈魚水之投，况帝室之胄乎？故不若出而讎跨有荊益之言，尚足以興漢也。仲連之輕世肆志，非以爲傲也。排難解紛，得之談笑，不謂其有經世之才乎？堯夫之與常秩同召，非所以待高賢也。内聖外王之學聞於天下，豈安樂先生之志邪？此愚之所謂以時權之者也，安可以爲盡隘乎？汲黯之嫉惡太甚，李膺之持議
translation_en:
…using cyclical dates after the beginning of the Yongchu era: could he possibly have been made a subject of the new dynasty? To identify him, though a scholar out of office, with the Jin was to commend his resolve.

The Four Hoary Elders withdrew from service under the Han, presumably fearing that Emperor Gao would subject them to the humiliation of his insolent abuse. They sang of how distant the days of Tang Yao and Yu Shun had become; their aspirations were lofty indeed, and in the end they left lasting names. Yet their single emergence secured the Han dynasty. Could their withdrawal have been an incurable fixation?

Zifang sought vengeance for Han, borrowing the strength of the Han dynasty to vent his anger over Bolang. When the plank road was burned, his ambition remained unfulfilled; in the end he helped establish the Han imperial enterprise. Yet he abstained from grain and would not remain in Han service. Was this not the resolve of one who knew when to stop and be content?

Ziling cherished benevolence and upheld righteousness, yet even Guangwu’s appointment of him as a Remonstrant could not win him over. Were his aspirations those of Yi Yin and Lü Shang [?]? Thus nothing was better than his single fishing line on the Tong River: even this carried the weight of the Nine Tripods for the Han.

Kongming, the Crouching Dragon, found in Zhaolie a congenial relationship like that of fish and water; moreover, Zhaolie was a scion of the imperial house. Thus nothing was better than to emerge and fulfill his proposal to occupy both Jing and Yi, which could still have brought about a restoration of the Han.

Zhonglian’s disdain for worldly standing and free pursuit of his aspirations did not spring from arrogance. He resolved difficulties and disentangled disputes amid conversation and laughter. Would one not say that he possessed the talents to put the world in order?

To summon Yaofu together with Chang Zhi was no way to treat an eminent worthy. His learning in the way of inward sagehood and outward kingship was renowned throughout the realm; could such a summons have accorded with the aspirations of the Master of Peace and Joy?

This is what I, in my humble view, call weighing one’s course according to the times. How could these men all be judged narrow-minded? Ji An’s hatred of evil was excessive; Li Ying’s adherence to his judgments…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
豈獨以德政著邪韓愈祝融一登而雲爲
開霽正直之所動也百世之師誦美於蘇
軾此豈獨以文章名邪寇準道州之行憫
剛直之弗容也然而澶淵一役談笑却虜
而天下服其忠吾乆不見寇準豈人君之
言哉歐陽脩夷陵之謫知政事之可以澤
物也卒而參議大政以風節自持而天下
稱其賢如歐陽脩何處得來盖亦見知於
明主矣凡此者皆遺澤之著于楚至于今
===
不衰也以產于楚者言之尹吉甫發物則
之詠廣文武之憲以輔成周宣中興之烈
可謂全才矣周子程子闡六經不傳之秘
接孔孟垂絕之緒使斯道粲然大明於世
可謂聖學矣黃香博學經典有天下無雙
之謠至孝之稱盖有本之學也歐陽玄屢
典制語有卓然名世之譽廉平之政盖有
用之才也蔣琬托志忠純負社稷之器休
休樂善人服其量司馬徽風致清雅有氷
punctuated:
豈獨以德政著邪？韓愈祝融一登，而雲爲開霽，正直之所動也。「百世之師」，誦美於蘇軾，此豈獨以文章名邪？寇準道州之行，憫剛直之弗容也。然而澶淵一役，談笑却虜，而天下服其忠。「吾乆不見寇準」，豈人君之言哉？歐陽脩夷陵之謫，知政事之可以澤物也。卒而參議大政，以風節自持，而天下稱其賢。「如歐陽脩何處得來」，盖亦見知於明主矣。凡此者，皆遺澤之著于楚，至于今不衰也。
以產于楚者言之，尹吉甫發物則之詠，廣文武之憲，以輔成周宣中興之烈，可謂全才矣。周子、程子闡六經不傳之秘，接孔孟垂絕之緒，使斯道粲然大明於世，可謂聖學矣。黃香博學經典，有天下無雙之謠、至孝之稱，盖有本之學也。歐陽玄屢典制語，有卓然名世之譽、廉平之政，盖有用之才也。蔣琬托志忠純，負社稷之器，休休樂善，人服其量。司馬徽風致清雅，有氷
translation_en:
…could it have been solely for virtuous government that he was renowned? When Han Yu ascended Zhurong Peak, the clouds parted and the sky cleared: this was the response his uprightness evoked. Su Shi praised him as “a teacher for a hundred generations.” Could his fame have rested solely on his writings? Kou Zhun’s journey to Daozhou evokes sorrow that his unbending integrity could not be tolerated. Yet at the battle of Chanyuan he repelled the enemy amid conversation and laughter, and all under Heaven admired his loyalty. “I have not seen Kou Zhun for a long time”—could these have been a ruler’s words [?]? In Ouyang Xiu’s banishment to Yiling, we see how government can confer benefits upon others. Eventually he participated in deliberations on the great affairs of state, maintaining his integrity, and all under Heaven acclaimed his worth. “Where could one find another Ouyang Xiu?” He too, evidently, won recognition from an enlightened ruler. All these men left conspicuous beneficent legacies in Chu, which remain undiminished to this day.
As for those born in Chu, Yin Jifu composed the ode on the inherent norms of things and extended the models of Kings Wen and Wu, helping King Xuan of Zhou accomplish the glorious restoration of his dynasty. He may be called a man of comprehensive talents. Master Zhou and Master Cheng elucidated the hidden meanings of the Six Classics that had ceased to be transmitted, and carried forward the nearly broken succession of Confucius and Mencius, making this Way shine brilliantly in the world. Their learning may be called the learning of the sages. Huang Xiang was broadly learned in the classics; a popular song proclaimed him unequalled under Heaven, and he was celebrated for consummate filial devotion. His learning indeed had a firm foundation. Ouyang Xuan repeatedly took charge of drafting imperial pronouncements. He enjoyed an outstanding reputation in his age and governed with integrity and impartiality: his was indeed talent put to practical use. Jiang Wan set his aspirations on loyalty and purity and possessed the capacity to sustain the state. Generous and delighting in goodness, he won others’ admiration for his magnanimity. Sima Hui’s bearing was refined and elegant; he had an ice-like …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
鑑之稱伏龍鳳雛人服其明黃瓊位居公
輔首奏貪汙忠鯁之氣重於海內岑文本
官至中書不營產業恭儉之節比之羔羊
馮京發自鄂渚登三魁之選而却張堯佐
之嬖倖阻王安石之新法范祖禹謂其有
中立不倚之操者此也宋庠宋祁本自安
陸應竝魁之讖而庠之風操祁之文藻宋
史謂其與陳堯咨堯叟為近之者此也胡
宏讀書於衡岳而知言一書真道學之樞
===
要制治之蓍龜也張栻講學於長沙而義
利一辨真仡仡乎其任道之勇卓卓乎其
立心之高也凡此者皆遺範之在于楚不
可一日忘也夫古人有言太上立德其次
立功其次立言斯之謂不朽愚以為執事
之所問備矣顧立志如何耳賈誼韓愈非
純於道者也然誼之治安策愈之原道其
大不過乎君臣父子之分仁義禮樂之指
其微不出乎飲食裘葛之常斗斛權量之
punctuated:
鑑之稱，伏龍、鳳雛，人服其明。黃瓊位居公輔，首奏貪汙，忠鯁之氣重於海內。岑文本官至中書，不營產業，恭儉之節比之羔羊。馮京發自鄂渚，登三魁之選，而却張堯佐之嬖倖，阻王安石之新法，范祖禹謂其有中立不倚之操者，此也。宋庠、宋祁本自安陸，應竝魁之讖，而庠之風操、祁之文藻，《宋史》謂其與陳堯咨、堯叟為近之者，此也。胡宏讀書於衡岳，而《知言》一書，真道學之樞要、制治之蓍龜也。張栻講學於長沙，而義利一辨，真仡仡乎其任道之勇，卓卓乎其立心之高也。凡此者，皆遺範之在于楚，不可一日忘也。
夫古人有言：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言，斯之謂不朽。」愚以為執事之所問備矣，顧立志如何耳。賈誼、韓愈非純於道者也，然誼之《治安策》、愈之《原道》，其大不過乎君臣父子之分、仁義禮樂之指，其微不出乎飲食裘葛之常、斗斛權量之
translation_en:
…a reputation as a clear mirror of discernment. His recognition of the “Crouching Dragon” and the “Phoenix Fledgling” won people's admiration for his insight. Huang Qiong held office among the highest ministers and took the lead in impeaching corrupt officials; his loyal and forthright spirit commanded respect throughout the realm. Cen Wenben rose to serve as Secretariat Director and did not build up private estates; his reverence and frugality were likened to the virtues celebrated in “The Lamb's Fur.” Feng Jing emerged from Ezhu and placed first in all three examinations. He resisted the undue favor enjoyed by Zhang Yaozuo and opposed Wang Anshi's New Policies. These were the grounds on which Fan Zuyu credited him with the integrity to stand in the center without leaning to either side. Song Xiang and Song Qi originally came from Anlu and fulfilled the prophecy that both would take first place. It was for Xiang's character and integrity and Qi's literary brilliance that the History of the Song compared them to Chen Yaozi and Chen Yaosou. Hu Hong studied at Hengyue, and his book Understanding Words (Zhiyan) is truly a key to the Learning of the Way and an oracle for establishing good government. Zhang Shi taught at Changsha; his discrimination between righteousness and profit truly displays his mighty courage in taking responsibility for the Way and the lofty resolve of his heart. All these are exemplary legacies preserved in Chu, which must not be forgotten for even a single day.
The ancients said: “Highest is the establishment of virtue; next comes the establishment of achievement; next comes the establishment of words. This is what is called immortality.” In my humble view, what you have asked about is fully encompassed here; it remains only to consider how one sets one's aspirations. Jia Yi and Han Yu were not wholly pure in their understanding of the Way. Yet in Jia Yi's Policy Essay on Order and Security (Zhi'an ce) and Han Yu's An Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao), the broadest concerns extend no further than the distinctions between ruler and minister, father and son, and the purport of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music; their smallest concerns remain within the everyday matters of food and drink, fur and hempen clothing, and the … of measures of capacity and standards of weight…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
細斯其爲用已廣矣乃若周子程子純於
道者也則寧學聖人而未至不欲以一善
而成名寧以一物不被爲己病不欲以一
時之利爲己功斯其爲體也宏矣斯尚友
之誼而士之本務也持此以往廟堂宣其
猷謨疆場樹其勛烈論議効其謇諤黼黻
崇其渾粹則固諸君子之所長者爾幸執
事進而教之
第五問
===
羅瑶
同考試官教諭包批抹荒不如備荒任法不如任
人子條答激切詳密可謂通世務者佳士佳士
同考試官教諭周批議論精確文辭古雅末言興
利二事尤楚人對病之藥敬服敬服
考試官教諭姜批有識尤可以用世者
考試官教授陸批通達治體鑿鑿可行
拯時之權道貴通變經國之理義在遠猷
夫天下無不變之時智者捄之以法以察
punctuated:
細，斯其爲用已廣矣。乃若周子、程子，純於道者也，則寧學聖人而未至，不欲以一善而成名；寧以一物不被爲己病，不欲以一時之利爲己功。斯其爲體也宏矣。斯尚友之誼，而士之本務也。持此以往，廟堂宣其猷謨，疆場樹其勛烈，論議効其謇諤，黼黻崇其渾粹，則固諸君子之所長者爾。幸執事進而教之。

第五問

羅瑶

同考試官教諭包批：抹荒不如備荒，任法不如任人。子條答激切詳密，可謂通世務者。佳士！佳士！

同考試官教諭周批：議論精確，文辭古雅。末言興利二事，尤楚人對病之藥。敬服！敬服！

考試官教諭姜批：有識，尤可以用世者。

考試官教授陸批：通達治體，鑿鑿可行。

拯時之權，道貴通變；經國之理，義在遠猷。夫天下無不變之時，智者捄之以法，以察
translation_en:
…such minute particulars: their practical application was already broad indeed. As for Master Zhou and Master Cheng, who were pure in their adherence to the Way, they preferred to study the sages even without attaining their level, rather than win fame through a single good deed. They preferred to regard any single creature left untouched by their beneficence as their own failing, rather than claim a temporary benefit as their own achievement. How expansive, then, was their fundamental substance! This is the meaning of taking the ancients as friends, and the essential duty of a scholar. Proceeding on this basis, you gentlemen may advance your plans and counsels at court, establish illustrious achievements on the frontiers, display forthright remonstrance in deliberation, and exalt wholeness and purity in literary embellishment. These are assuredly your particular strengths. I hope that you, honored sirs, will further instruct me.

Fifth Question

Luo Yao 羅瑶

Comment by Associate Examiner Bao, Instructor: Dealing with famine [?] is inferior to preparing against famine; relying on laws is inferior to relying on people. Your point-by-point response is impassioned and incisive, detailed and thorough. You may indeed be called someone who understands the affairs of the world. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The arguments are precise, and the language has classical elegance. The two proposals for promoting benefits mentioned at the end are especially apt remedies for the ailments of the people of Chu. I admire this greatly! I admire this greatly!

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: A man of insight, particularly capable of putting his abilities to use in public affairs.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: Thoroughly conversant with the essentials of governance; the proposals are concrete and practicable.

In devising expedients to rescue the age, the guiding principle prizes adapting to change; in the principles of governing the state, what is right lies in far-reaching plans. Now, there is no age in the world that does not change. The wise remedy its troubles through measures, in order to discern…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其情以和其心以紓其急是故其情察則
幽隱可達於上其心和則怨苦可輯於下
其急紓則蕃祉可待於後夫然後可恃以
不亂天下無不貫之道仁者畫之以心以
經其常以計其變以憲其慮是故經其常
故阜生可紀也計其變故裁成可遂也憲
其慮故機宜可燭也夫然後有以捄之而
不敗是故以智者謀之是謂通變以仁者
運之是謂遠猷語曰長慮却顧逸而有終
===
舉近遺遠謀而不集正謂此也愚誦執事
之問至於足國裕民窮原探本不爲一朝
一夕之計而登於富壽爲之浩歎而流涕
也昔者成周之時陰陽調均百物遂生其
詩曰雨我公田遂及我私民力於田畝敘
時作事其詩曰率我婦子饁彼南畝田畯
至喜穡豐其野婦寧其室其詩曰匪且有
且匪今斯今振古如兹愚竊以此生人之
常何足爲頌也其後也旱魃爲虐而饑饉
punctuated:
其情，以和其心，以紓其急。是故其情察，則幽隱可達於上；其心和，則怨苦可輯於下；其急紓，則蕃祉可待於後。夫然後可恃以不亂。天下無不貫之道，仁者畫之以心，以經其常，以計其變，以憲其慮。是故經其常，故阜生可紀也；計其變，故裁成可遂也；憲其慮，故機宜可燭也。夫然後有以捄之而不敗。是故以智者謀之，是謂通變；以仁者運之，是謂遠猷。語曰：「長慮却顧，逸而有終；舉近遺遠，謀而不集。」正謂此也。
愚誦執事之問，至於足國裕民、窮原探本、不爲一朝一夕之計而登於富壽，爲之浩歎而流涕也。昔者成周之時，陰陽調均，百物遂生。其詩曰：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」民力於田畝，敘時作事。其詩曰：「率我婦子，饁彼南畝，田畯至喜。」穡豐其野，婦寧其室。其詩曰：「匪且有且，匪今斯今，振古如兹。」愚竊以此生人之常，何足爲頌也？其後也，旱魃爲虐，而饑饉
translation_en:
…their circumstances, to bring harmony to their hearts and relieve their urgent distress. Thus, when their circumstances are understood, hidden suffering can be communicated to those above; when their hearts are at peace, resentment and hardship can be assuaged among those below; and when their urgent distress is relieved, abundant blessings may be expected thereafter. Only then can one count on freedom from disorder. There is no circumstance under Heaven that the Way does not encompass. The benevolent devise plans with care: they manage ordinary conditions, reckon with changes, and give form to their deliberations [?]. By managing ordinary conditions, they can establish an orderly basis for enriching livelihoods; by reckoning with changes, they can carry through appropriate adjustments; by giving form to their deliberations [?], they can discern what circumstances require. Only then can they bring relief without failure. Thus, planning with wisdom is called adapting to change; acting with benevolence is called foresight. As the saying goes: “Consider the distant future and look back: you will proceed with ease and reach a successful conclusion. Attend to what is near and neglect what is distant: your plans will not succeed.” This is precisely what it means.
When I humbly read your question, reaching the passage about providing adequately for the state and enriching the people, tracing matters to their origins and probing their foundations, and planning beyond a single morning or evening so as to attain prosperity and longevity, I sighed deeply and shed tears. Formerly, in the flourishing days of Zhou, yin and yang were in harmony, and all things grew to maturity. Its poetry says: “Rain upon our common fields, and then reach our private plots.” The people labored in the fields, ordering their work by the seasons. Its poetry says: “I lead my wife and children to bring food to those southern fields; the field overseer comes and is pleased.” Harvests were abundant in the countryside, and women were at peace in their homes. Its poetry says: “This has not been so only now [?], nor is it a thing of today alone; from remotest antiquity it has been thus.” I venture to think that this is the normal condition of human life: why should it merit a hymn of praise? Later, the drought demon wreaked havoc, and famine…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
起其詩曰赫赫炎炎云我無所君憂於上
以銷去之其詩曰上下奠瘞靡神不舉民
困於下生理無聊其詩曰周餘黎民靡有
孑遺愚竊以此適然之變而云無遺何邪
吾楚連歲大饑腴壤石田居掠其聚行遷
其次轉徙頓踣道殣相望裂地而薇殫涸
川而魚竭曩與吾居也其生也十室而五
曩與吾居也其徙也十室而七曩與吾居
也其鬻也十室而九宜執事之不忍聞也
===
向非
聖明善貸之仁諸司匍匐之惠蠲復不下帑藏
不發愚又不知其幾也乃知孑遺之歌斯
人生之至勤而振古之頌王道之大成也
是故荒政之策載在今昔諸司固已極力
拯援見諸施行况在今日則既往之事也
聖德格天被于方內上錫順成之惠下起扄野
之懽是吾民更生之辰也民惟邦本本固
邦寧執事可以無慮矣然而曲突徙薪之
punctuated:
起。其詩曰：「赫赫炎炎，云我無所。」君憂於上，以銷去之。其詩曰：「上下奠瘞，靡神不舉。」民困於下，生理無聊。其詩曰：「周餘黎民，靡有孑遺。」愚竊以此適然之變，而云無遺，何邪？吾楚連歲大饑，腴壤石田，居掠其聚，行遷其次，轉徙頓踣，道殣相望。裂地而薇殫，涸川而魚竭。曩與吾居也，其生也十室而五；曩與吾居也，其徙也十室而七；曩與吾居也，其鬻也十室而九。宜執事之不忍聞也！
向非聖明善貸之仁、諸司匍匐之惠，蠲復不下，帑藏不發，愚又不知其幾也。乃知孑遺之歌，斯人生之至勤，而振古之頌，王道之大成也。是故荒政之策，載在今昔，諸司固已極力拯援，見諸施行。况在今日，則既往之事也。聖德格天，被于方內，上錫順成之惠，下起扄野之懽。是吾民更生之辰也。民惟邦本，本固邦寧，執事可以無慮矣。然而曲突徙薪之
translation_en:
…arose. The Odes say: “Blazing and scorching, we say we have nowhere to turn.” The ruler, above, anxiously sought to dispel the calamity. The Odes say: “Offerings were laid out and buried for the powers above and below; no spirit went without worship.” The people, below, were distressed and had no means of sustaining life. The Odes say: “Of Zhou’s remaining common people, not a single one survives.” I humbly thought this merely an occasional calamity: why, then, say that none remained?
In our Chu, severe famine has continued year after year. Fertile soil has become stony fields; those who remain plunder accumulated stores, while those on the move shift their stopping places [?]. Wandering and collapsing, the starving dead lie within sight of one another along the roads. The earth has been dug open until the wild vetch is exhausted; the rivers have been drained until no fish remain. Of those who formerly lived among us, five households in ten survive; of those who formerly lived among us, seven households in ten have migrated; of those who formerly lived among us, nine households in ten have sold themselves or their family members [?]. No wonder you cannot bear to hear of it!
Had it not been for the enlightened sovereign’s benevolence in generously providing aid, and the compassion of the various offices in hastening to our relief—had remissions and exemptions not been ordered and treasury reserves not been released—I cannot imagine how many more would have suffered. Only then did I understand that the song about not a single survivor expresses the utmost hardship of human life, while the ode declaring “thus it has been since ancient times” celebrates the great fulfillment of the Kingly Way.
Thus, measures for famine relief are recorded in writings both ancient and modern. The various offices have indeed exerted themselves to the utmost in rescue and assistance, putting these measures into practice. Moreover, by now these events belong to the past. The sage sovereign’s virtue reaches Heaven and extends throughout the realm. Above, Heaven bestows the blessing of favorable seasons and ripened crops; below, joy arises in the countryside [?]. This is the moment when our people begin life anew. The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace. You may therefore set your worries aside. Yet the thought of bending the chimney and moving the firewood away to prevent a fire…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
思而執事每惓惓而爲之計斯仁智之用
心也古者三年之耕藏一年之積九年之
耕藏三年之積以三十年之通則雖以凶
旱水溢而不懼何也其備之者具也古者
詔萬民之食豐則人四鬴中則人三鬴儉
則人二鬴人不能二鬴則移以就穀而不
病何也其察之者周也繇此觀之則堯之
九年湯之七年豈有捐瘠之民乎傳曰田
野縣鄙財之本也垣窌倉廩財之末也百
===
姓時和事業得敘財之源也等賦府庫財
之流也故必謹養其和使天下必有餘而
上不患不足嗟乎執事窮原探本之問其
養和之說乎夫積逋淫禁未足爲憂也近
鬻遠竄未足爲憂也輕徭省刑未足爲憂
也貯粟平糶未足爲憂也豪强兼倂貪墨
爲虐未足爲憂也愚之過計竊以爲憂者
獨曰任人而已也不然則古人之成法儒
先之定論具在也任得其人則誚讓自囚
punctuated:
思，而執事每惓惓而爲之計，斯仁智之用心也。古者三年之耕，藏一年之積；九年之耕，藏三年之積。以三十年之通，則雖以凶旱水溢而不懼。何也？其備之者具也。古者詔萬民之食，豐則人四鬴，中則人三鬴，儉則人二鬴；人不能二鬴，則移以就穀而不病。何也？其察之者周也。繇此觀之，則堯之九年、湯之七年，豈有捐瘠之民乎？
傳曰：「田野縣鄙，財之本也；垣窌倉廩，財之末也；百姓時和，事業得敘，財之源也；等賦府庫，財之流也。故必謹養其和，使天下必有餘，而上不患不足。」
嗟乎！執事窮原探本之問，其養和之說乎？夫積逋淫禁，未足爲憂也；近鬻遠竄，未足爲憂也；輕徭省刑，未足爲憂也；貯粟平糶，未足爲憂也；豪强兼倂、貪墨爲虐，未足爲憂也。愚之過計，竊以爲憂者，獨曰任人而已也。不然，則古人之成法、儒先之定論具在也。任得其人，則誚讓自囚
translation_en:
…such forethought; and you, sir, continually and earnestly devise measures for it. This is the concern of one who is benevolent and wise. In antiquity, three years of cultivation yielded a year's provisions in reserve, and nine years of cultivation yielded three years' provisions in reserve. With resources balanced over thirty years, there was no fear even of crop failure, drought, or flooding. Why? Because preparations were complete. In antiquity, regulations prescribed food allowances for all the people: in abundant years, four fu per person; in middling years, three fu; and in lean years, two fu. If two fu per person could not be provided, the people were moved to where grain was available, and thus suffered no distress. Why? Because oversight was thorough. Viewed in this light, could there have been people abandoned and starving during Yao's nine years of flooding or Tang's seven years of drought?
The transmitted text says: “Fields and outlying settlements are the root of wealth; enclosed storage grounds, underground stores, and granaries are its branches. When the common people live in harmony with the seasons and their occupations proceed in proper order, this is the source of wealth; graded taxation and government treasuries are its onward flow. Thus one must carefully nurture this harmony, ensuring that all under Heaven have a surplus, so that those above need not worry about insufficiency.”
Ah! Your question, sir, which probes the source and seeks the root, surely concerns this principle of nurturing harmony. Accumulated arrears and excessive imprisonment are not sufficient grounds for anxiety; people selling themselves nearby or fleeing far away are not sufficient grounds for anxiety; reducing labor services and punishments is not sufficient grounds for anxiety; storing grain and selling it at equitable prices is not sufficient grounds for anxiety; nor are engrossment by the powerful and oppression by corrupt officials sufficient grounds for anxiety. In my perhaps excessive deliberations, the sole matter I venture to regard with anxiety is the appointment of personnel. Otherwise, the established methods of the ancients and the settled judgments of earlier Confucian scholars are all available. If the right people are appointed, then, by rebuking others and placing oneself in confinement…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
如陽城積逋可理也一訊立辨如周濂溪
淫禁可解也庸直歸質如柳宗元近鬻可
贖也增户四萬如虞詡遠竄可還也蒲鞭
示辱如劉寬刑罰可省也居官如家如衞
颯差役可薄也閉閤思過如韓延壽豪强
可化也望風畏肅如蘇章貪墨可清也秉
慘怛之愛調盈縮之權揆俗情之宜建長
久之法廣招輯之政推恩信之實則下有
按堵之樂上有長城之賴朱子所謂感召
===
和氣以致豐穰者此也任不得其人則牧
羊束濕之譏皆得以制乎其上雖日日而
程之事事而制之吾懼其不能也况於舉
吾民而秦越之雖有良法美意祗見其文
焉而已矣而又因以虐乎雖然若舉其勢
之緩急事之先後從而斟酌焉夫刑罰省
則民重生重生則樂業徭役輕則民安土
安土則妄賄息兼併之害除而良善得以
遂其日用之常貪墨之吏革則小民得以
punctuated: 如陽城，積逋可理也；一訊立辨，如周濂溪，淫禁可解也；庸直歸質，如柳宗元，近鬻可贖也；增户四萬，如虞詡，遠竄可還也；蒲鞭示辱，如劉寬，刑罰可省也；居官如家，如衞颯，差役可薄也；閉閤思過，如韓延壽，豪强可化也；望風畏肅，如蘇章，貪墨可清也。秉慘怛之愛，調盈縮之權，揆俗情之宜，建長久之法，廣招輯之政，推恩信之實，則下有按堵之樂，上有長城之賴。朱子所謂感召和氣以致豐穰者，此也。任不得其人，則牧羊束濕之譏，皆得以制乎其上；雖日日而程之，事事而制之，吾懼其不能也。况於舉吾民而秦越之，雖有良法美意，祗見其文焉而已矣，而又因以虐乎？雖然，若舉其勢之緩急、事之先後，從而斟酌焉，夫刑罰省，則民重生；重生，則樂業。徭役輕，則民安土；安土，則妄賄息。兼併之害除，而良善得以遂其日用之常；貪墨之吏革，則小民得以
translation_en:
…as in the case of Yang Cheng, accumulated arrears can be settled. By establishing the facts in a single interrogation, as Zhou Lianxi did, wrongful imprisonment can be ended. By applying wages toward the redemption of those pledged into servitude, as Liu Zongyuan did, those sold nearby can be redeemed. By increasing the number of households by forty thousand, as Yu Xu did, those who have fled far away can be brought back. By using a rush whip to express disgrace, as Liu Kuan did, punishments can be reduced. By administering one’s jurisdiction as one’s own household, as Wei Sa did, service obligations can be lightened. By shutting oneself indoors to reflect on one’s faults, as Han Yanshou did, powerful local bullies can be reformed. By inspiring awe and fear through one’s reputation, as Su Zhang did, corruption can be cleared away. Hold fast to compassionate concern; exercise discretion in adjusting surpluses and shortfalls; consider what suits local customs and sentiments; establish enduring regulations; extend measures to attract and settle the people; and give practical effect to kindness and good faith. Then those below will enjoy living securely, while those above will have a Great Wall upon which to rely. This is what Master Zhu meant by calling forth harmonious vital forces to bring about abundant harvests.
If suitable men are not appointed, then the reproaches concerning herding sheep and bundling wet firewood may all serve to constrain their superiors [?]. Even if their performance is assessed daily and every affair regulated, I fear that success will remain impossible. How much worse if all our people are treated with the indifference of Qin toward Yue: even with good laws and fine intentions, only their outward form will be visible—and what if these are further used to oppress the people?
Nevertheless, if we weigh the relative urgency of circumstances and the proper sequence of affairs, then reducing punishments will make the people value life; valuing life, they will take pleasure in their occupations. Lightening labor service will enable the people to remain content on their land; content on their land, they will cease illicit payments [?]. When the harm of engrossment is removed, honest people can pursue their ordinary daily livelihoods. When corrupt officials are dismissed, the common people will be able to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
免漁獵之困四者耗財之最者也四者試
去積逋淫禁可以得紓而軍儲藩賦亦從
容可給矣近鬻遠竄可以得復而資糧贖
金可以不費而辨矣常平之粟平糶之法
可以因時而制矣四者而或不能去焉則
愁憤上干于天氛癘下行于地謂之養和
可乎故吾楚今日正在撫存休養之時譬
之大病湯劑砭灸雖已少甦而將護節宣
尤其急者惟執事加之意而已是吾民之
===
幸也然愚又有獻焉吾楚地廣民稀而十
日之霖大浸也一月之旱赤土也愚竊以
為宜度于官視其地之高亢窪濕一用古
人潴泄濬距之法以興陂塘之利而使不
泄以崇隄障之勢而使不浸乃又擇官時
督之毋令鹵莽滅裂而使無不耕則穀粟
不可勝食矣吾楚湖池最多舊屬課程𠇍
多湮塞地極肥饒乃皆為豪富所有今其
赤曆可攷也愚竊以為宜請于
punctuated:
免漁獵之困。四者，耗財之最者也。四者試去，積逋淫禁可以得紓，而軍儲藩賦亦從容可給矣；近鬻遠竄可以得復，而資糧贖金可以不費而辨矣。常平之粟、平糶之法，可以因時而制矣。四者而或不能去焉，則愁憤上干于天，氛癘下行于地，謂之養和可乎？故吾楚今日正在撫存休養之時。譬之大病，湯劑砭灸，雖已少甦，而將護節宣，尤其急者。惟執事加之意而已，是吾民之幸也。
然愚又有獻焉。吾楚地廣民稀，而十日之霖，大浸也；一月之旱，赤土也。愚竊以為宜度于官，視其地之高亢窪濕，一用古人潴泄濬距之法，以興陂塘之利而使不泄，以崇隄障之勢而使不浸。乃又擇官時督之，毋令鹵莽滅裂，而使無不耕，則穀粟不可勝食矣。吾楚湖池最多，舊屬課程，𠇍多湮塞，地極肥饒，乃皆為豪富所有。今其赤曆可攷也。愚竊以為宜請于
translation_en:
…escape the hardships of predatory exploitation. These four are the greatest drains upon resources. If these four were removed [?], the burden of accumulated arrears and excessive prohibitions could be eased, while military provisions and provincial tax obligations could readily be met. Those sold nearby and those who have fled far away could be restored, and provisions and redemption money could be arranged without expense. Grain in the ever-normal granaries and measures for selling grain at fair prices could then be regulated according to circumstances. But if any of these four cannot be removed, sorrow and indignation will rise to affront Heaven, and pestilential vapors will spread below upon the earth. Could this be called nurturing harmony? Thus our land of Chu is now precisely at a time when its people must be comforted, sustained, and allowed to recuperate. It is like a person suffering from a grave illness: although decoctions, stone needles, and moxibustion have brought some recovery, careful nursing and regulation of daily life are especially urgent. If you would only give this your attention, it would be a blessing for our people.
Yet I have another proposal to offer. Our land of Chu is vast and sparsely populated, but ten days of continuous rain bring great floods, while a month of drought leaves the soil bare. I humbly believe that the authorities should assess the terrain, examining which land is high and dry and which is low and wet, and apply throughout the methods of the ancients for storing and releasing water and dredging drainage channels. They should develop the benefits of reservoirs and ponds so that water is retained, and strengthen dikes and barriers so that the land is not inundated. Officials should then be selected to supervise this work regularly, allowing no careless or slipshod practices and ensuring that all the land is cultivated. Grain would then be more than could be consumed. Our land of Chu has lakes and ponds in great abundance. They were formerly subject to assessed levies; many have silted up [?], and their soil is extremely fertile, yet all have come into the possession of powerful and wealthy families. Their red registers can still be consulted today. I humbly believe that a request should be submitted to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
上減其歲額而均以則壤成賦之法召民耕佃
比於屯田以補軍儲藩賦之不足則財用
不患于匱乏矣此萬世之利也朱子曰賑
饑無奇策不如講求水利非愚之私言也
剝膚之征惟執事財擇焉
punctuated: 上減其歲額，而均以則壤成賦之法，召民耕佃，比於屯田，以補軍儲、藩賦之不足，則財用不患于匱乏矣。此萬世之利也。朱子曰：「賑饑無奇策，不如講求水利。」非愚之私言也。剝膚之征，惟執事財擇焉。
translation_en: …His Majesty to reduce their annual quota and distribute the assessment equitably according to the quality of the soil, recruiting commoners to cultivate the land as tenants, on the model of military agricultural colonies, to make up deficiencies in military provisions and provincial revenues. There would then be no fear of insufficient funds. This would bring benefits for ten thousand generations. Master Zhu said: “There is no extraordinary strategy for famine relief; nothing is better than investigating and developing water management.” This is not merely my own humble opinion. As for these skin-flaying exactions [?], I leave it to you, the officials in charge, to weigh and select what is appropriate.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄕試錄後序
仰惟我
睿宗獻皇帝文德之純久洽民心
皇上龍興撫運覃敷文敎衡郢江
漢之區固
聖澤之所源委也是以一時賢士
莫不勇於趨化而奮庸共臣
===
之願率先寰宇旣增解額則
旌淑之途愈闢彙征之良益
繁彬彬乎思皇之譽焉嘉靖
丙午復當大薦監察御史高
節振德維風加愼厥典内外
諸司洎百執事咸與矢心恪
職和衷翼勵之誠視常爲烈
punctuated:
湖廣鄕試錄後序

仰惟我睿宗獻皇帝文德之純，久洽民心。皇上龍興撫運，覃敷文敎。衡郢江漢之區，固聖澤之所源委也。是以一時賢士，莫不勇於趨化，而奮庸共臣之願，率先寰宇。旣增解額，則旌淑之途愈闢，彙征之良益繁，彬彬乎思皇之譽焉。嘉靖丙午，復當大薦。監察御史高節，振德維風，加愼厥典。内外諸司洎百執事，咸與矢心恪職，和衷翼勵之誠，視常爲烈。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

We reverently reflect that the purity of the civil virtue of our Emperor Ruizong Xian has long permeated the hearts of the people. His Majesty rose like a dragon to assume the mandate of the age and spread cultural instruction far and wide. The regions of Heng and Ying, and of the Jiang and Han rivers, are indeed where the beneficence of the sage sovereign originates and flows. Thus the worthy scholars of our time have all eagerly responded to this transforming influence. In their aspiration to exert themselves in service as ministers [?], they have taken the lead throughout the realm. Since the provincial quota was increased, the avenue for honoring the worthy has opened still wider, and ever more good men have advanced together, winning praise for their cultivated excellence and worthiness.

In the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], the time again arrived for the great selection of men for recommendation. Investigating Censor Gao Jie promoted virtue and upheld proper customs, taking additional care over the conduct of this examination. The various offices, both within and outside, together with all the functionaries, pledged themselves to discharge their duties conscientiously. Their sincerity in working harmoniously and encouraging one another with reverent diligence exceeded the ordinary.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其爭相濯磨而起獻藝者夫
亦盛倍往昔矣精神意氣所
感非機之相為通者哉且聞
之楚歲不登阻饑告瘁用以
上廑
帝念是年雨暘時若恒應雲霓之
望江漢底寧不虞濫溢之流
===
來牟受厥明黃茂遂以嘉鬯
康年之錫蓋共云希睹者也
而賓賢之典適維其期識者
知天道為不虛矣周始入境
見畒夫操銍艾羣集于稼濟
濟焉桎桎焉于是乎太和之
蒸得諸在野入鄂則巷謳達
punctuated: 其爭相濯磨而起獻藝者，夫亦盛倍往昔矣。精神意氣所感，非機之相為通者哉？且聞之，楚歲不登，阻饑告瘁，用以上廑帝念。是年雨暘時若，恒應雲霓之望；江漢底寧，不虞濫溢之流。來牟受厥明，黃茂遂以嘉鬯。康年之錫，蓋共云希睹者也。而賓賢之典，適維其期，識者知天道為不虛矣。周始入境，見畒夫操銍艾，羣集于稼，濟濟焉，桎桎焉。于是乎太和之蒸，得諸在野。入鄂，則巷謳達
translation_en:
Those who vied with one another in refining themselves and came forward to display their abilities were indeed far more numerous than in former times. Was this not a mutual responsiveness stirred by shared spirit and resolve? Moreover, I had heard that in Chu the yearly harvests had failed, and that the people, beset by hunger, reported their distress, thereby troubling the Emperor’s thoughts. This year, rain and sunshine arrived in season, repeatedly fulfilling the longing for rain-bearing clouds; the Jiang and Han rivers were tranquil, with no fear of overflowing waters. Wheat and barley received their bright blessing [?], and the yellowing, luxuriant grain flourished splendidly. All agreed that the bestowal of such a bountiful year was a rare sight. The ceremony for honoring worthy men as guests happened to fall at just this time. Those of discernment knew that the Way of Heaven was not without substance.
When I, Zhou, first entered the territory, I saw farmers wielding sickles to reap, gathered in the grain fields in great numbers, busily harvesting [?]. Thus I found the burgeoning of supreme harmony among those in the countryside. Upon entering E, the songs in the lanes reached …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於觀風民依慊於司牧上下
承秉胥交爲慶于是乎太和
之合得諸在位旣入鎖院裒
諸士子之辭章俯而讀仰而
思雅麗殊則嚴腴因材則無
不冲融豐豫可以觀樂土之
華焉于是乎太和之發得諸
===
人文至其撤棘懸象賓筵醴
洽蓋所謂有飶其香邦家之
光者居然斯明徵也於戲休
哉善彰片言則星舍順軌明
揚介士則雲物垂祥况俊彥
旅升之會而其所以昭天地
闡性命者燦然具陳于前哉
punctuated:
於觀風，民依慊於司牧，上下承秉，胥交爲慶。于是乎太和之合得諸在位。旣入鎖院，裒諸士子之辭章，俯而讀，仰而思，雅麗殊則，嚴腴因材，則無不冲融豐豫，可以觀樂土之華焉。于是乎太和之發得諸人文。
至其撤棘懸象，賓筵醴洽，蓋所謂「有飶其香，邦家之光」者，居然斯明徵也。於戲，休哉！善彰片言，則星舍順軌；明揚介士，則雲物垂祥。况俊彥旅升之會，而其所以昭天地、闡性命者，燦然具陳于前哉！
translation_en:
…reached those observing local customs, while the people's needs were satisfied by their shepherds, the local officials. Those above and below fulfilled their responsibilities and joined in mutual congratulations. Thus I found the concord of supreme harmony among those holding office. Once inside the sealed examination compound, I gathered the candidates' compositions, bent my head to read, and raised it to reflect. Their elegance and beauty followed differing standards, their gravity and richness accorded with their talents [?]; yet all were harmonious, ample, and exuberant, revealing the cultural flowering of this happy land. Thus I found the expression of supreme harmony in literary achievement.
When the thorn barriers were removed and the results displayed [?], sweet wine flowed freely at the banquet for the honored guests. Here indeed was clear evidence of the saying, “Fragrant is its aroma; the glory of the state and its ruling house.” Ah, how splendid! When goodness is made manifest in a single utterance, the stars follow their proper courses; when upright scholars are conspicuously advanced, the clouds display auspicious signs. How much more so at a gathering where outstanding talents advance together, and the writings through which they illuminate Heaven and Earth and expound human nature and destiny are brilliantly set forth before us!

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
故曰漸仁摩義
神聖作人之化也同心協力臣人
得士之功也時和年豐
上帝啓賢之祚也周等濫司遴拔
蚤夜祗慄惟懼不明以遺厥
良旣懼枝葉之辭或有庸違
以眩厥智恃玆三者信可以
===
渙釋所慮矣讌之日諸士序
進衆音迭作始歌鹿鳴周乃
諗之曰敷奏厎績謀猷經邦
皆言之貴也諸子行以對揚
于
廷則務是好
君爲勗再歌南山有臺復曰選賢
punctuated:
故曰：漸仁摩義，神聖作人之化也；同心協力，臣人得士之功也；時和年豐，上帝啓賢之祚也。周等濫司遴拔，蚤夜祗慄，惟懼不明，以遺厥良；旣懼枝葉之辭或有庸違，以眩厥智。恃玆三者，信可以渙釋所慮矣。
讌之日，諸士序進，衆音迭作。始歌《鹿鳴》，周乃諗之曰：「敷奏厎績，謀猷經邦，皆言之貴也。諸子行以對揚于廷，則務是好君爲勗。」再歌《南山有臺》，復曰：「選賢
translation_en:
Thus we say: immersion in benevolence and cultivation through righteousness are the transforming work by which our sagely sovereign nurtures men of talent; unity of purpose and concerted effort are the means by which his servants succeed in obtaining worthy scholars; a harmonious season and abundant harvest are the blessings through which the Lord on High brings forth worthies. We, Zhou and the others, unworthily entrusted with selection, have trembled in reverence morning and night, fearing only that our discernment might fail and we might overlook worthy men. We have also feared that ornamental language might conceal outward assent and inward disobedience, thereby confounding our judgment. Relying on these three things, we can indeed dispel our anxieties.
On the day of the banquet, the scholars advanced in order, and the various musical sounds arose in succession. First they sang “The Deer Call” (Lu ming). Zhou then admonished them: “Presenting reports and achieving results, devising plans and ordering the realm—these are what make words valuable. When you gentlemen go forth to respond to and extol imperial favor at court, strive to take devotion to the ruler as your encouragement [?].” Next they sang “On the Southern Mountain There Is Terrace Grass” (Nanshan you tai), and he spoke again: “Selecting the worthy …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則克用乂純徵匪曰圖榮將
以利吾
邦家也如其言浮而道戾得無
忝於基哉湛露歌闋則申之
曰柔嘉之德儀色之令樊侯
所爲賦政於中外也尚其慎
玆以往期永終顯允豈弟之
===
譽主司亦與有望焉由是錄
成當
獻周循職事敬次言之以終其
義云
浙江處州府麗水縣儒學教
諭姜周謹序
punctuated:
則克用乂，純徵匪曰圖榮，將以利吾邦家也。如其言浮而道戾，得無忝於基哉？」《湛露》歌闋，則申之曰：「柔嘉之德，儀色之令，樊侯所爲賦政於中外也。尚其慎玆以往，期永終顯允豈弟之譽，主司亦與有望焉。」由是錄成當獻，周循職事，敬次言之，以終其義云。
浙江處州府麗水縣儒學教諭姜周謹序。
translation_en:
…then they can be employed to bring about good government, and their pure qualities will be attested [?]. The aim is not to seek glory, but to benefit our state. If their words are empty and their conduct contrary to the Way, would they not disgrace their position as its foundation?” When the singing of “Luxuriant Dew” (Zhan lu) ended, he further admonished them: “Gentle and admirable virtue, excellent bearing and demeanor—these were the qualities through which the Marquis of Fan administered government within and beyond the royal court. May you carefully attend to these from this time forward, hoping always to preserve a reputation for manifest trustworthiness and gracious ease. The officials presiding over the examination likewise place their hopes in you.”
Thus, with the record completed and ready for presentation to the throne, I, Zhou, in fulfillment of my duties, have respectfully set these words in order to bring their meaning to a conclusion.
Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Zhou, Instructor of the Confucian School of Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
太高祖逖之發憤太遽寇準之召謗太疎
執事固疑其激矣乃若郭林宗之遜言危
行程明道之平心和氣史弼之平原無黨
鮮于侁之三難比之數子則又不專憤時
以為激者矣然要之均以應世也蓋甞論
之長孺多欲之譏雖武帝且不能堪况敵
以下者乎然招之不來麾之不去蓋社稷
之臣也林宗瞻烏之慟蓋不免於憤世而
黨事獨免焉澄之不清撓之不濁蓋千頃
之陂也膺之獨持風裁激素行而立廉尚
其志足以風動天下矣使荀爽見險遠害
之諷行膺豈有禍邪準之素抱忠節仗大
策以却強虜其功足以奠安宗社矣使張
詠不學無術之戒行準豈能貶邪弼以無
黨獲罪而頡頏嚴吏善類賴以保全何其
壯也史曰活千人者子孫必封弼豈為此
者哉逖以中原板蕩為憂而大功不就卒
怏怏以至於死何其迫也傳曰得時則大
punctuated:
太高，祖逖之發憤太遽，寇準之召謗太疎，執事固疑其激矣。乃若郭林宗之遜言危行，程明道之平心和氣，史弼之平原無黨，鮮于侁之三難，比之數子，則又不專憤時以為激者矣。然要之，均以應世也。
蓋甞論之：長孺多欲之譏，雖武帝且不能堪，况敵以下者乎？然招之不來，麾之不去，蓋社稷之臣也。林宗瞻烏之慟，蓋不免於憤世，而黨事獨免焉。澄之不清，撓之不濁，蓋千頃之陂也。膺之獨持風裁，激素行而立廉尚，其志足以風動天下矣。使荀爽見險遠害之諷行，膺豈有禍邪？準之素抱忠節，仗大策以却強虜，其功足以奠安宗社矣。使張詠不學無術之戒行，準豈能貶邪？弼以無黨獲罪，而頡頏嚴吏，善類賴以保全，何其壯也！史曰：「活千人者，子孫必封。」弼豈為此者哉？逖以中原板蕩為憂，而大功不就，卒怏怏以至於死，何其迫也！傳曰：「得時則大
translation_en:
…too lofty; Zu Ti’s indignant resolve was too impetuous, and Kou Zhun was too careless in inviting slander. You certainly suspect that they went to extremes. Yet consider Guo Linzong’s modest speech and upright conduct, Cheng Mingdao’s even temper and harmonious disposition, Shi Bi’s refusal to recognize any faction at Pingyuan, and Xianyu Shen’s three difficulties. Compared with the others, these men did not simply let indignation at their times drive them to extremes. Ultimately, however, all were responding to the world in which they lived.
I have reflected on this: even Emperor Wu could not bear Changru’s criticism of his many desires—how much less could those of equal or lesser standing? Yet he would not come merely when beckoned, nor leave merely when waved away: he was indeed a minister devoted to the state. Linzong’s grief at the sight of the crows surely showed that he could not escape indignation at the world, yet he alone escaped implication in the factional affair. Settling could not make him clearer, nor stirring make him turbid: he was like a reservoir covering a thousand qing. Ying alone upheld standards of conduct, spurring others toward unadorned behavior and establishing esteem for integrity. His resolve was sufficient to transform the moral climate throughout the realm. Had Xun Shuang’s admonition to recognize danger and keep clear of harm been heeded, would Ying have met with disaster? Zhun had always cherished loyalty and integrity; by relying on a great strategic decision to repel powerful invaders, he rendered service sufficient to secure the dynasty and the state. Had Zhang Yong’s warning about being without learning or practical understanding been heeded, could Zhun have been demoted? Bi incurred punishment for refusing to recognize a faction, yet stood up to harsh officials, and good men relied on him for their preservation. How heroic he was! The histories say: “The descendants of one who saves a thousand lives will surely be enfeoffed.” But could Bi have acted for that reason? Ti grieved over the turmoil in the Central Plain, yet his great undertaking remained unfinished, and he died in bitterness. How sorely pressed he was! The Commentary says: “When one meets with the right time, one greatly…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
行不得則龍蛇𨓆何爲者哉明道之不非
青苗獵較之意也廓然大公物來順應豈
其所謂尚氣者哉觀非一家私議之言安
石且爲之愧屈爾矣珖之善處新法豈弟
之心也上不害法下不傷民豈其所謂泥
方者哉觀憂患太息之疏神宗且有文學
可用之喜矣此愚之所謂以道裁之者也
安可遂以爲激乎夫事之所處有可否焉
時之所值有順逆焉勢之所處有難易焉
===
因其事以度其時因其時以察其勢因其
跡以原其心庶乎其得之矣雖然君子寧
病於隘不隘則必自卑以求幸其道而砥
柱之風衰寧病於激不激則必自貶以求
歡於時而殉國之志懈愚以是知諸賢之
未可以易議也然而君子安所取衷焉是
故非澹泊無以明志非寧靜無以致遠吾
得之孔明嗟乎此伊尹之志也純粹如精
金温潤如良玉吾得之明道嗟乎此顏子
punctuated:
行，不得則龍蛇。𨓆何爲者哉？明道之不非青苗，獵較之意也。廓然大公，物來順應，豈其所謂尚氣者哉？觀「非一家私議」之言，安石且爲之愧屈爾矣。珖之善處新法，豈弟之心也。上不害法，下不傷民，豈其所謂泥方者哉？觀憂患太息之疏，神宗且有文學可用之喜矣。此愚之所謂以道裁之者也，安可遂以爲激乎？夫事之所處有可否焉，時之所值有順逆焉，勢之所處有難易焉。因其事以度其時，因其時以察其勢，因其跡以原其心，庶乎其得之矣。

雖然，君子寧病於隘，不隘則必自卑以求幸其道，而砥柱之風衰；寧病於激，不激則必自貶以求歡於時，而殉國之志懈。愚以是知諸賢之未可以易議也。然而君子安所取衷焉？是故非澹泊無以明志，非寧靜無以致遠，吾得之孔明。嗟乎！此伊尹之志也。純粹如精金，温潤如良玉，吾得之明道。嗟乎！此顏子
translation_en:
…act on a grand scale; when the opportunity is lacking, be like a dragon or snake in concealment. What, then, was [Zu Ti?] doing? Mingdao’s refusal to condemn the Green Sprouts policy expressed the same intention as participating in the hunt. Entirely open and impartial, he responded appropriately to things as they arose: could this be what is called acting out of temper? Consider his statement that this was “not a matter for one family’s private deliberation”: even Anshi was shamed into yielding. Guang’s skill in handling the New Policies arose from a kindly heart. Above, he did not impair the laws; below, he did not injure the people. Could this be what is called rigid adherence to rules? Consider his memorial expressing anxious concern and deep sighs: even Emperor Shenzong rejoiced that his literary learning could be put to use. This is what I mean by judging according to the Way. How could one simply dismiss it as excessive zeal? In dealing with affairs, some courses are acceptable and others are not; the times one encounters may be favorable or adverse; the circumstances one faces may be difficult or easy. Assess the times in light of the affair, examine the circumstances in light of the times, and trace the intentions behind the actions: one may then come close to a sound judgment.

Nevertheless, a gentleman would rather incur the fault of narrowness. Without such strictness, he is bound to lower himself in the hope of securing acceptance for his Way, and the spirit of standing firm like a pillar amid the torrent will decline. He would rather incur the fault of excessive zeal. Without such zeal, he is bound to demean himself to win the favor of his age, and his resolve to sacrifice himself for the state will weaken. From this I know that these worthy men cannot be judged lightly. Yet where should a gentleman find the proper balance? “Without freedom from worldly desires, one cannot make one’s purpose clear; without tranquility, one cannot attain far-reaching ends”: this I have learned from Kongming. Ah! This is the resolve of Yi Yin. “Pure as refined gold, warm and lustrous as fine jade”: this I have learned from Mingdao. Ah! This is Master Yan’s…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之學也君子由孔明以志伊尹之所志由
明道以學顏子之所學則持心何有於不
平適用何有於不周而安有招尤失已之
爲病乎若其進而無伊尹之志退而無顏
子之學而徒因其氣質之所用以來其居
身之所珍卽使不至於招尤而失已君子
猶以爲未也執事以爲何如
第四問
唐萬幾
===
同考試官教諭宋批楚中宦蹟名賢甚多試商確
一二而子皆能論著精當且歆慕之懷激昂之志溢於言外末有
聖賢而不豪傑者是誠在子健矣健矣
考試官教諭姜批學有考據有本原佳士也
考試官教授陸批博學强記志向卓然
夫誦休以崇哲盛德之所思也論世以軌
修志士之所奮也斯二者皆尚友之誼而
士之本務也夫吾楚之有茲土也封疆之
臣或弭難以亨時或振民以育德抗峻操
punctuated:
之學也。君子由孔明以志伊尹之所志，由明道以學顏子之所學，則持心何有於不平，適用何有於不周，而安有招尤失已之爲病乎？若其進而無伊尹之志，退而無顏子之學，而徒因其氣質之所用，以來其居身之所珍，卽使不至於招尤而失已，君子猶以爲未也。執事以爲何如？
第四問
唐萬幾
同考試官教諭宋批：楚中宦蹟名賢甚多，試商確一二，而子皆能論著精當，且歆慕之懷、激昂之志溢於言外。末有聖賢而不豪傑者，是誠在子。健矣！健矣！
考試官教諭姜批：學有考據，有本原，佳士也。
考試官教授陸批：博學强記，志向卓然。
夫誦休以崇哲，盛德之所思也；論世以軌修，志士之所奮也。斯二者皆尚友之誼，而士之本務也。夫吾楚之有茲土也，封疆之臣或弭難以亨時，或振民以育德，抗峻操
translation_en:
…such was his learning. If the gentleman follows Kongming in aspiring to what Yi Yin aspired to, and follows Mingdao in studying what Master Yan studied, how could his mind fail to be balanced or his practical application fail to be comprehensive? How could incurring blame and losing his integrity trouble him? But if, when advancing into office, he lacks Yi Yin’s aspirations, and, when withdrawing, he lacks Master Yan’s learning, and merely follows the impulses of his temperament to obtain what he prizes in his personal conduct [?], then even if he avoids blame and does not lose his integrity, the gentleman would still consider him wanting. What is your judgment, honored sir?
Fourth Policy Question
Tang Wanji
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: There are many renowned worthies who served as officials in Chu. Asked to discuss and assess one or two, you have treated them all with precision and sound judgment. Moreover, your admiration and ardent aspirations overflow beyond the words themselves. There has never been a sage or worthy who was not also a man of outstanding spirit [?]. This truly lies within your power. How vigorous! How vigorous!
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: His learning rests on documented evidence and has a firm foundation. An excellent scholar.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: Broad learning, a powerful memory, and outstanding aspirations.
Now, to recite fine deeds in order to honor the wise is what those of abundant virtue contemplate; to discuss past ages in order to guide one’s own cultivation is what inspires men of aspiration. Both embody the principle of seeking friendship with the worthies of the past and are fundamental duties of a scholar. In this land of ours in Chu, officials entrusted with territorial administration have sometimes quelled troubles to bring prosperity to their age, sometimes succored the people to nurture virtue, upholding lofty integrity…

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而建茂功宣美績而播休聞而形於甘棠
之留滋久而逾懷蓋曰此嘗以父母生全
我者如在其耳目且山川靈精賢喆間出
抒大雅之華振周行之譽垂道德之光揖
高風而起敬起慕則又曰是其出於兒童
里社之所跂足而希心者也而頡頏之志
油然以興故曰尚友之誼而士之本務也
夫子曰事其大夫之賢者友其士之仁者
況乎其已試之成績而前哲之遺休可睹
===
也以愚之不敏而仰承執事之問直為是
凛凛焉爾矣夫起於思而覈於名則誦說
易歡其志信於目而貴於耳則精神必奮
其衷蓋人情之所嗜而今昔之所同也何
也其投之者必入而其為心易受也執事
之為惠也蓋遠矣請以宦於楚者言之仲
山甫封樊者也抱柔嘉之德炳明哲之幾
不茹不吐以行其志立戲之諫料民之箴
卓卓乎有補袞之思焉其周之名臣與令
punctuated:
而建茂功，宣美績而播休聞，而形於甘棠之留，滋久而逾懷。蓋曰：「此嘗以父母生全我者。」如在其耳目。且山川靈精，賢喆間出，抒大雅之華，振周行之譽，垂道德之光。揖高風而起敬起慕，則又曰：「是其出於兒童里社之所跂足而希心者也。」而頡頏之志油然以興，故曰尚友之誼而士之本務也。夫子曰：「事其大夫之賢者，友其士之仁者。」況乎其已試之成績，而前哲之遺休可睹也！以愚之不敏，而仰承執事之問，直為是凛凛焉爾矣。夫起於思而覈於名，則誦說易歡其志；信於目而貴於耳，則精神必奮其衷。蓋人情之所嗜，而今昔之所同也。何也？其投之者必入，而其為心易受也。執事之為惠也，蓋遠矣！

請以宦於楚者言之。仲山甫，封樊者也，抱柔嘉之德，炳明哲之幾，不茹不吐以行其志。立戲之諫，料民之箴，卓卓乎有補袞之思焉。其周之名臣與！令
translation_en:
…and established great achievements, made their fine accomplishments known, and spread their good repute. This found expression in the preservation of the sweet pear tree: the longer the years passed, the more deeply they were remembered. People would say, “This is one who once nurtured and preserved us like a father or mother,” as though he were still before their eyes and within their hearing. Moreover, the numinous essence of the mountains and rivers has brought forth worthy and wise men from time to time. They displayed the splendor of great refinement, won renown in the ranks of service, and bequeathed the radiance of the Way and virtue. Bowing before their lofty example, people feel reverence and admiration, and say, “Here is someone who came from our own childhood village community, whom we strain upward to emulate and aspire to in our hearts.” Thus the ambition to rival them arises spontaneously. Hence I call this the duty of befriending the worthy of the past, and a fundamental obligation of scholars. The Master said, “Serve the worthy among its great officers, and befriend the humane among its scholars.” How much more should this apply when their proven accomplishments and the blessings bequeathed by earlier worthies can still be seen! Slow-witted though I am, on respectfully receiving your question, I am filled with awe at precisely this. When reflection is tested against their renown, recitation and discussion readily gladden one's aspirations; when what the eyes attest is esteemed through what the ears hear, one's spirit is surely stirred within. This is what human feeling delights in, alike in past and present. Why? What is imparted necessarily enters, for the heart readily receives it. Far-reaching indeed is the benefit you confer!

Allow me to speak of those who held office in Chu. Zhong Shanfu was enfeoffed at Fan. He possessed gentle and admirable virtue and a luminous discernment of the subtleties of wise conduct. Neither swallowing the weak nor spitting out the strong, he pursued his purpose. His remonstrance against the installation of Xi and his admonition concerning the enumeration of the people conspicuously expressed his desire to mend the royal robe—that is, to remedy his ruler's faults. Was he not an eminent minister of Zhou! The Director …

title: 嘉靖二十五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
尹子文相楚者也奮紓難之忠溥撫下之
惠不喜不怒以逃於祿而伐隨伐鄭滅弦
滅黃多其力焉其楚之忠臣與衛颯之守
桂陽病俗未知禮下車而首興庠序吏孜
其政則居官如家蓋豈弟君子也欒巴之
守桂陽以南陲不閑訓典定婚姻使知禮
禁止其視事明察有烹鮮之風焉周瑜破
曹瞞於烏林何其偉也兆三分之業其赤
壁之戰乎岳飛褫京超於富水何其雄也
===
復中原之志其六郡之屯乎劉弘位居方
牧豺狼斂跡然其舉賢登善一州清宴故
有振吳起之譽羊祜身受戎閫江漢歸心
然其輕裘緩帶開布大信故有樂毅孔明
之推服狄仁傑出判復州而惠愛大行狄
使君活汝夫豈聲音之所能為邪賈誼傅
相長沙而忠貞不變烈士殉名非賦鵩之
所以自廣乎劉昆江陵一拜而反風滅火
至誠之所感也長者之言受知於光武此

translation_en:
…Chief Minister Ziwen served as minister to Chu. He displayed the loyalty that relieved crises and extended benevolence in caring for those below him. Neither delighted by appointment nor angered by dismissal, he shunned official emoluments. The campaigns against Sui and Zheng and the destruction of Xian and Huang owed much to his efforts. Was he not a loyal minister of Chu!

When Wei Sa governed Guiyang, he was troubled that local customs showed no knowledge of ritual propriety. Upon taking office, his first act was to establish schools. Diligent in his administration [?], he treated his office as his own home: surely he was an amiable and easygoing gentleman. When Luan Ba governed Guiyang, because the southern borderlands were unfamiliar with canonical teachings, he regulated marriage and taught the people ritual propriety and prohibitions [?]. He handled affairs with clear discernment, governing with the light touch used in cooking a small fish.

How magnificent was Zhou Yu’s defeat of Cao Man at Wulin! Was it not the battle of Chibi that laid the foundation for the realm’s division into three? How heroic was Yue Fei’s overthrow of Jing Chao at Fushui! Was not his stationing of troops in the six commanderies an expression of his determination to recover the Central Plain?

Liu Hong held office as a regional governor, and wolves and jackals hid their tracks. Yet it was because he promoted the worthy and advanced the good, bringing peace to an entire province, that he earned praise for reviving the achievements of Wu Qi. Yang Hu was entrusted with military command, and the people of the Jiang and Han region gave him their allegiance. Yet it was because he wore light furs and a loosely fastened sash, openly demonstrating his great good faith, that he won admiration comparable to that accorded Yue Yi and Kongming.

Di Renjie went out to serve as assistant prefect of Fuzhou, and his benevolent care spread widely. “Prefect Di has saved your lives!” Could mere words have accomplished this? Jia Yi served as Grand Mentor to the prince of Changsha, remaining unwavering in loyalty and integrity. “Men of high resolve sacrifice themselves for their reputation”: was this not how his Rhapsody on the Owl sought to console him?
